descripcion: Índice de las guías CaVeSal® (Historia Clínica y Emergencias) para uso de IA. Texto plano por ficha, con fuentes y enlaces. Se regenera solo desde las guías publicadas; no editar a mano.

fichas.texto: Pregnancy lasts, on average, 280 days (40 weeks) from the first day of the LMP — 9 calendar months or 10 lunar months. Always expressed in completed weeks. Rules to estimate EDD: Wahl (LMP+10 days, -3 months) · Naegele (LMP+7 days, -3 months). Ultrasound correction: if it differs beyond the accepted margin, GA by ultrasound takes priority — the earlier the scan, the more reliable (maximum precision in the 1st trimester).
fichas.fuentes: CLAP-PAHO/WHO

fichas.texto: Systematic evaluation by parameter (normal/mild/moderate/severe) to detect clinical deterioration in time: Parameter Normal Mild Moderate Severe RR (rpm) 12–20 21–24 25–30 >30 SpO₂ (%) ≥95 90–94 85–89 <85 HR (bpm) 60–100 101–120 121–140 >140 Systolic BP 110–139 140–159 160–179 ≥180 Diastolic BP 60–89 90–99 100–109 ≥110 Temperature 36.0–37.5 37.6–38.0 38.1–39.0 >39.0 Consciousness Alert Anxious Confused Unconscious Proteinuria Negative +/++ +++ ++++ Contractions/30min <5 5–8 >8 — Vaginal bleeding Absent Mild Moderate Severe Fetal movements Present Decreased Absent —
fichas.fuentes: WHO

fichas.texto: Low risk: no identifiable factors, standard follow-up. Moderate: maternal age 35-39, overweight/obesity, adverse history, mild anemia, treated STI. High risk: <15 or >35-40 years, multiple gestation, prior fetal death, prior preeclampsia, chronic hypertension, diabetes, heart disease, chronic renal/pulmonary disease, autoimmune disease, moderate/severe anemia, STI/HIV/hepatitis, active TB, uterine malformation, placenta previa, abruption, FGR, oligo/polyhydramnios, sexual violence, substance use. Reassess at every visit.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay 2022 / WHO

fichas.texto: Tdap: international 27-36 wk, national (EPI) 16-20 wk. COVID-19: international any trimester, national from 20 wk. Maternal RSV: 28-36 wk (not part of the national schedule). Flu: any trimester. Contraindicated (live attenuated): MMR, varicella, yellow fever (except high risk), zoster, BCG, oral rotavirus.
fichas.fuentes: CDC / ACOG / NICE / MSPyBS (EPI)

fichas.texto: Folic acid: 400-800µg/day standard, 4-5mg/day high risk Iron: 30-60mg/day prophylaxis, 60-120mg/day anemia treatment Calcium: 1200mg/day (vs. 800 outside pregnancy) Vitamin D: 1000-2000 IU/day insufficiency, 2000-4000 deficiency Omega-3 (DHA): 200-300mg/day from 2nd trimester Iodine: 150-250µg/day from preconception
fichas.fuentes: WHO / ACOG / ATA / Cochrane

fichas.texto: 1st trimester: CBC, blood group/Rh/indirect Coombs, VDRL/RPR+confirmatory, HIV, HBsAg, glucose, urea/creatinine/uric acid, liver panel, TSH per risk, urinalysis/urine culture. 2nd trimester (24-28 wk): CBC, 75g OGTT, HbA1c if at risk, repeat VDRL/HIV, toxoplasmosis, urinalysis. 3rd trimester (35-37 wk): CBC, coagulation panel, glucose, renal/liver function, GBS swab.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay 2022 / WHO / ACOG

fichas.texto: 1st trimester (5-14 wk): early scan + dedicated 11-14 wk scan (NT, nasal bone, ductus venosus, uterine artery Doppler). 2nd trimester (18-24 wk): complete morphology scan, placenta, amniotic fluid, cervical length per risk. 3rd trimester (32 wk+): growth, amniotic fluid, presentation, Doppler/biophysical profile as indicated.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay 2022 / FMF / ISUOG / NICE

fichas.titulo: Physical exam by stage of pregnancy
fichas.texto: Vital signs: every visit Fundal height: from month 4 FHR: Doppler from month 4, Pinard from month 6 Leopold maneuvers: from month 6-7 Genital exam: 1st visit and at month 8
fichas.fuentes: CLAP-PAHO/WHO

fichas.texto: Detection of heartbeat: real-time ultrasound 6-8 wk, Doppler from 12 wk, stethoscope from 20 wk. Fetal movements: perceived from 18-20 wk (nulliparous). Self-monitoring: 4 movements in the 1st hour = normal, or up to 10 in 12h · or 30min post each meal, totaling 10+. If 10 movements are not reached in 12h, or fluid loss/contractions occur: seek care.
fichas.fuentes: CLAP-PAHO/WHO

fichas.texto: Warning signs: bleeding, foul-smelling discharge, decreased movements, severe abdominal pain, contractions before term, fever, severe headache/blurred vision, sudden edema, difficulty breathing, fluid loss. Restrictions: tobacco, alcohol, drugs, unnecessary radiation, medication without indication.
fichas.fuentes: WHO / National guidelines

fichas.texto: The theoretical risk of a method is always lower than that of an unwanted pregnancy. Right to choose freely, without coercion. Options: condom, ring, injectable, pills, copper/hormonal IUD, implant, sterilization, patch. Estrogen-containing methods are contraindicated in the first 6 months of breastfeeding.
fichas.fuentes: WHO — Medical Eligibility Criteria

fichas.texto: Safe and recommended: ≥150 min/week moderate aerobic activity (walking, swimming, stationary bike, prenatal yoga/pilates). Avoid: contact sports/fall-risk activities. Contraindications: TPL, placenta previa after week 26, PROM, FGR, severe heart disease, severe anemia.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG / WHO

fichas.texto: WHO: minimum 8 contacts (before 12, then 20/26/30/34/36/38/40 wk). National (MSPyBS): minimum 4 (before 12, 22-26, 27-32, 36-38 wk). Low risk: monthly up to 28 wk, every 2-3 wk up to 35-36, weekly in the last month.
fichas.fuentes: WHO 2016 / FIGO / MSPyBS Paraguay 2022

fichas.texto: Total energy cost ~80,000 kcal, ~300 kcal/day extra. Gain by BMI: underweight 12.5-18.0kg · normal 11.5-16.0kg · overweight 7.5-11.5kg · obesity 6.0kg. Distribution: 500g/month (T1) · 1000g/month (T2) · 1500g/month (T3). Macros: 55% carbs, 15% protein, 30% fat.
fichas.fuentes: IOM 2009 / WHO

fichas.titulo: Mean Arterial Pressure (MAP) as a predictor
fichas.texto: MAP = (SBP + 2×DBP) / 3 MAP ≥105: warning for gestational hypertension/preeclampsia, assess proteinuria/hepatorenal function MAP >90 in 1st trimester (≤14 wk): higher risk, consider prophylactic aspirin MAP >90 outside 1st trimester: routine surveillance
fichas.fuentes: WHO / NICE / ISUOG / FMF / ACOG / Cochrane

fichas.titulo: Fetal growth: SGA / FGR / AGA / LGA
fichas.texto: By percentile (EFW): severe SGA/FGR <P3 · FGR P3-P10+abnormal Doppler · SGA P3-P10+normal Doppler · AGA P10-P90 · borderline LGA P90-P97 · significant LGA ≥P97. By birth weight (WHO): extremely low <1000g · very low 1000-1499g · low <2500g · normal 2500-3999g · macrosomia ≥4000g · severe ≥4500g.
fichas.fuentes: Figueras F. EJOGR 2008 · Barcelona Fetal Medicine 2024 · ISUOG Delphi 2020 · WHO

fichas.titulo: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy — Classification and severity criteria
fichas.texto: Classification: Chronic: BP ≥140/90 before pregnancy or diagnosed before week 20 Gestational: BP ≥140/90 after wk 20, without proteinuria or organ dysfunction Preeclampsia: BP ≥140/90 after wk 20 + proteinuria (≥0.3g/24h) or ≥1 severity criterion, even without proteinuria Chronic with superimposed preeclampsia: worsening + new proteinuria/organ dysfunction Eclampsia: tonic-clonic seizures in preeclampsia, with no other neurological cause Severity criteria (≥1 confirms severe preeclampsia): BP ≥160/110 on 2 readings 15min apart, thrombocytopenia <100,000, doubled transaminases, creatinine >1.1 or doubled, pulmonary edema, new neuro-visual symptoms.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 (2020) · FIGO Guidelines on Preeclampsia Prevention and Management (2019) · ISSHP Classification (2021)

fichas.titulo: Hypertensive disorders — Aspirin prophylaxis and antihypertensive management
fichas.texto: Prophylaxis (high risk): ASA 100-150mg/day PO at night, from wk 12-16 to wk 36. Elemental calcium 1.5-2.0g/day if low intake. Chronic treatment (BP >140/90): Labetalol 100-400mg PO q8-12h (max 2,400mg/day) · Alpha-methyldopa 250-500mg PO q6-8h · Extended-release nifedipine 20-60mg PO q12-24h. ⚠️ Contraindicated: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, renin inhibitors. Hypertensive crisis (≥160/110): IV labetalol bolus 20mg → 40mg → 80mg q10min (max 300mg) · IV hydralazine bolus 5-10mg q20min (max 20mg) · Oral nifedipine 10-20mg (not sublingual).
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 (2020) · FIGO Guidelines on Preeclampsia (2019) · ISSHP 2021

fichas.titulo: Magnesium sulfate — Seizure prevention and management
fichas.texto: Indication: preeclampsia with severity criteria, and eclampsia. Dose: 4-6g IV loading dose in 100mL 0.9% NS over 15-20 min → continuous maintenance 1-2g/hour IV for 24h postpartum or post-last seizure. Monitoring: patellar reflex present, RR >12-14/min, urine output >30mL/h. ⚠️ Signs of toxicity: RR<12rpm, absent patellar reflex, oliguria <30mL/h, AV block. ⚠️ Antidote — 10% Calcium Gluconate, two current standards (equivalent in available elemental calcium, not contradictory): National standard (MSPyBS Paraguay, Code Red 2nd ed. 2021): 10% Calcium Gluconate — 1g (10mL) IV slow push over 3 min. Advanced international resuscitation standard (AHA · Universidad de Antioquia · PAHO): 10% Calcium Gluconate — 3g (30mL) IV, or alternatively 10% Calcium Chloride — 1g (10mL) IV. This is not a dosing error: 1g of calcium gluconate provides ~93mg of elemental calcium, while 1g of calcium chloride provides ~272mg — which is why the international advanced-resuscitation regimen uses a larger volume of gluconate (3g/30mL) to match the elemental calcium delivered by 1g of chloride. Which to use? The national standard for an isolated toxicity sign (RR<12, areflexia, oliguria); the international regimen for frank cardiorespiratory arrest from hypermagnesemia.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 (2020) · FIGO 2019 · ISSHP 2021 · MSPyBS Paraguay — National Maternal and Neonatal Code Red Guideline (2nd ed., 2021) · AHA / Universidad de Antioquia / PAHO

fichas.titulo: Maternal CPR and perimortem cesarean delivery
fichas.texto: CPR specifics in pregnancy: continuous manual left uterine displacement (or 15-30° left lateral tilt) from the start, to relieve aortocaval compression; chest compressions slightly higher on the sternum; defibrillation at the same energies as outside pregnancy (not contraindicated). Fundal height threshold (fundus at or above the umbilicus, ≈20 weeks): from this point on, the gravid uterus causes enough aortocaval compression to invalidate the effectiveness of chest compressions — this is the action threshold, defined by maternal benefit, not fetal viability. ≥22-24 weeks is a separate, later threshold: fetal viability — a secondary consideration about the expected neonatal outcome, not about whether to perform the hysterotomy. 4-5 minute rule: if there is no return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) by 4 minutes of high-quality CPR, begin the cesarean/perimortem hysterotomy incision in situ (do not transfer to the operating room) to achieve delivery by minute 5. The primary goal is maternal: evacuating the uterus improves venous return and compression effectiveness.
fichas.fuentes: AHA — Circulation 2020;142(suppl 2):S366-S368 · ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 212, Obstet Gynecol 2019;134(4):e132-e140 · Queenan JT, et al. — Management of High-Risk Pregnancy

fichas.texto: Lipid elevation is physiological in pregnancy — no routine screening. Targeted in: family history of early CVD, pre-pregnancy obesity, prior diabetes/preeclampsia, severe hypertriglyceridemia. Treatment: 1st line diet/exercise. Statins: FDA (2021) withdrew the absolute contraindication, individualized use in very high risk. Bile acid sequestrants (the only ones approved in pregnancy): Cholestyramine, Colestipol, Colesevelam. Omega-3: reduces preterm birth risk (Cochrane 2018).
fichas.fuentes: AHA/ACC frameworks · National Lipid Association (2024) · ACOG

fichas.texto: Diagnosis: nocturnal palmoplantar pruritus, without primary skin lesion. Labs: bilirubin, AST/ALT, ALP, GGT. Pathway 1 (with total bile acids): Normal <10 μmol/L · Anicteric 10-39 → delivery at wk 38 · Icteric 40-99 (+bili >1.2) → wk 36 · Severe ≥100 → wk 34-36. Pathway 2 (regional Paraguay criterion, without total bile acids): Anicteric (AST/ALT >40, normal bili) → wk 38 · Icteric (+bili >1.2) → wk 36. Treatment: Ursodeoxycholic acid 10-15mg/kg/day PO + Vitamin K if prolonged. ⚠️ Deliver at any sign of fetal compromise, regardless of pathway or GA.
fichas.fuentes: MINSAL Chile Perinatal Guideline 2015 · RCOG Green-top No. 43 (2022) · SFMFM · ACOG · EASL · Williamson et al. Lancet 2018 · Ovadia et al. Lancet 2019

fichas.titulo: Threatened preterm labor (TPL) — Diagnosis and tocolysis
fichas.texto: Diagnosis: regular uterine dynamics (≥4/20min) + cervical changes, 22-36+6 wk. TVUS: CL >30mm rules out TPL · CL <25mm high risk · 20-30mm → biomarkers (fetal fibronectin/PAMG-1). Tocolysis (22/24-33+6 wk): Nifedipine (1st line) loading dose 10-20mg q20min → maintenance q6-8h · Atosiban (NICE/RCOG) · Indomethacin (before wk 32, do not combine with MgSO4 or nifedipine).
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 171 (2016, reaffirmed 2020) · NICE NG25 (2019, updated 2022) · FIGO Recommendations on Preterm Birth (2021)

fichas.texto: Cutoffs by guideline: ACOG wk 24-33+6 (late 34-36+6) · FIGO/WHO 24-34+6 · NICE offer 24-33+6, consider 34-35+6. Regimens: Betamethasone 12mg IM q24h (2 doses) · Dexamethasone 6mg IM q12h (4 doses). Rescue course: if >14 days have passed, GA <34 wk, imminent risk within 7 days.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 171 · FIGO/WHO · NICE NG25

fichas.texto: Cutoffs by guideline: ACOG before wk 32 · NICE before wk 30 (consider 30-33+6) · FIGO/WHO before wk 32 (some extend to <34 if imminent). Regimen: 4g IV loading dose over 20-30 min → maintenance 1g/hour until delivery or 24h. ⚠️ Antidote (see full detail in "Magnesium sulfate — Seizure prevention and management"): national standard 10% Calcium Gluconate 1g (10mL) IV slow push over 3 min · advanced international resuscitation standard 3g (30mL), or 10% Calcium Chloride 1g (10mL) — same concentration, larger gluconate volume to match the elemental calcium delivered by the chloride.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 171 · NICE NG25 · FIGO/WHO · MSPyBS Paraguay — Code Red 2nd ed. 2021 · AHA / Universidad de Antioquia / PAHO

fichas.texto: Clinical: clear fluid leakage (>90% reliability if visualized through the cervical os). Tests: Fern test, Nitrazine (pH>6.5), PAMG-1/IGFBP-1, vaginal urea/creatinine (>90-95% sensitivity). Amniocentesis (doubtful cases): Indigo Carmine + tampon, check staining at 20-30min. ⚠️ Methylene Blue contraindicated.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 217 (2020) · FIGO Guidelines on PROM Management (2021) · Cowles et al. (1993)

fichas.texto: Previable (<22-24 wk): expectant, counseling. No routine antibiotics/corticosteroids. Far from term preterm (24-33+6): expectant, inpatient, complete lung maturation course, neuroprotective MgSO4 if <32 wk, mandatory latency antibiotics, tocolysis restricted to 48h. Late preterm (34-36+6): delivery/induction at diagnosis. Exception: expectant until wk 37 if no infection. Term (≥37): induction within 12-24h.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 217 · FIGO PROM (2021)

fichas.titulo: PROM — Latency antibiotic regimens and criteria for delivery
fichas.texto: Standard (7 days, 24-34 wk): Days 1-2 IV: Ampicillin 2g q6h + Erythromycin 250mg q6h. Days 3-7 oral: Amoxicillin 500mg q8h + Erythromycin 333mg q8h. Alternative: Ampicillin 2g IV q6h x48h → Amoxicillin 500mg PO q8h x5d + Azithromycin 1g PO single dose. ⚠️ Avoid Amoxicillin+Clavulanate (neonatal NEC). Immediate delivery: chorioamnionitis, abruption, fetal distress, established labor, stillbirth.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG/NICHD

fichas.titulo: Hyperemesis gravidarum — Diagnosis and PUQE score
fichas.texto: NVP: physiological, up to 80%, wk 4-9 to 16-20. HG: severe, 0.3-2%. Triad: intractable vomiting + >5% weight loss + ketonuria/electrolyte disturbance. PUQE score (24h, 3 questions, 1-5pts): ≤6 mild · 7-12 moderate · ≥13 severe HG (inpatient).
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 189 (2018, reaffirmed 2021) · Koren et al. (2002/2005) · RCOG Green-top No. 69 (2016)

fichas.titulo: Hyperemesis gravidarum — Stepwise treatment and rehydration
fichas.texto: 1st line: Pyridoxine B6 10-25mg q6-8h · Doxylamine+Pyridoxine 2 tabs/night. 2nd line: Dimenhydrinate, Metoclopramide (<5 days), Promethazine. 3rd line: Ondansetron (from wk 10) · Methylprednisolone (last resort, >10 wk). ⚠️ Golden rule: Thiamine B1 100mg IV before/with the first dextrose infusion — prevents Wernicke's encephalopathy.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 189 · RCOG Green-top No. 69

fichas.titulo: Amniotic fluid disorders — Methods and diagnostic criteria
fichas.texto: Methods: SDP/DVP (preferred) · AFI (4 quadrants). Classic: Oligohydramnios AFI<5/SDP<2 · Normal 5.1-24.9/2.1-7.9 · Polyhydramnios AFI≥25/SDP≥8. ACOG/SMFM ranges: Anhydramnios=0 · Severe <1/<3 · Lower borderline 5.1-8.0 (follow-up) · Physiological normal 8.1-18.0 · Upper borderline 18.1-24.9.
fichas.fuentes: ISUOG Practice Guidelines (2024) · SMFM Consult Series #46 (2018) · ACOG Clinical Consensus No. 3 (2022)

fichas.texto: Mild: AFI 25.0-29.9 (80% of cases) Moderate: 30.0-34.9 Severe: ≥35 (>50% association with malformations)
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Clinical Consensus No. 3 (2022)

fichas.texto: Oligohydramnios: maternal (placental insufficiency, hypertension, APS, dehydration, drugs) · fetal (urinary anomalies, FGR, post-term) · membrane-related (PROM, TTTS donor). Polyhydramnios: maternal (diabetes) · fetal (GI, CNS, neuromuscular, cardiac, chromosomal) · membrane-related (TTTS recipient) · idiopathic 50-60%.
fichas.fuentes: ISUOG 2024 · SMFM #46 · ACOG Consensus No. 3

fichas.titulo: Fetal structural morphology — 7 systems (20-24 week scan)
fichas.texto: Structured system-by-system checklist, 18-24 weeks, immediately after the 2nd-trimester FMF screening. CNS: cavum septum pellucidum (absent ⚠️), symmetric thalami, cranial shape ("lemon"/"strawberry" sign ⚠️), lateral ventricular atrium (normal <10mm · mild 10-15mm · severe >15mm, measured at the level of the choroid plexus glomus), cisterna magna (normal 3.0-10.0mm; <2-3mm obliterated, >10mm mega cisterna magna), 2T nuchal fold (valid 15.0-20.6 wk, normal <6.0mm), banana sign, and cerebellar vermis agenesis. An obliterated cisterna magna plus a banana sign point toward open spina bifida — correlate with the spine. Face: orbits, nose, maxilla, palate (retronasal coronal view), and upper lip. Orbital diameters: IOD/OOD ratio >0.40 hypertelorism, <0.25 hypotelorism (rule of thirds). Spine: bony continuity on longitudinal + axial views, and intact overlying skin. Chest and heart (+ CDH): situs, 4-chamber view, ventricular/atrial symmetry, interventricular septum (VSD), outflow tracts, 3-vessel and trachea view, aortic arch. Cardiothoracic area ratio: normal 0.25-0.33, cardiomegaly >0.35. Congenital diaphragmatic hernia: intrathoracic gastric bubble, side (left Bochdalek ~85%), O/E LHR <25% severe · 25-44.9% moderate · ≥45% favorable. Abdomen: stomach (rule out "double bubble" — duodenal atresia, ~30% association with T21), abdominal wall/cord (omphalocele vs. gastroschisis), renal pelvic dilation (<33 wk obstructive >10.0mm; ≥33 wk obstructive >10.0mm with a distinct normal cutoff of <7.0mm), kidneys (uni/bilateral agenesis, multicystic dysplasia), single umbilical artery, 2T/3T megacystis (≥16 wk, pathological if longitudinal diameter > [GA in weeks + 12]mm), and "keyhole sign" (PUV). Limbs: 3 segments per limb (humerus/radius-ulna/hand; femur/tibia-fibula/foot) to avoid missing reduction defects, polydactyly (soft marker for T13/Meckel-Gruber/Bardet-Biedl if isolated), and clubfoot. Placenta, cord, amniotic fluid, cervix: placental location (low-lying <20mm from the internal os) and cord insertion site (marginal "racquet" vs. velamentous — vasa previa risk, confirm with color Doppler).
fichas.fuentes: ISUOG Practice Guidelines (2020/2023) — CNS, face, heart · Paladini & Volpe (2018) · Jeanty P et al. 1984 · Mayden KL et al. 1982 · Corteville JE et al. 1991/1992 · FMF/Nicolaides · CDHSG / Jani et al. 2007

fichas.texto: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS: accreta/increta/percreta). Main risk factor: prior cesarean plus anterior placenta previa/low-lying placenta. ⚠️ Golden rule: whenever signs of accreta are present, never attempt manual placental removal — leave the placenta in situ and proceed to en bloc hysterectomy, at a Level III-IV center, with a planned cesarean at 34+0-35+6 weeks. Risk factors: number of prior cesareans, prior uterine curettage, prior uterine surgery (myomectomy), history of Asherman syndrome — in addition to placenta previa/low-lying placenta and maternal age >35 or IVF, already recorded under Morphology and History. 2D ultrasound signs: loss of the clear zone, myometrial thinning (<1mm), irregular placental lacunae ("Swiss cheese" appearance), interruption of the bladder-uterine interface, placental bulging toward the bladder, focal exophytic mass. Color Doppler signs: uterovesical and subplacental hypervascularity, bridging vessels, lacunar feeder vessels, parametrial involvement. FIGO Classification (surgical/histopathological confirmation): Grade 1 (Accreta) · Grade 2 (Increta) · Grade 3a (Percreta limited to the uterine serosa) · Grade 3b (Percreta with urinary bladder invasion) · Grade 3c (Percreta with invasion of other pelvic tissues/organs: broad ligament, vaginal wall, pelvic sidewall or any other pelvic organ, with or without bladder invasion). Jauniaux E, et al. FIGO, Int J Gynecol Obstet 2019;146:20-24. ⚠️ Probability and Extent are calculated using the "CaVeSal Classification" — a proprietary scoring scheme developed by the team (not a published FIGO/ISUOG/ACOG score) that combines risk factors + 2D signs + Doppler signs. The FIGO Classification is a separate data point, based on surgical/histopathological confirmation — it does not replace, and should not be confused with, the CaVeSal Classification.
fichas.fuentes: FIGO/Jauniaux 2018 · ISUOG/Jauniaux 2016-2018 · ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No.7 (2018/2021) · MSPyBS Paraguay

fichas.texto: Modalities: Complete (Manning, 5 variables, 10 points + NST) · Ultrasound-only (8 points, no NST) · Abbreviated (Clark: NST + amniotic fluid) · Vintzileos (graded 0/1/2 plus Grannum placental grade, up to 12 points). Variables: fetal breathing movements, body/limb movements, fetal tone, NST reactivity, amniotic fluid volume (plus placental grade in Vintzileos). Management depends on the combination of score × amniotic fluid status × GA, not on the total score alone: 10/10 or 8/10 with normal fluid: expectant management. 8/10 with oligohydramnios: deliver at ≥36-37 wk; if preterm, daily Doppler. 6/10 with normal fluid: reassess in 12-24h (or 2h per MSPyBS), or deliver if at term. 6/10 with oligohydramnios: deliver if viability is assured. 4/10 with normal fluid: if <32 wk, repeat in 2h plus corticosteroids plus MgSO4 plus ductus venosus Doppler; cesarean only if it persists or the Doppler decompensates. 4/10 with decreased fluid: immediate emergency cesarean, regardless of GA. ≤2/10 (any fluid status): immediate emergency cesarean, regardless of GA or fluid. All markers are acute, except placenta and amniotic fluid, which are chronic markers — key to interpreting a low score in the correct context. If the score indicates delivery and GA is preterm, add lung maturation with corticosteroids.
fichas.fuentes: Manning 1980 · Vintzileos 1983 · Clark 1989 · Queenan/Spong/Lockwood 7th ed. · MSPyBS Paraguay

fichas.texto: Baseline FHR: tachycardia >160 bpm · bradycardia <110 bpm (same criterion as the heart rate assessed on the 2T morphology scan — Chest and heart). Variability: absent, minimal, moderate, or saltatory. Reactivity: 15×15 rule (≥32 weeks) or 10×10 (<32 weeks). Decelerations: Dips I/II/III (Caldeyro-Barcia). Shoulders vs. overshoot — NOT synonyms: shoulders are a reassuring finding (brief acceleration before/after a deceleration, intact autonomic baroreflex); overshoot is a non-reassuring finding (exaggerated/rigid acceleration after a deceleration, associated with evolving hypoxia/acidosis). ⚠️ Special morphological patterns — lambda waves, omega pattern: these are informal visual analogies, frequently used for teaching/clinical purposes, that describe the shape of the tracing, but are not official nomenclature of FIGO, ACOG, or NICHD. The W sign (Welt 1984) is different: it does correspond to a published pattern with its own verified source (biphasic variable deceleration).
fichas.fuentes: FIGO Consensus Guidelines (Ayres-de-Campos et al. 2015) · ACOG Practice Bulletin 229/106 · Caldeyro-Barcia R. et al. 1966 · Welt AM et al. 1984 · Dawes GS, Redman CWG et al. (Oxford)

fichas.titulo: FGR and fetal Doppler — Definitions and diagnostic criteria
fichas.texto: Constitutional SGA: EFW/AC P3-P10, strictly normal Doppler, low risk. Early FGR (<32 wk): isolated EFW/AC<P3 or UA with absent/reversed flow · or combined (≥2 of: EFW/AC<P10, UA-PI>P95, UtA-PI>P95). Late FGR (≥32 wk, 70-80% of cases): isolated EFW/AC<P3 · or combined (≥2 of: EFW/AC<P10, drop >2 quartiles, CPR<P5, MCA-PI<P5, UtA-PI>P95).
fichas.fuentes: Gordijn SJ, et al. Consensus Delphi (2016) · ISUOG Practice Guidelines (2020) · SMFM Consult Series #52 (2020)

fichas.texto: Stage I (mild): EFW<P3, or CPR<P5, or UtA-PI>P95, or UA-PI>P95 with present diastolic flow. Doppler every 7 days. Delivery at wk 37. Stage II (severe): persistent absent end-diastolic flow in UA (AEDF) >50% of cycles. Inpatient monitoring, Doppler every 48-72h. Elective cesarean at wk 34 (after lung maturation course).
fichas.fuentes: Figueras F, Gratacós E. Fetal Diagn Ther/Barcelona Fetal Medicine (2014/2021)

fichas.texto: Stage III: persistent reversed flow in UA, or DV-PI>P95. Strict hospitalization, Doppler every 24-48h. Cesarean at wk 30 (lung maturation + MgSO4 neuroprotection). Stage IV: reversed/absent A-wave in DV, umbilical vein pulsations, or STV<3ms. Continuous emergency. Immediate cesarean from wk 26 (or limit of viability). Summary of cutoffs: wk 37-38 (SGA/Stage I) · wk 34 (Stage II) · wk 30-32 (Stage III) · wk 26-28 immediate (Stage IV).
fichas.fuentes: Figueras F, Gratacós E. (2014/2021)

fichas.titulo: HIV in pregnancy — Diagnosis and treatment
fichas.texto: Confirmed HIV: immediate ART regardless of GA/CD4/viral load. Regimen: TDF+FTC/3TC+Dolutegravir. Mode of delivery: vaginal if viral load undetectable · elective cesarean if VL>1000 at wk 36. Neonatal prophylaxis: zidovudine 4mg/kg q12h x4 weeks.
fichas.fuentes: ETMI Plus Paraguay 2024 · DHHS Guidelines 2024 · PAHO

fichas.titulo: Syphilis in pregnancy — Diagnosis and treatment
fichas.texto: Treatment: Benzathine penicillin G IM (the only option valid in pregnancy). Primary/secondary/early latent: 2.4M IU single dose. Late latent: 2.4M IU weekly x3 weeks. Allergy: desensitization mandatory. Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction: 24h fetal monitoring.
fichas.fuentes: CDC STI 2021 · PAHO Vertical Transmission Elimination 2024 · ETMI Plus 2024

fichas.texto: HBsAg+: neonatal immunoprophylaxis within 12h (vaccine+HBIG). If HBV-DNA>200,000 IU/mL or HBeAg+: Tenofovir 300mg/day from wk 28.
fichas.fuentes: EASL 2017 · ACOG · ETMI Plus 2024

fichas.texto: Confirm Anti-HCV+ with HCV-RNA. Vertical transmission ~5-7% (up to 11% with HIV). No neonatal prophylaxis or antiviral treatment during pregnancy (contraindicated).
fichas.fuentes: EASL 2020 · AASLD · ETMI Plus 2024

fichas.texto: Confirmed (2 reactive techniques): vertical transmission ~5-10%. Benznidazole/nifurtimox contraindicated in pregnancy. Newborn: cord blood PCR + at 30 days; if positive, Benznidazole 5-7mg/kg/day x60d.
fichas.fuentes: PAHO 2023 · ETMI Plus 2024 · Torrico F, Lancet (2018)

fichas.titulo: Toxoplasmosis in pregnancy — Diagnosis and treatment
fichas.texto: High avidity: indicates infection >16 wk before the test, not before conception — calculate GA at testing − 16wk to determine if it could have been in the 1st trimester. 3 levels of prevention: 1️⃣ primary (hygiene) · 2️⃣ secondary (infected mother: Spiramycin 1g q8h, does not cross the placenta) · 3️⃣ tertiary (fetal infection confirmed by amniotic fluid PCR: switch to Pyrimethamine+Sulfadiazine+Folinic acid, which does cross the placenta). ⚠️ Pyrimethamine-Sulfadiazine contraindicated in T1 (teratogenic) and the last month (kernicterus). Duration: no single consensus — most continue until delivery; variants use alternating 3-week cycles, or others stop 2 weeks before delivery.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay National Guidelines · SLIPE · Spanish Society of Pediatric Infectious Diseases

fichas.texto: IgG(-): MMR vaccine contraindicated in pregnancy, vaccinate postpartum. IgM(+): Congenital Rubella Syndrome, risk>85% in T1 (cataracts, heart disease, deafness). No specific treatment. Mandatory reporting.
fichas.fuentes: CDC · PAHO · ACOG

fichas.texto: IgM(+) low avidity: vertical transmission 30-40%. Amniocentesis PCR if GA>21wk. Consider maternal Valacyclovir 8g/day. Newborn: urine/saliva PCR at 3 weeks.
fichas.fuentes: Rawlinson WD et al. J Clin Virol (2017) · Leruez-Ville M et al. AJOG (2020)

fichas.texto: Rh(-): indirect Coombs at T1 and at wk 28. Negative: anti-D prophylaxis at wk 28 and postpartum. Positive (sensitized): active surveillance for fetal anemia, no prophylaxis.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG · SMFM

fichas.texto: MCA-PSV in MoM: <1.29 normal · 1.29-1.49 mild anemia (surveillance) · ≥1.50 moderate-severe (cordocentesis+urgent transfusion).
fichas.fuentes: Mari G et al. NEJM (2000)

fichas.titulo: Rh isoimmunization — Alternative method with amniocentesis (Liley)
fichas.texto: ΔOD450 spectrophotometry, valid from wk 27. Zone 1 mild · Zone 2 moderate · Zone 3 severe (transfusion/delivery). Before wk 27: Queenan chart or MCA Doppler.
fichas.fuentes: Liley AW (1961)

fichas.titulo: Rh isoimmunization — Algorithm by GA and intrauterine transfusion
fichas.texto: MoM≥1.50 before wk 35: cordocentesis+intrauterine transfusion (repeat every 2-4 wk). After wk 35: consider delivery instead of transfusion. Procedure-related fetal loss risk ~1-3%.
fichas.fuentes: SMFM · ACOG

fichas.titulo: Hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism — Values by trimester
fichas.texto: TSH: T1 0.1-2.5 · T2 0.2-3.0 · T3 0.3-3.5 µIU/mL. Hypothyroidism (clinical or subclinical): levothyroxine, target TSH per trimester. Hyperthyroidism: PTU in T1, Methimazole T2-T3. Never radioactive iodine.
fichas.fuentes: ATA Guidelines 2017 · ACOG

fichas.texto: Anti-TPO+ (>34IU/mL) + elevated TSH: Hashimoto's, start levothyroxine. Anti-TPO+ with normal TSH: recheck every 4-6wk (2-5x risk of gestational hypothyroidism). Some guidelines suggest adjusting already from preconception. Confirmed pregnancy on prior treatment: +25-30% starting dose.
fichas.fuentes: ATA 2017 · Endocrine Society

fichas.texto: Cervical length <25mm: vaginal progesterone 200mg/night, follow-up every 2wk. <15mm: urgent cerclage if <23+6wk. History of cervical insufficiency: prophylactic cerclage wk 12-14 + progesterone from the start.
fichas.fuentes: FMF/Nicolaides · ACOG

fichas.titulo: Progesterone in pregnancy — Uses, indications and evidence
fichas.texto: Preterm birth/short cervix: solid evidence (see cervical insufficiency guide). Threatened miscarriage: generally controversial (ACOG). Clearer benefit only with ≥1 prior miscarriage+bleeding (RR 1.08). Regimen: 400mg q12h until wk 16. Luteal support in IVF/ICSI: established standard, routine practice. 400mg q12h vaginal. Advanced maternal age alone: no solid independent evidence.
fichas.fuentes: FMF · ACOG · NICE · PRISM/PROMISE Trials · Cochrane 2021

fichas.texto: Risk x10 in pregnancy, x5 postpartum (peak 1st week), x4 with cesarean. ↑fibrinogen/FVII-VIII-X/vWF/PAI. ↓Protein S. Left lower limb predilection (May-Thurner + uterine compression).
fichas.fuentes: RCOG Green-top 37a (2015) · ACOG PB 196

fichas.titulo: VTE — Diagnostic algorithm for DVT and PE
fichas.texto: DVT: lower-limb venous Doppler ultrasound. PE: 3-item triage (signs of DVT, hemoptysis, PE most likely) → D-dimer and/or CT angiography per result.
fichas.fuentes: RCOG (2015) · ACOG PB 196

fichas.texto: Criteria: ≥1 thrombosis or ≥1 obstetric morbidity + confirmed labs on 2 occasions (12 wk apart). Treatment: ASA 100mg/night + prophylactic LMWH from FHR confirmation until 42 days postpartum.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 197 · ASH 2018

fichas.titulo: VTE — Postpartum risk assessment and thromboprophylaxis
fichas.texto: Point scale (1-4 per factor). Score 0: none · 1-4: pneumatic compression · 5-6: LMWH · ≥7: LMWH+compression.
fichas.fuentes: RCOG Green-top 37a (2015)

fichas.texto: Weight-adjusted prophylactic enoxaparin (20-80mg/day by kg). Therapeutic: 1mg/kg q12h, minimum 3-6 months + 6 wk postpartum. DOACs contraindicated. Avoid warfarin in T1 and peripartum.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 196 · RCOG

fichas.titulo: VTE — Peripartum management and neuraxial anesthesia
fichas.texto: Hold prophylactic LMWH 12h before puncture/surgery, therapeutic 24h before. Resume 12h post-vaginal / 24h post-cesarean.
fichas.fuentes: RCOG (2015) · ACOG PB 196

fichas.texto: Active bleeding, platelets<50,000, CrCl<15, PT<40%, persistent severe hypertension ≥4h.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 196

fichas.texto: Latch: mouth >130°, everted lip, chin touching breast, rounded cheeks. On-demand 8-12 feeds/day. Crack prevention: correct latch, avoid soaps, own milk after feeding.
fichas.fuentes: WHO/UNICEF · ACOG

fichas.texto: Clinical picture: localized pain/erythema/warmth + fever ± flu-like symptoms. S. aureus predominant. Do not stop breastfeeding — frequent emptying of the affected breast (hand/nursing/pump), continue nursing on that side. Antibiotic therapy (if systemic/persistent >12-24h despite emptying): Cephalexin 500mg PO q6h for 7-10 days (first line) Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875/125mg PO q12h (or 500/125mg q8h) for 7-10 days Penicillin allergy or suspected MRSA: Clindamycin 300-450mg PO q8h for 7-10 days
fichas.fuentes: WHO 2023 · Spencer JP, Am Fam Physician 2008;78(6):727-734 · Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine · ACOG

fichas.texto: T1 fasting: <92 normal · 92-125 GDM · ≥126 pregestational. Wk 24-28: 75g OGTT (92/180/153), 1 abnormal value confirms. Postpartum: reclassify with adult OGTT.
fichas.fuentes: IADPSG/WHO/ADA/ALAD

fichas.titulo: Gestational Diabetes — Targets, self-monitoring and nutrition
fichas.texto: Targets: fasting 70-95, 1h<140, 2h<120. Split diet into 6 meals. Insulin if ≥20% of readings out of target after 1-2 wk of diet/exercise.
fichas.fuentes: ADA/ALAD

fichas.titulo: Gestational Diabetes — Hypoglycemia management and correction regimens
fichas.texto: 15-15 rule for hypoglycemia. Scheduled basal-bolus regimen preferred over reactive sliding scale. Ultra-rapid analogs preferred over Regular insulin.
fichas.fuentes: ADA/ALAD

fichas.titulo: Gestational Diabetes — Basal-bolus dose and ISF calculation
fichas.texto: TDD: 0.7-1.0 IU/kg/day by trimester. 50% basal + 50% bolus. ISF = 1800/TDD (ultra-rapid). Titrate per persistent fasting/postprandial values.
fichas.fuentes: ADA/ALAD

fichas.titulo: Acute gastroenteritis (AGE) and pregnancy — Etiology, management and antibiotic therapy
fichas.texto: Viral etiology (70-80%): Norovirus and Rotavirus (community outbreaks), enteric Adenovirus, Astrovirus. Self-limiting (24-72h): profuse watery diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, low-grade fever. Bacterial: Campylobacter jejuni (most common bacterial cause), non-typhoidal Salmonella enterica / S. typhi (risk of bacteremia/transplacental spread), Shigella spp. (dysentery, tenesmus, mucus/blood), E. coli (ETEC/EPEC/STEC-EHEC O157:H7), Clostridioides difficile (post-antimicrobial). Listeria monocytogenes: flu-like illness with fever, myalgias and preceding watery diarrhea. ⚠️ Critical risk: maternal bacteremia with transplacental spread → chorioamnionitis, septic abortion, intrauterine fetal death or severe neonatal sepsis. Parasitic: Giardia lamblia, Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium parvum. General management: hydration and electrolyte rebalancing as the cornerstone. Mild-moderate: ORS in frequent sips. Severe/oral intolerance: admission + 0.9% NS or Lactated Ringer's 2,000-3,000mL/24h, adjusted by electrolyte panel (potassium monitoring). Safe symptomatic treatment: antiemetics (Doxylamine+Pyridoxine, Metoclopramide 10mg PO/IV q8h, Dimenhydrinate 50mg PO/IV q6-8h) · Acetaminophen 500-1000mg PO q6-8h (max 4g/day). Loperamide restricted use (avoid in inflammatory/dysenteric diarrhea with fever or suspected invasive pathogen, due to risk of toxic megacolon); Racecadotril has limited data in pregnancy. By trimester: 1st trimester: mandatory differential diagnosis with Hyperemesis Gravidarum (AGE presents with watery diarrhea and sudden onset, unlike HG). Avoid NSAIDs entirely. If antibiotics are required: beta-lactams (Amoxicillin, Ampicillin) or macrolides (Azithromycin), safe during organogenesis. 2nd trimester: dehydration and prostaglandins from the intestinal inflammatory process can irritate the myometrium and trigger uterine activity/threatened late miscarriage. Differential: acute appendicitis (the cecum and appendix rise with the gravid uterus). Monitor FHR and cervical length if regular contractions are present. 3rd trimester: severe bacterial diarrhea and hypovolemia are frequent triggers of preterm labor (PTL) and placental abruption. Electronic fetal monitoring/NST with maternal fever. In the peripartum period, if active bacterial AGE is present (Salmonella, Campylobacter, Listeria): maximize enteric isolation and precautions during delivery (vertical transmission). Antibiotic therapy — indications: dysenteric diarrhea (blood/mucus + fever ≥38.5°C), suspected/confirmed gestational Listeriosis, suspected invasive Shigella/Campylobacter/Salmonella, immunocompromised pregnant patients, severe dehydration or bacteremia/sepsis. Microorganism Preferred regimen Alternative Considerations Campylobacter jejuni Azithromycin 500mg PO q24h x3-5d Erythromycin 500mg PO q6h x5d Fluoroquinolones contraindicated in pregnancy Shigella spp. Azithromycin 500mg day 1, then 250mg/day (d2-5), or 500mg/day x3d Ceftriaxone 1-2g IV q24h x5d Reduces spread and duration of illness Invasive non-typhoidal Salmonella Ceftriaxone 1-2g IV/IM q24h x7-10d Azithromycin 500mg PO q24h x7d, or Amoxicillin 1g PO q8h Always treat to prevent bacteremia/chorioamnionitis Listeria monocytogenes Ampicillin 2g IV q4h (min. 14-21d) ± Gentamicin 5mg/kg/day IV TMP/SMX 5mg/kg (TMP) IV q8h (only for severe penicillin allergy; caution in 1st/3rd trim.) Start immediately for a compatible febrile presentation Clostridioides difficile Vancomycin 125mg PO q6h x10d Fidaxomicin 200mg PO q12h x10d (or Metronidazole 500mg PO q8h) Oral vancomycin has no systemic absorption — safe in all trimesters Severe empiric therapy (pending stool culture) Azithromycin 500mg PO q24h x3d Ceftriaxone 1g IV q24h if hospitalization required Coverage against Campylobacter/Shigella/Salmonella
fichas.fuentes: IDSA 2017 · ACOG Committee Opinion No. 614 (2014, reaffirmed 2021) · WHO 2019

fichas.titulo: Respiratory infections (COVID-19, Influenza and ILI) in pregnancy
fichas.texto: ILI (Influenza-Like Illness): sudden-onset fever (≥37.8-38.0°C) + cough or sore throat, with no other diagnosis. Virologic diagnosis: nasopharyngeal swab for multiplex RT-PCR (Influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2, RSV), or rapid antigen test (high specificity, lower sensitivity — confirm with PCR if clinical suspicion is high and the result is negative). 1st trimester: Acetaminophen 500-1000mg PO q6-8h (max 3-4g/day). Early temperature control is mandatory — sustained hyperthermia >38.5°C during organogenesis is associated with neural tube defects and congenital heart disease. Influenza: Oseltamivir 75mg PO q12h x5d, within the first 48h (safe in all trimesters). Mild COVID-19: hydration and rest, avoid NSAIDs; risk of progression: consider Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir based on risk-benefit balance. 2nd trimester: continue Acetaminophen and Oseltamivir at standard dosing. Fetal monitoring: FHR and uterine activity (paroxysmal cough and fever can induce myometrial irritability). Moderate/severe COVID-19 requiring O2: Dexamethasone 6mg/day IV/PO x10 days (or until discharge). Hospitalize if SpO2 <94% or tachypnea. 3rd trimester: greater vulnerability — diaphragm elevation reduces functional residual capacity, with risk of rapid hypoxemia and ARDS. Continuous electronic fetal monitoring (NST/CTG). Thromboprophylaxis in hospitalized COVID-19: Enoxaparin 40mg SC/day during admission, extend based on postpartum risk factors. If pregnancy must be ended for maternal respiratory deterioration between wk 24-34: Dexamethasone 6mg q12h (4 doses) — dual purpose (maternal treatment + fetal lung maturation). Preferred antiviral regimens: Influenza A and B: Oseltamivir 75mg PO q12h x5 days (double to 10 days in immunosuppressed patients or severe ICU cases). High-risk mild-moderate COVID-19: Nirmatrelvir + Ritonavir (Paxlovid) 300/100mg PO q12h x5 days (start within the first 5 days of symptoms). Severe/hospitalized COVID-19 with hypoxemia (SpO2 <94%): Dexamethasone 6mg IV/PO once daily for up to 10 days + Remdesivir 200mg IV day 1, then 100mg IV/day x4 additional days (safe in pregnancy under hepatic/renal monitoring) + weight-adjusted prophylactic Enoxaparin.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG 2023 · CDC 2023 · WHO

fichas.texto: The physiologic hypervolemia and baseline tachycardia of pregnancy mask the early signs of shock. The period of greatest risk is the defervescence phase (fever drop, days 3-7), with massive plasma leakage and hemoconcentration. Obstetric risk: threatened miscarriage, preterm birth, placental abruption, postpartum hemorrhage and vertical transmission (if the illness occurs in the immediate peripartum period). Group A — no warning signs (supervised outpatient management): acute fever + ≥2 of: myalgias, arthralgias, headache, retro-orbital pain, rash, leukopenia; no decompensated comorbidities and adequate oral tolerance. Abundant oral hydration 2-3L/day. Acetaminophen 500-750mg PO q6h (max 3g/day). ⚠️ Absolute prohibition: NSAIDs, Dipyrone (hypotension/dyscrasias) and Aspirin (hemorrhage/Reye syndrome). Daily clinical review with CBC (Hct/platelets) until 48h post-defervescence. Group B — every pregnant patient is classified here due to her physiologic vulnerability → requires hospital observation: B1 (no warning signs, with a risk condition): hospitalization for close monitoring and maintenance oral or IV fluid/electrolyte replacement. B2 (with warning signs — incipient leakage): intense/continuous abdominal pain, persistent vomiting (≥3/h or ≥4/6h), fluid accumulation (ascites, pleural effusion, thickened gallbladder wall), mucosal bleeding, lethargy/drowsiness, postural hypotension, hepatomegaly >2cm, rising Hct with rapidly falling platelets. 0.9% NS or Lactated Ringer's 10mL/kg/h x1-2h → if improving: stepwise taper (5-7 → 3-5 → 2-3mL/kg/h) to complete 24-48h; if not improving or Hct rises: manage as Group C. Group C — severe dengue (hemorrhagic/shock/organ failure, ICU management): dengue shock (weak/undetectable pulse, cold extremities, capillary refill >2sec, pulse pressure ≤20mmHg) or respiratory distress from fluid accumulation; severe hemorrhage (hematemesis, melena, massive genital bleeding/PPH, intra-abdominal bleeding); severe organ involvement (AST/ALT ≥1,000 IU/L, altered consciousness, cardiomyopathy, renal failure). Resuscitation: crystalloids (Lactated Ringer's or 0.9% NS) 20mL/kg IV bolus over 15-30min. If shock reverses: reduce to 10mL/kg/h x1-2h and taper gradually. If it does NOT reverse after 2-3 boluses: elevated Hct → colloids (Albumin 0.5-1g/kg or synthetic colloids 10-20mL/kg over 30-60min); sharply falling Hct → suspect occult/GI/uterine hemorrhage → immediate packed red blood cell transfusion (10mL/kg). Platelet transfusion: not recommended prophylactically based on count alone (<20,000-50,000/µL). Indicated for active severe hemorrhage or need for emergency surgery/cesarean with platelets <50,000/µL.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay (National Dengue/Chikungunya/Zika Guideline) · PAHO/WHO 2016/2022

fichas.texto: 4-5-3 mnemonic rule for the first hour of management of obstetric septic shock (postpartum/endometritis/septic abortion source): Fluid resuscitation: crystalloids 20-30mL/kg IV bolus within the first hour for hypoperfusion or elevated lactate. Vasopressor (if MAP<65 despite volume load): Norepinephrine 0.05-0.5mcg/kg/min IV, titrated to MAP≥65. Empiric antibiotic therapy within the first hour (postpartum/endometritis/septic abortion source): Ampicillin/Sulbactam 3g IV q6h + Gentamicin 5mg/kg/day IV — alternative: Piperacillin/Tazobactam 4.5g IV q6-8h ± Clindamycin (anaerobic/pelvic source coverage). Obtain blood cultures and achieve source control (uterine evacuation if septic abortion/retained products) without delaying antibiotic initiation.
fichas.fuentes: Evans L, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign, Crit Care Med 2021;49(11):e1063-e143 · MSPyBS Paraguay — National Maternal and Neonatal Code Red Guideline (2nd ed., 2021)

fichas.texto: Candidiasis: C. albicans (85-90%). Intense itching + clumpy white discharge. pH<4.5, hyphae. Tx: Fluconazole 150mg PO single dose. Recurrent: days 1-4-7 → weekly maintenance x6mo. Bacterial vaginosis: dysbiosis. Fishy-smelling discharge. Amsel ≥3/4. Tx: Metronidazole 500mg q12h x7d. Trichomoniasis: STI. Frothy yellow-green discharge. "Strawberry" cervix. Tx: Metronidazole 2g single dose + treat partner.
fichas.fuentes: CDC STI Guidelines (2021) · ACOG PB 215 (2020)

fichas.texto: Polymicrobial ascending infection. Stages (Monif): I salpingitis without peritonitis · II with pelvic peritonitis · III TOA · IV rupture/septic shock. Dx: pelvic pain + cervical/uterine/adnexal motion tenderness. Outpatient Tx: Ceftriaxone 500mg IM + Doxycycline 100mg q12h x14d + Metronidazole 500mg q12h x14d. Inpatient: Ceftriaxone 1g IV q24h + same regimen. Surgery: TOA ≥8-10cm or failure at 48-72h; rupture = emergency.
fichas.fuentes: CDC STI Treatment Guidelines (2021) · Monif GRG

fichas.texto: In May 2026, an international consensus of 56 organizations (The Lancet, endorsed by WHO) renamed the condition from "Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS)" to "Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS)" — it does not change the diagnostic criteria (Rotterdam/Monash), it better reflects the systemic, metabolic and multi-hormonal nature of the condition. ≥2 of 3: (1) oligo/anovulation · (2) clinical/biochemical hyperandrogenism · (3) PCOM (ultrasound ≥20 follicles or elevated AMH). Phenotypes: A complete · B anovulatory (normal ultrasound) · C ovulatory (PCOM, regular cycles) · D non-androgenic.
fichas.fuentes: Monash Guideline (Teede et al., 2023) · Rotterdam Consensus (ESHRE/ASRM) · Teede HJ, et al. The Lancet (2026)

fichas.texto: Endometrial gland/stroma within the myometrium. Criteria: asymmetric uterus, myometrial cysts 1-5mm, echogenic islands, fan-shaped shadowing, transition zone ≥12mm, translesional vascularity on Doppler. Classification: Focal or Diffuse.
fichas.fuentes: MUSA Group Consensus (Van den Bosch et al., 2015)

fichas.texto: rASRM: I minimal 1-5pts · II mild 6-15 · III moderate 16-40 · IV severe >40. Enzian (deep): A vagina/rectovaginal septum · B uterosacrals/parametria · C rectum/sigmoid · FA extraperitoneal. Severity 1(<1cm)/2(1-3cm)/3(>3cm).
fichas.fuentes: ESHRE Guidelines (2022) · rASRM · Enzian

fichas.texto: Type 0 pedunculated intracavitary · 1 sessile <50% intramural · 2 sessile ≥50% · 3 100% intramural (contacts endometrium) · 4 100% intramural (no contact) · 5 subserosal ≥50% · 6 subserosal <50% · 7 subserosal pedunculated · 8 other locations.
fichas.fuentes: FIGO AUB Systems (Munro, 2018)

fichas.texto: Distance relative to the hymen (0cm). Stage 0 no prolapse (-3cm) · I >1cm above the hymen · II between -1 and +1cm · III >+1cm without exceeding TVL-2 · IV total eversion.
fichas.fuentes: POP-Q System (Persu et al., 2011) · ICI-ICS Guidelines (2017)

fichas.texto: SUI: urethral hypermobility, triggered by effort, small volume, no urinary frequency. UUI: detrusor overactivity, sudden urge, large volume, with frequency/nocturia. SUI Tx: Kegel → pessaries → sling (TVT/TOT). UUI Tx: bladder retraining → antimuscarinics/Mirabegron → botulinum toxin/neuromodulation.
fichas.fuentes: AUA/SUFU Guidelines 2023/2015

fichas.titulo: MRS scale and Hormone Replacement Therapy
fichas.texto: MRS (11 items): somatic, psychological, urogenital. NAMS/Heinemann scheme (total score only): 0-4 mild · 5-8 moderate · ≥9 severe (consider HRT). SOCHEG scheme (broken down by domain, each with its own severe-alteration cutoff): Somatic (items 1-4) ≥8 · Psychological (items 5-8) ≥6 · Urogenital (items 9-11) ≥3 · Total (items 1-11) ≥15. HRT by uterine status: no uterus → estrogen alone. Uterus present, perimenopause → sequential/cyclic. Postmenopause → continuous combined. Transdermal HRT (preferred, especially with hypertension, obesity BMI>30, hypertriglyceridemia, VTE risk): 17β-Estradiol gel 0.75-1.25g/day, or patches 25-50mcg/day. Endometrial protection (intact uterus): Micronized natural progesterone 200mg/day for 10-14 days/month (sequential regimen) or 100mg/day continuous · or Dydrogesterone 10-20mg/day. Tibolone (STEAR): 2.5mg/day PO (or 1.25mg/day in lower body weight or advanced perimenopause) — covers vasomotor symptoms, urogenital atrophy and bone loss prevention; does not require an added progestogen. Tissue-selective estrogen complex (alternative when avoiding a progestogen is preferred): Conjugated equine estrogens 0.45mg/day + Bazedoxifene 20mg/day — bazedoxifene (a SERM) replaces the progestogen for endometrial protection, without the bleeding or breast tenderness associated with it. Evidence from the SMART-1/SMART-2 trials (12 weeks): significant reduction in hot flush frequency/severity vs. placebo, with a 50% reduction by day 8-10 and a sustained ~90% reduction by day 83 of use; no increased risk of breast cancer, endometrial cancer, VTE, stroke or coronary disease in pooled analyses (follow-up up to 2 years — confidence limited by low event incidence and lack of longer-term data). ⚠️ Availability in Paraguay not confirmed — verify locally before prescribing. Alternative endometrial protection — 52mg LNG-IUD: off-label use alongside systemic estrogen to provide endometrial protection (plus contraception if applicable) — replace at 5 years when used for this purpose (the approved contraceptive lifespan is 8 years, but the evidence supporting endometrial protection in HRT covers up to 5 years). Local availability (Paraguay, confirm against the current pharmacy/distributor): transdermal 17β-estradiol gel/spray (e.g., Ginoderm) — available. 17β-estradiol vaginal ring — not available. Conjugated equine estrogens + bazedoxifene — availability unconfirmed. This information is contextual, to anticipate the availability conversation with the patient — it should not be used to exclude an option from the clinical list. Interaction with GLP-1/GIP agonists: the gastric emptying delay induced by semaglutide/tirzepatide (more pronounced with the latter) may reduce absorption of oral HRT — in patients on GLP-1/GIP therapy, prefer the transdermal route for estrogen therapy (same pharmacokinetic principle as in the Contraception during tirzepatide guide).
fichas.fuentes: NAMS Position Statement (2022) · Heinemann et al. (2004) · Manual para Manejo de la Mujer en Edad del Climaterio, 2nd ed. (SOCHEG, 2020) · Stute P, et al. EMAS 2026 framework, Maturitas 2026;212:109060 · MSPyBS Paraguay Res. S.G. No. 267/2023 · ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e364

fichas.titulo: Fezolinetant and elinzanetant — NK receptor antagonists, non-hormonal therapy for vasomotor symptoms
fichas.texto: Mechanism: neurokinin receptor antagonists that act on hypothalamic KNDy neurons involved in thermoregulation, with no hormonal action. Fezolinetant: selective NK3 antagonist. Elinzanetant: dual NK1/NK3 antagonist. Fezolinetant: 45mg PO once daily, with or without food. FDA-approved for vasomotor symptoms (VMS). ⚠️ FDA boxed warning: requires baseline liver function testing, repeated monthly during the first 3 months of use, and again at 6 and 9 months. Elinzanetant: 120mg PO once daily. FDA-approved for VMS and also for menopause-related sleep disturbance (a sleep benefit not included in fezolinetant's specific approval). Requires liver function testing before starting and again at 3 months of treatment — a less intensive monitoring cadence than fezolinetant. Indication (both): moderate-to-severe VMS of the climacteric, a first-line alternative when HRT is contraindicated or not the patient's preference (hormone-dependent cancer history, VTE, personal preference). In indirect network comparisons (ACOG CPG13), both drugs show similar efficacy on VMS frequency and severity; elinzanetant showed a greater effect on sleep disturbance (PROMIS sleep disturbance score) in indirect comparison with fezolinetant. Most common adverse effects vs. placebo in the OASIS trials with elinzanetant: headache and fatigue.
fichas.fuentes: Pratt MC, et al. Expert Rev Clin Pharmacol 2023;16(5):389-398 · Panay N, et al. Climacteric 2024;27(3):221-235 · ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e364 (Table 2)

fichas.texto: Interventions with supporting evidence for vasomotor symptoms (VMS), sleep disturbance and mood symptoms of the climacteric — all recommended as adjuncts to hormonal or non-hormonal pharmacologic therapy, not as first-line substitutes when pharmacologic treatment is indicated: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT): improves VMS, sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-to-moderate-quality evidence). Can be delivered in person, by phone, or online. Mindfulness-based interventions (meditation, body scanning, breathing exercises, yoga): improve sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-to-moderate-quality evidence); usual duration 8 weeks in the trials. Physical exercise: improves sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-to-moderate-quality evidence); greatest sleep benefit with 70-90 minute sessions. Clinical hypnosis: reduces VMS and improves sleep and anxiety symptoms (conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence); weekly 45-minute sessions or self-hypnosis programs with a daily 20-minute recording. Acupuncture: reduces VMS and improves sleep and mood (conditional recommendation, low-quality evidence); high heterogeneity across protocols, most trials conducted in China. ⚠️ Natural products and supplements — NOT recommended: the available evidence does not support the efficacy or safety of phytoestrogens (e.g., soy isoflavones) or herbal supplements for the treatment of vasomotor or menopausal symptoms — limited by small sample sizes and heterogeneity of formulations/doses/durations across trials. Since they are not FDA-regulated or evaluated for safety/purity as nutritional supplements, no leading international guideline (ACOG, NAMS/The Menopause Society, IMS) includes them among recommended treatment options.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 13. Management of Menopause-Related Vasomotor, Sleep, and Mood Symptoms. Obstet Gynecol. 2026;148(5):e345-e364

fichas.texto: T-Score: normal ≥-1.0 · osteopenia -1.0 to -2.5 · osteoporosis ≤-2.5 · severe +fracture. Z-Score (premenopausal): ≤-2.0 abnormal. FRAX (osteopenia): treat if major fracture risk ≥20% or hip ≥3%. Basic support (all patients): Elemental calcium 1,000-1,500mg/day + Vitamin D3 800-2,000 IU/day (target ≥30ng/mL). Antiresorptives: Alendronate 70mg PO weekly · Zoledronic acid 5mg IV annually · Denosumab 60mg SC every 6 months (do not stop abruptly without transitioning to another antiresorptive, due to rebound vertebral fracture risk). Anabolics (severe osteoporosis/high fracture risk): Teriparatide 20mcg/day SC, maximum 24 months of use.
fichas.fuentes: NOF/BHOF (2022) · AACE/ACE (2020) · WHO Criteria · Stute P, et al. EMAS 2026 framework, Maturitas 2026;212:109060 · MSPyBS Paraguay Res. S.G. No. 267/2023

fichas.titulo: Vitamin K2 (MK-7) — Bone and vascular health
fichas.texto: Mechanism: vitamin K2 is a cofactor for the carboxylation of vitamin K-dependent proteins — it activates osteocalcin (calcium binding to bone) and matrix Gla protein/MGP (an inhibitor of soft-tissue calcification, including the arterial wall). Distinct from vitamin K1 (dietary, predominantly hepatic/coagulation-related). Bone (Knapen et al. 2013, RCT, n=244 healthy postmenopausal women, 3 years): MK-7 180mcg/day decreased age-related loss of bone mineral content (BMC) and bone mineral density (BMD) at the lumbar spine and femoral neck (not at total hip), improved femoral neck bone strength indices, and reduced loss of vertebral height in the lower thoracic region. The source consulted does not publish the exact percentage BMD change figures or p-values — refer to the original article for those numbers before citing them with decimal precision. Vascular (Vossen et al., VitaK-CAC, JAMA Cardiology 2026, RCT, n=167 with symptomatic coronary artery disease and coronary calcium 50-400 AU, 2 years): MK-7 360mcg/day modestly slowed progression of coronary calcification (Agatston score) vs. placebo (between-group difference p=0.02), with plasma MK-7 levels in the active arm rising from 0.50 to 6.56mcg/L (p<0.001). ⚠️ The authors and the accompanying editorial describe the effect as "modest" and of still-uncertain clinical significance — they call for larger, longer-follow-up trials before considering it an intervention with impact on hard cardiovascular events. No relevant adverse events were reported. Practical doses (per the evidence cited, two distinct contexts — not interchangeable): bone loss prevention in the climacteric: MK-7 180mcg/day. Cardiovascular context (established coronary disease): the dose studied was 360mcg/day, in a population with already-diagnosed heart disease — there is no equivalent evidence in general primary prevention. Combination with vitamin D3: both vitamins act on complementary axes of bone metabolism (D3 increases calcium absorption and osteocalcin synthesis; K2 activates/carboxylates it) — see the vitamin D3 dose in the Osteoporosis and bone densitometry guide (above).
fichas.fuentes: Knapen MHJ, Drummen NE, Smit E, Vermeer C, Theuwissen E. Three-year low-dose menaquinone-7 supplementation helps decrease bone loss in healthy postmenopausal women. Osteoporos Int. 2013;24(9):2499-2507 · Vossen LM, de Leeuw PW, Schurgers LJ, et al. Two Years of Menaquinone-7 Supplementation and Coronary Artery Calcification: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA Cardiol. 2026 (online Jun 10, 2026). doi:10.1001/jamacardio.2026.1279

fichas.titulo: WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria (MEC) for contraception
fichas.texto: Categories: 1 no restriction · 2 benefits>risks · 3 risks>benefits · 4 absolute contraindication. Cat 4 (combined methods): severe hypertension, VTE/thrombosis, thrombophilias, active breast cancer, smoker ≥35yo+15cig/day, migraine with aura, severe liver disease.
fichas.fuentes: WHO MEC (2015) · CDC US MEC (2016) · ACOG CO 736 (2018)

fichas.titulo: Contraception — General classification and mechanisms of action
fichas.texto: By family: hormonal (combined estrogen+progestin vs. progestin-only) · barrier (condom, diaphragm, spermicides) · IUD (non-hormonal copper vs. hormonal LNG-IUS) · LARC (implant, IUD/IUS) · permanent (tubal ligation/vasectomy) · fertility awareness-based methods (FABM). Combined mechanisms (estrogen+progestin): suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary axis (inhibit the GnRH/FSH-LH surge → anovulation) + thickening of cervical mucus + endometrial thinning. Progestin-only mechanisms: the dominant and constant effect is thickening of cervical mucus (barrier to sperm migration); suppression of ovulation is dose- and route-dependent — high with the injectable/implant, variable with the minipill. Copper IUD: local spermicidal/inflammatory effect, non-hormonal (foreign-body reaction + copper cytotoxicity on sperm and the ovum). LNG-IUS: dominant local endometrial effect (atrophy, mucus thickening) + partial, dose-dependent suppression of ovulation, greater with higher released doses.
fichas.fuentes: World Health Organization. Medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use, 6th ed. 2025 · World Health Organization. Family planning/contraception methods. WHO Fact Sheet, updated 3 July 2025

fichas.texto: Group of non-hormonal methods that identify the fertile window to avoid intercourse (or use a barrier) on those days. Effectiveness is highly dependent on instruction and discipline of use — the gap between perfect use and typical use is the widest of all contraceptive methods (see comparative table). Calendar/Ogino-Knaus: estimates the fertile window from the history of previous cycles — unreliable with irregular cycles. Basal body temperature (BBT): detects the post-ovulatory rise (~0.3-0.5°C), retrospectively confirming that ovulation has already occurred — see also the biphasic pattern described in the ovarian cycle physiology guide. Cervical mucus (Billings method): identifies the elastic/clear mucus around ovulation. Symptothermal (Sensiplan protocol): combines basal temperature + cervical mucus in a standardized protocol — has shown high effectiveness in studies with intensive training and adherence; those results should not be automatically extrapolated to the whole user population without that same level of instruction. Standardized mucus methods (Creighton Model FertilityCare System): conceptually derived from Billings, with structured observation and charting; requires formal instruction and follow-up by a certified instructor. Standard Days Method / CycleBeads: a simplified calendar-based method, included in WHO/CDC recommendations — identifies a fixed fertile window based on cycle day, most useful with regular cycles. Fertility monitors/apps (e.g. Marquette): algorithms that combine urinary biomarkers (LH, estrogen metabolites) with cervical mucus and/or temperature via a dedicated monitor; evidence of population-level effectiveness is heterogeneous by protocol and device — consider as a support tool, not a substitute for method education. For FABM effectiveness figures, use the Peragallo Urrutia et al. 2018 systematic review (above) as the main reference — not a single figure for all methods: real-world effectiveness varies a great deal depending on which of these protocols is used and with what level of instruction/adherence, not merely by "being a FABM".
fichas.fuentes: Manhart MD, Duane M, Lind A, Sinai I, Golden-Tevald J. Fertility awareness-based methods of family planning: a review of effectiveness for avoiding pregnancy using SORT. Osteopath Fam Physician. 2013;5(1):2-8 · Peragallo Urrutia R, Polis CB, Jensen ET, Greene ME, Kennedy E, Stanford JB. Effectiveness of Fertility Awareness-Based Methods for Pregnancy Prevention: A Systematic Review. Obstet Gynecol. 2018;132(3):591-604

fichas.titulo: Contraception — Comparative effectiveness (perfect use vs. typical use) and master table
fichas.texto: Failure rate per year (pregnancies per 100 users), approximate Pearl Index: Method Perfect use Typical use Subdermal implant 0.05% 0.05% Female sterilization 0.5% 0.5% Vasectomy 0.10% 0.15% IUD/IUS (LNG) 0.1–0.2% 0.1–0.2% Copper IUD 0.6% 0.8% Injectable (DMPA) 0.2% 4% Combined pill / progestin-only pill 0.3% 7% Patch / vaginal ring 0.3% 7% Diaphragm + spermicide 6% 12% Male condom 2% 13% Female condom 5% 21% FABM (depending on method) 0.4–5% 2–23% Spermicides alone 18% 21% No method 85% 85% LARCs (implant, IUD/IUS) are the only methods where perfect use and typical use practically coincide — they do not depend on the user's daily/per-act adherence, which explains their superior real-world effectiveness.
fichas.fuentes: Trussell J. Contraceptive failure in the United States. Contraception. 2011;83(5):397-404 · Peragallo Urrutia R, et al. Obstet Gynecol. 2018;132(3):591-604 (FABM row)

fichas.texto: Etonogestrel subdermal implant (Implanon/Nexplanon, 1 rod): approved duration of 5 years — the FDA extended the approval from 3 to 5 years in January 2026, based on a trial (NCT04626596) with no pregnancies and a Pearl Index of 0.0 during years 4 and 5. Dominant mechanism: suppression of ovulation (anovulation) + thickening of cervical mucus. Immediate reversibility upon removal. 2-rod levonorgestrel implant (Jadelle/Norplant-2/Sino-Implant): 5 years. Mechanism somewhat different from etonogestrel: endometrial atrophy and the cervical mucus plug predominate over suppression of ovulation (which is more variable with this implant). LNG-IUS (levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system) — 3 distinct doses/durations, not a single one: LNG 52mg (Mirena/Liletta/Levosert/Asertia): 8 years. LNG 19.5mg (Kyleena): 5 years. LNG 13.5mg (Jaydess/Skyla — sometimes marketed as a hormonal "Mini IUD", not to be confused with the copper mini-IUD in the following row): 3 years, with lower serum LNG levels and greater preservation of ovulatory cycles than the higher doses. Copper IUD — duration depends on copper load/frame size, not a single value: High-load (TCu380A and equivalents, e.g. Multiload 375, Nova T, Flexi, T Cu 380A): 10-12 years per WHO (the range depends on the specific product). Reduced-frame/"mini" copper IUD (smaller copper surface area, usually reserved for nulliparous patients or small uterine cavities): shorter duration, typically on the order of 5 years — confirm against the specific model/brand's insert, since a lower copper load corresponds to a shorter approved duration. Silver-core IUD (Cu-Ag, e.g. Andalan Silverflex): the silver core slows fragmentation/oxidation of the copper wire inside the uterus — a mechanism that in theory extends the device's useful life relative to a pure copper IUD. However, at least one regional manufacturer labels its "Silver T" presentation with a duration of 5 years, shorter than that of high-load copper IUDs — ⚠️ there is real variability between brands/markets; confirm the duration against the specific brand's insert used in your practice before treating it as a single figure for this guide. Regarding silver's "bactericidal" effect: ionic silver does have well-documented general antibacterial activity in the microbiology/materials literature — but the source educational material (AC Hormonal 2025) specifically describes silver's role in the IUD as slowing copper fragmentation, not as a local anti-infective mechanism aimed at reducing PID; ⚠️ I did not find a gynecology-specific source documenting a clinically relevant bactericidal effect of the silver core on pelvic infection risk — if you have a specific reference for that, happy to add it. All IUDs/IUSs are also useful as post-coital emergency contraception (see following guide). Non-contraceptive benefits of the LNG-IUS: significantly reduces menstrual bleeding (therapeutic use in AUB, see corresponding guide), and offers some relative protection against symptomatic PID compared with the copper IUD. Contraindications (MEC Cat 4): see the WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria guide — distortion of the uterine cavity, active pelvic infection, untreated cervical/endometrial cancer (IUDs in general); active breast cancer (LNG-IUS, due to the hormonal component).
fichas.fuentes: WHO — Intrauterine devices, fact sheet (updated) · FDA — extended-use approval, Nexplanon (January 2026) · FDA labeling Kyleena/Mirena/Liletta/Jaydess-Skyla · Puesta al Día en AC Hormonal 2025 (curated educational material) · World Health Organization. Medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use, 6th ed. 2025

fichas.titulo: Emergency contraception — Yuzpe, LNG, Ulipristal, Mifepristone, IUD
fichas.texto: LNG, Ulipristal, and Yuzpe share a mechanism: they inhibit or delay ovulation — they are not abortifacients, they do not interrupt an already-implanted pregnancy. Mifepristone (added to this group by WHO in 2026) is the exception on this list: its mechanism is dose/timing-dependent (see detail in its own bullet). Levonorgestrel 1.5mg single dose: effective up to 72-96h, with decreasing effectiveness the more time has passed since intercourse — the sooner, the better. Ulipristal acetate 30mg single dose: effective up to 120h (5 days), and holds its effectiveness better near the day of ovulation than LNG. ⚠️ Reduces the effectiveness of regular hormonal contraception started afterward — use a barrier method or postpone restarting the usual hormonal method by ~5 days. Yuzpe regimen (combined high-dose ethinylestradiol+levonorgestrel, given as 2 doses 12h apart): historical alternative when LNG/Ulipristal are not available — less effective and with more adverse effects (nausea/vomiting) than current dedicated methods. Mifepristone 10-50mg single dose (added by WHO, expanded contraceptive options guideline, Sept. 2026): effective as soon as possible and within 5 days post-coitus. Dose/timing-dependent mechanism: given before the LH surge, it delays/inhibits ovulation just like the other methods in this group; given already in the luteal phase (post-ovulation), its antiprogestogenic effect does demonstrably delay endometrial maturation — unlike LNG (no demonstrated endometrial alteration) and Ulipristal (theoretical antiprogestogen, with no demonstrated anti-implantation effect at the EC dose). Availability and the regulatory framework vary by country — confirm before prescribing. ⚠️ Medico-legal note (relevant given CaVeSal®'s international reach): this mechanistic distinction matters depending on each jurisdiction's legal framework on the onset of life. Where life is considered to begin at fertilization/conception (e.g. Paraguay), a method with no demonstrated anti-implantation effect is not classified as abortifacient; where it is considered to begin at implantation, the distinction loses legal relevance. This guide describes both frameworks without taking a position. Post-coital copper IUD: the most effective method of emergency contraception (failure rate <0.1%), insertable up to 5 days post-coitus — with the added advantage of remaining in place as long-term ongoing contraception.
fichas.fuentes: World Health Organization. Medical eligibility criteria for contraceptive use, 6th ed. 2025 · World Health Organization. Selected practice recommendations for contraceptive use, 4th ed. 2025 · World Health Organization. WHO guidelines on expanding contraceptive options, 23 Sept. 2026 (mifepristone as EC — primary text on WHO IRIS blocked to automated access in this session; figures corroborated via independent secondary coverage, DevelopmentAid.org)

fichas.texto: What it is: a natural estrogen of fetal origin (synthesized by the fetal liver from estriol), with tissue-selective activity — agonist in the CNS, bone and genital tissue, antagonist in breast tissue, and little estrogenic effect in liver and vascular tissue. Hepatic metabolism by glucuronidation only (no CYP450 pathway), which reduces the risk of drug interactions. Combined formulation: Estetrol 15mg + Drospirenone 3mg, 1 tablet/day. Efficacy: Pearl Index 1.52 (95% CI 1.04-2.16) in the pivotal phase 3 trials (31 pregnancies / 2,837 women / 26,455 cycles). Regular cycles in 82-94%; spotting ~15% at cycle 12; amenorrhea ~10%. Coagulation/VTE profile: ⚠️ the available literature does not provide a relative risk or odds ratio for VTE versus other combined hormonal contraceptives — this figure is pending verification against the primary articles before being cited as a number. What is documented: a smaller rise in sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG +54% vs. +74% with ethinylestradiol) and smaller changes in lipid profile, with no change in thrombin generation (Douxfils 2020) — surrogate markers suggesting a smaller hepatic/procoagulant impact than ethinylestradiol, but which do not equate to a confirmed clinical VTE risk figure: the pivotal studies recorded 1 case of DVT in 30,289 cycles, too small a number to estimate a comparative rate. The authors themselves note that these advantages remain mostly theoretical and require post-marketing surveillance. Why it may be worth raising in consultation: it is an additional option within the combined contraceptive group, useful for an informed conversation with patients who ask about it specifically — the evidence does not yet support positioning it ahead of established combined methods in terms of thrombotic safety.
fichas.fuentes: Viroga S. Un nuevo estrógeno: estetrol. Boletín Farmacológico 2025;16(2):1-3 · Creinin MD, et al. Contraception 2021;104(3):222-228 · Gemzell-Danielsson K, et al. BJOG 2022;129(1):63-71 · Douxfils J, et al. Contraception 2020;102:396-402 · AEMPS label, cima.aemps.es, code 1211547001

fichas.texto: LAM (>98%): amenorrhea + exclusive breastfeeding + <6 months postpartum, all three together. Progestin-only: Cat 1-2 from the start. Combined: Cat 4 if <6 wk breastfeeding; improves over time. Copper IUD: Cat 1 immediate (<48h) or delayed (≥4wk); Cat 3 in between.
fichas.fuentes: WHO MEC (2015)

fichas.texto: PALM (structural): Polyp · Adenomyosis · Leiomyoma · Malignancy/hyperplasia. COEIN (non-structural): Coagulopathy · Ovulatory dysfunction · Endometrial · Iatrogenic · Not otherwise classified.

fichas.texto: 💡 For hyperprolactinemia (anovulation/infertility), see the full guide in the "Preconception and Fertility" chapter.

Reproductive age: Mediterranean diet, 500-750kcal deficit, aerobic 150-300min/week + strength training. Climacteric: protein 1.2-1.6g/kg/day, Calcium+Vitamin D, strength training 3x/week, impact/balance exercises.
