fichas.titulo: Vitamin D — Tissue associations and supplementation schemes (FLASOG)
fichas.texto: The vitamin D receptor (VDR) is present in multiple tissues of the reproductive tract and neighboring tissues, underlying the clinical associations described in Table 1 of the FLASOG document: Table 1 — Tissue distribution of the VDR and impact on gyn-obstetric conditions: Ovary and endometrium → PMOS (formerly PCOS), infertility, endometriosis → proposed mechanism: endometrial receptivity, implantation, insulin sensitivity, inflammatory modulation. Placenta → gestational complications (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth) → placental angiogenesis and maternal-fetal immune tolerance. Vagina, bladder, and urethra → genitourinary syndrome of menopause, recurrent urinary tract infections → vaginal epithelial integrity, collagen synthesis, pH regulation, mucosal immunity. Bone and skeletal muscle → osteosarcopenia, osteoporosis, bone fragility, risk of falls/fractures → bone mineralization, preservation of muscle mass (type II fibers), muscle fat clearance. Pelvic floor musculature → pelvic floor dysfunction, urinary incontinence, pelvic sarcopenia → type II striated muscle fibers, muscle strength. Mammary gland → proliferative conditions → regulation of cell proliferation, local tissue homeostasis. Table 2 — Guiding supplementation schemes (cholecalciferol, unless calcifediol is indicated): Prevention: 1,000-2,000 IU/day — standard maintenance dose. Insufficiency: 2,000 IU/day or 50,000 IU/month — gradual correction. Moderate deficiency: 50,000 IU every 2 weeks × 6-8 weeks — prioritizes comfort and adherence. Severe deficiency (<10 ng/mL): 50,000 IU/week × 6-8 weeks — rapid correction; avoid massive annual/spaced-out doses. Obesity or malabsorption: doses 2-3 times the usual amount, due to lower bioavailability. Clarification — GLP-1/GIP is not the same as malabsorption: use of GLP-1/GIP analogues (semaglutide, tirzepatide — see corresponding guide) is not by itself an indication to raise the Vitamin D dose under the "obesity or malabsorption" scheme above. These drugs slow gastric emptying and reduce intake, but do not create a state of fat/fat-soluble vitamin malabsorption comparable to bariatric surgery (gastric bypass, sleeve with a malabsorptive component), which does justify it. Adjust the Vitamin D dose in a patient on GLP-1/GIP according to her actual nutritional status/serum levels, not automatically because she is on the drug. Cholecalciferol vs. calcifediol: the FLASOG document positions cholecalciferol as the usual first line, reserving calcifediol for scenarios of obesity/malabsorption, liver disease, need for faster correction, or insufficient response to cholecalciferol. Pregnancy: 1,000-2,000 IU/day as the usual scheme; for deficiency requiring more intensive correction, individualize under supervision, not exceeding 4,000 IU/day. Note: the FLASOG document frames the therapeutic goal as reaching "adequate serum 25(OH)D concentrations," without setting a single numeric target range in ng/mL in its text — which is why this guide does not reproduce a single "target" figure (an earlier version used 40-80 ng/mL; it was removed as it was not sourced in this document). The deficiency/insufficiency thresholds are explicit and underlie Table 2 above. ⚠️ Caution note: some educational sources mention experimental very-high-dose protocols (e.g. "Coimbra," 40,000-100,000 IU/day) for autoimmune disease — these protocols are experimental, carry real risk of hypercalcemia/hypercalciuria/kidney stones, and are not endorsed by any formal FLASOG, ACOG, NICE, or USPSTF guideline; they must not be confused with the standard supplementation schemes in this guide. See the next guide for the current controversy over whether population-wide screening (routine 25-OH-D testing) is warranted before prescribing this supplementation.
fichas.fuentes: Federación Latinoamericana de Sociedades de Obstetricia y Ginecología (FLASOG). Recomendaciones sobre Vitamina D en Salud Reproductiva. Ginecol Obstet Mex. 2026;94:e11309 · Demay MB, Pittas AG, Bikle DD, et al. Vitamin D for the Prevention of Disease: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline. J Clin Endocrinol Metab. 2024

fichas.titulo: Vitamin D — Controversy over population screening (FLASOG vs. Neuquén/USPSTF)
fichas.texto: There is a real, current divergence between organizations over whether population-wide screening (routine 25-OH-D testing) and active supplementation are warranted in healthy women — CaVeSal presents both positions explicitly, without taking sides, so the clinical decision remains in your hands case by case: FLASOG 2026 position (interventionist): recommends active assessment and supplementation to reach "adequate serum 25(OH)D concentrations" (the document does not set a single numeric target range in its text — see the deficiency/insufficiency thresholds in Table 2 of the previous guide), based on the tissue associations described in the previous guide (preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, preterm birth, PMOS). Neuquén Bulletin 2026 position (restrictive, citing USPSTF/NICE/CONETEC/Endocrine Society): recommends against routine 25-OH-D testing in the healthy population — available evidence does not consistently demonstrate that screening followed by supplementation improves clinically relevant maternal or fetal outcomes beyond standard population-wide supplementation without prior testing (already in the Supplementation in Pregnancy guide in this same index); reserves targeted testing for specific risk groups. Both positions come from current literature from different bodies — there is, as of this guide, no single consensus reconciling them. The choice between actively screening or supplementing without prior testing remains at your clinical discretion, case by case.
fichas.fuentes: FLASOG — Recomendaciones sobre Vitamina D en Salud Reproductiva (2026) · Comité de Biotecnología, Ministerio de Salud de Neuquén — Boletín Vitamina D (September 2026), citing USPSTF/NICE/CONETEC/Endocrine Society

fichas.texto: Basson model. Pelvic floor/Kegel. Lubricants. Dual protection + post-coital voiding.
fichas.fuentes: ISSWSH (2019) · ACOG CO 141

fichas.titulo: Sexual health in the climacteric and postmenopause
fichas.texto: GSM: hyaluronic acid, local topical estrogen, Prasterone, Ospemifene. HSDD: off-label transdermal testosterone + CBT.
fichas.fuentes: NAMS GSM (2020) · ISSWSH · ACOG CO 141

fichas.texto: Definition: onset of secondary sexual characteristics before age 8 (thelarche or adrenarche) or menarche before age 9. Central precocious puberty (CPP/true, GnRH-dependent): premature activation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, with a complete and accelerated isosexual sequence (thelarche → pubarche → menarche). Idiopathic in >80-90% of girls; rule out CNS lesions (hamartomas, gliomas, hydrocephalus), especially if <6 years. Peripheral precocious puberty (PPP/pseudopuberty, GnRH-independent): autonomous secretion of sex steroids, with basal or suppressed FSH/LH from negative feedback. May be isosexual or contrasexual (virilization). Non-progressive variants: isolated premature thelarche (no bone-age advance or uterine estrogenization) and idiopathic premature adrenarche (pubic/axillary hair and apocrine odor, with DHEA-S consistent with Tanner II-III and normal basal 17-OHP). Pelvic ultrasound (transabdominal, with bladder filling) — quantitative criteria: Parameter Prepubertal Pubertal / stimulated Uterine length <35-40mm ≥40-45mm Uterine volume <2.0-3.0mL ≥3.0-4.0mL Body/cervix ratio 1:2 (or 1:1) 2:1 (or 3:1) Configuration Tubular Pear-shaped Endometrial line Not visible Visible/thickened >2mm Ovarian volume <1.5-2.0mL >2.0-3.0mL Antral follicles Absent or <4mm ≥6 of 4-8mm, or dominant >10mm A pubertal uterus (2:1 ratio, visible endometrium) reflects sustained estrogen exposure — central or ovarian in origin. Strictly prepubertal uterus and ovaries with isolated adrenarche rule out a gonadal origin and point to the adrenal gland. Anteroposterior and transverse uterine diameters are recorded together with length to calculate volume by the ellipsoid formula (L×AP×T×0.523); they do not carry an independently validated cutoff of their own. Interpretation and limitations of ultrasound (Calcaterra et al. 2021 · Kim et al., Korean CPP Guideline 2023 · Nguyen et al., meta-analysis 2021 · Chen et al. 2015 · Eugster 2015): pelvic ultrasound is an ancillary/complementary tool, not diagnostic on its own — it is interpreted together with clinical findings, Tanner stage, and hormonal profile. Published cutoffs vary considerably between studies (uterine length ≈32-40mm, ovarian volume ≈1-3mL depending on the series); a meta-analysis of 13 studies found that a uterine length of 3.2cm had a pooled sensitivity of 81.8% and specificity of 82.0% for differentiating precocious puberty from premature thelarche (Nguyen et al. 2021) — useful as a reference point, not as an absolute boundary. After age 8, overlap between prepubertal and early-pubertal values increases considerably (Eugster 2015): in girls aged 8-9, avoid concluding "axis not activated" from ultrasound alone — report in terms of presence or absence of ultrasound signs of estrogenization, and always correlate with Tanner stage and gonadotropins. Follicular distribution (peripheral/diffuse) is documented descriptively: the isolated presence of small follicles does not equal pubertal activation and can be seen normally in prepubertal girls (Eugster 2015). Algorithm: bone age by left hand-wrist X-ray (Greulich & Pyle) — an advance >1.5-2 years confirms biological impact. Basal LH ≥0.3mIU/mL + elevated estradiol + pubertal uterus → CPP (confirm with GnRH test, LH peak >5mIU/mL, and mandatory brain MRI). Basal LH <0.3mIU/mL (quiescent axis) → evaluate peripheral causes: elevated 17-OHP and DHEA-S → adrenal origin; elevated estradiol with normal 17-OHP → ovarian origin (autonomous follicular cyst, granulosa cell tumor, McCune-Albright).
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay (2025) · Carel et al. (2009) · Latronico et al. (2016) · Badouraki et al. (2008) · Greulich & Pyle (1959) · Calcaterra et al. (2021) · Kim et al., Korean CPP Guideline (2023) · Nguyen et al., meta-analysis (2021) · Chen et al. (2015) · Eugster (2015)

fichas.titulo: Precocious puberty — Doppler, additional findings, and ultrasound report template
fichas.texto: Doppler (optional): not essential; ovarian vascularization can be described and, if color Doppler is available, uterine vascularization as well. Additional findings to rule out: ovarian cysts, tumors, müllerian malformations, free pelvic fluid, adnexal abnormalities. Structured ultrasound report template: Transabdominal pelvic ultrasound Uterus: anteverted, ___ × ___ × ___ mm (length × AP × transverse), volume ___ mL. Tubular/pear-shaped morphology. Body/cervix ratio ___. Homogeneous myometrium. Endometrium: not visible / visible, thickness ___ mm. Right ovary: ___ × ___ × ___ mm, volume ___ mL. ___ follicles present, largest ___ mm, peripheral/diffuse distribution. Left ovary: ___ × ___ × ___ mm, volume ___ mL. ___ follicles present, largest ___ mm, peripheral/diffuse distribution. Cul-de-sac: no free fluid. Conclusion: uterus and ovaries with morphological and biometric features showing no clear ultrasound signs of significant pubertal estrogenization / with ultrasound signs of estrogenization and onset of pubertal development / with pubertal development appropriate for age. Correlate with Tanner stage and hormonal evaluation (LH, FSH, estradiol) according to clinical context, especially in girls aged 8-9 given the overlap between prepubertal and early-pubertal patterns.
fichas.fuentes: Calcaterra et al. (2021) · Lee et al. (2016) · Eugster (2015)

fichas.texto: Basal 17-OHP (points to adrenal origin): <1.0ng/mL rules out a major 21-hydroxylase deficiency. 1.0-2.0ng/mL gray zone — stimulation test needed. >2.0ng/mL high suspicion of non-classic congenital adrenal hyperplasia (NC-CAH). >10-20ng/mL virtually unequivocal diagnosis of CAH, or suspicion of an adrenal neoplasm (add adrenal ultrasound/CT/MRI). ACTH stimulation test (250µg IV/IM, 17-OHP at 60 min): post-stimulation >10ng/mL (>1000ng/dL) is the gold standard confirming NC-CAH from 21-hydroxylase deficiency. CPP — axis suppression with depot GnRH agonists: Leuprolide 3.75-7.5mg IM/SC every 28 days (monthly) or 11.25mg every 84 days (quarterly). Triptorelin 3.75mg IM every 28 days or 11.25mg every 12 weeks. Goal: growth velocity <4-5cm/year, stabilizing Tanner stage and preserving adult height. Discontinuation: once bone age reaches 11.0-11.5 years. NC-CAH — adrenal suppression: hydrocortisone 8-12mg/m²/day in 2-3 oral doses, with the larger dose at night (suppresses the morning ACTH peak). Indicated for symptomatic accelerated adrenarche, bone age advanced >1.5-2 years, virilization, or compromised predicted height. Follow-up: growth velocity, annual bone age, and periodic 17-OHP/androstenedione/DHEA-S — avoid iatrogenic hypercortisolism.
fichas.fuentes: Speiser et al. (2018) · Endocrine Society · Carel et al. (2009) · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025)

fichas.titulo: Care for sexual assault survivors — Principles and history-taking
fichas.texto: Primary medical emergency. Do not require a prior police report. Non-judgmental history: time elapsed, type of contact, LMP, subsequent hygiene.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay · CDC (2021) · WHO

fichas.titulo: Care for sexual assault survivors — Examination and samples
fichas.texto: Exam with consent explained step by step. Forensic and clinical samples if <72h (HIV, VDRL, HBsAg, NAAT).
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay · CDC (2021) · WHO

fichas.titulo: Care for sexual assault survivors — Contraception and STI prophylaxis
fichas.texto: Levonorgestrel 1.5mg single dose (ideally <72h). Ceftriaxone+Azithromycin+Metronidazole. Hep B + Tetanus vaccination.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay · CDC (2021)

fichas.titulo: Care for sexual assault survivors — HIV and legal management
fichas.texto: HIV PEP: TDF/FTC + Dolutegravir, start <72h, 28 days. Mandatory reporting. Immediate mental health referral.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay · CDC (2021)

fichas.texto: Breast development (girls): M1 prepubertal (nipple only) · M2 breast bud/thelarche · M3 further enlargement without contour separation · M4 areola forms a secondary mound · M5 mature. Genital development (boys): G1 infantile (<4mL) · G2 volume 4-8mL, scrotal reddening · G3 penile lengthening, 10-12mL · G4 increased girth+glans, 15-20mL, darkened scrotum · G5 adult, >20mL. Pubic hair (both sexes): I no hair · II sparse/fine · III darker/curlier · IV adult type, reduced area · V adult type, complete. Thelarche precedes menarche by ~2.5 years (average 12.5 years). Assess breast/genital development and hair separately.
fichas.fuentes: Marshall WA, Tanner JM. Archives of Disease in Childhood (1969/1970)

fichas.titulo: Bone age assessment by hand and wrist X-ray
fichas.texto: Technique: AP X-ray of the left hand and wrist. Greulich and Pyle Atlas: visual comparison by age/sex. Key milestone: sesamoid bone of the adductor pollicis marks the onset of the growth spurt (≈11 girls, 13 boys). TW3 Method: quantitative, 20 bones, greater precision for predicting adult height. Interpretation: normal ±1-1.5 years · delayed >1.5-2 years (constitutional delay, hypothyroidism, GH deficiency, malnutrition) · advanced >1.5-2 years (precocious puberty, obesity, CAH).
fichas.fuentes: Greulich WW, Pyle SI (2nd ed., 1959) · Tanner JM et al., TW3 Method (2001)

fichas.titulo: Müllerian anomalies — Agenesis and unicornuate uterus (Class I-II)
fichas.texto: Embryology: Müllerian ducts → tubes/uterus/cervix/upper 2-3 of vagina. Urogenital sinus → lower 1/3 of vagina/hymen/bladder/urethra. ⚠️ 30-50% of Müllerian anomalies are associated with renal malformations — renal ultrasound mandatory. Class I (MRKH): absent uterus/vagina, functional ovaries, primary amenorrhea with developed breasts. Class II (unicornuate): failure of one duct. Risk of ectopic pregnancy in the rudimentary horn + preterm birth.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Müllerian Anomalies Classification (2021) · ESHRE/ESGE Consensus (2013/2016) · ACOG CO 730 (2018)

fichas.titulo: Müllerian anomalies — Didelphys, bicornuate, septate, DES (Class III-VII)
fichas.texto: Class III (didelphys): 2 uteri/cervices, vaginal septum. OHVIRA syndrome: +obstructive septum+ipsilateral renal agenesis → hematocolpos. Class IV (bicornuate): 1 cervix, external fundal notch >1cm. Class V (septate, most common): normal serosa, internal septum. Leading cause of recurrent miscarriage. Tx: hysteroscopic metroplasty. Class VI (arcuate): normal variant. Class VII (DES): T-shaped uterus.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM (2021) · ESHRE/ESGE (2013/2016)

fichas.titulo: Urogenital sinus anomalies and diagnostic algorithm
fichas.texto: Imperforate hymen: cryptomenorrhea + violaceous bulging → hematocolpos. Transverse vaginal septum: perforated or complete. Congenital cloaca: vagina-urethra-rectum confluence (common in CAH). Algorithm: 3D ultrasound → pelvic MRI → mandatory renal ultrasound → HSG/hysteroscopy.

fichas.titulo: Hysteroscopy — Technical principles and distension media
fichas.texto: Bettocchi/"no-touch" technique: no speculum or tenaculum. Media: saline/Ringer's (bipolar) · Glycine/Sorbitol (monopolar only). Fluid deficit limits: saline stop at 2,500mL (1,500 in cardiac/renal disease) · Glycine stop at 1,000mL (risk of severe hyponatremia).
fichas.fuentes: AAGL Practice Guidelines (2020) · Bettocchi S et al. (2016) · ESHRE/ESGE (2023)

fichas.titulo: Hysteroscopy — Anatomical classification of the cervical canal
fichas.texto: Type 1 physiological (straight, smooth entry) · Type 2 tortuous (S/Z-shaped, requires scope rotation) · Type 3 stenotic/atrophic (prepare with estrogen ± Misoprostol) · Type 4 obstructed (adhesions/polyps, millimetric dissection).
fichas.fuentes: AAGL (2020) · Bettocchi et al. (2016)

fichas.titulo: Hysteroscopy — Diagnostic indications and surgical techniques
fichas.texto: Indications: AUB (1st choice for focal PALM-COEIN), polyps, FIGO 0/1/2 submucosal fibroids, hyperplasia/carcinoma, infertility/recurrent miscarriage, retained IUD. Techniques: polypectomy (bipolar loop) · myomectomy (FIGO 0/1 ≤3-4cm, slicing) · metroplasty (septum incision) · adhesiolysis (centrifugal).
fichas.fuentes: AAGL (2020) · ESHRE/ESGE (2023) · RCOG Green-top No. 59

fichas.titulo: Hysteroscopy — Prevention and management of major complications
fichas.texto: False tract/perforation: blunt+stable instrument→observation+antibiotics. Activated electrode→mandatory exploratory laparoscopy. Vasovagal reflex: Trendelenburg+fluids+Atropine 0.5-1.0mg IV if persistent. Gas embolism: do not purge with air, intrauterine pressure 70-100mmHg.
fichas.fuentes: AAGL (2020) · ESHRE/ESGE (2023)

fichas.titulo: Urethral continence — Anatomical-functional basis and diagnostic evaluation
fichas.texto: Hammock theory (DeLancey): fibroconnective/muscular support that compresses the urethra. Q-Tip test: hypermobility if deflection ≥30°. VLPP: >90 pure hypermobility · 60-90 mixed · <60 intrinsic sphincter deficiency (ISD). Blaivas-Olsson: 0 not demonstrated · I <1.5cm without cystocele · IIa >1.5cm with cystocele · IIb already descended at rest · III open at rest (=ISD).
fichas.fuentes: DeLancey JO (1994) · Petros PE, Ulmsten UI (1990/1993) · ICS/IUGA (2020)

fichas.titulo: SUI — Conservative management and minimally invasive therapies
fichas.texto: 1st line: PFMT/Kegel ≥3 sets/day x3 months + biofeedback. Pessaries. 2nd line (office-based): Luksenburg system (suburethral PDO/PCL thread mesh, outpatient) — most recent technique, less consolidated evidence than the rest of this guide. Vaginal laser/radiofrequency. Bulking agents (Bulkamid).
fichas.fuentes: ACOG & AUGS PB 155 (2015, reaffirmed 2025) · Luksenburg A.

fichas.texto: Luksenburg system (suburethral spider web): PDO/PCL thread mesh, outpatient under local anesthesia — hammock-type support + directed neocollagenesis (12-24 months). Note: most recent technique, less consolidated evidence than the rest of this guide. Other options: vaginal laser/fractional radiofrequency (collagen remodeling) · urethral bulking agents (Bulkamid) in elderly/high surgical risk patients.
fichas.fuentes: Luksenburg A. Suburethral Thread Web · ACOG & AUGS PB 155 (2015, reaffirmed 2025)

fichas.texto: Hypermobility (VLPP>60-90): Retropubic TVT (>85-90% efficacy, mandatory cystoscopy) · Transobturator TOT (lower bladder risk) · Burch colposuspension (if mesh contraindicated). ISD (Blaivas III, VLPP<60): Retropubic TVT (superior to TOT) · Autologous fascial sling (rescue) · Artificial urinary sphincter (refractory).
fichas.fuentes: ACOG & AUGS PB 155 (2015, reaffirmed 2025)

fichas.texto: Monthly, day 5-10 of the cycle. Inspection (3 positions) + palpation (3 fingers, circular motions, clavicle-inframammary fold, sternum-axilla).
fichas.fuentes: ACOG · American Cancer Society

fichas.titulo: STI panel in gynecology — Diagnostic tests
fichas.texto: NAAT/PCR: Chlamydia, gonorrhea, Mycoplasma genitalium, Trichomonas, high-risk HPV. Serology: syphilis, HIV, Hep B/C. Wet mount: Candida, clue cells, trophozoites.
fichas.fuentes: CDC STI 2021 · WHO

fichas.texto: Ceftriaxone 500mg IM single dose (1g if ≥150kg). Disseminated: 1g IV/IM q24h x7d. Azithromycin monotherapy no longer prioritized due to resistance.
fichas.fuentes: CDC 2021 · WHO 2021

fichas.texto: With Chlamydia not ruled out: +Doxycycline 100mg q12h x7d. With Trichomonas: Metronidazole 500mg q12h x7d. Empiric PID: Ceftriaxone+Doxycycline+Metronidazole x14d.
fichas.fuentes: CDC 2021

fichas.texto: Chlamydia: Doxycycline 100mg q12h x7d. M. genitalium: sequential therapy Doxycycline→Azithromycin (or Moxifloxacin if resistant). Ureaplasma: usual commensal, treat only if symptomatic.
fichas.fuentes: CDC 2021 · IUSTI (2021) · WHO 2016

fichas.texto: Non-hormonal: Tranexamic acid 1.3g PO 3x/day x5 days/cycle. NSAIDs. Hormonal: combined OCPs, progestins, 52mg LNG-IUD, GnRH agonists/antagonists with add-back therapy.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG (2013) · Mayo Clinic Proc (2019) · StatPearls (2025)

fichas.titulo: Abnormal uterine bleeding — Surgical indications by cause
fichas.texto: Criteria: stability, severity, failed medical treatment, fertility desire. Fibroid: myomectomy/RFA/embolization/hysterectomy. Adenomyosis: hysterectomy if fertility not desired. Polyps: polypectomy. Severe acute: D&C. Endometrial ablation: alternative, ends fertility.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG (2013) · ACOG PB 228

fichas.titulo: Ovarian and endometrial cycle — Physiology by phase
fichas.texto: 28 days: Early follicular (1-5, menstruation) · Late follicular (6-13, E2>200) · Ovulatory (14±2, LH peak) · Mid luteal (15-24, P4>10) · Late luteal (25-28, luteolysis). LH peak 24-36h pre-ovulation. Implantation window days 20-24. Day 21 P4 >3-5 confirms ovulation. Basal body temperature (BBT) patterns: monophasic (no clear rise — suggests an anovulatory cycle, no functional corpus luteum) · biphasic (typical ovulatory pattern — rises ~0.3-0.5°C after ovulation, sustained through the luteal phase) · triphasic (second rise 6-12 days post-ovulation — may be associated with implantation/early pregnancy in ~12% of confirmed cases, not diagnostic on its own, ~88% of pregnancies do not show this pattern).
fichas.fuentes: Speroff (9th ed., 2019) · Mihm et al. (2011)

fichas.texto: Early follicular (2-4): FSH <8-10 optimal, >15 low reserve. LH/FSH>2-3 suggests PCOS. AMH: optimal 1.2-3.5. Mid luteal (day 21): P4 ≥10 optimal. Thyroid: TSH target <2.5. Normal PRL <20-25.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Female Infertility Evaluation (2021) · ATA (2017)

fichas.texto: 3 pillars: (1) Ovarian — hormonal profile + AMH + AFC. (2) Tubal — HSG/HyFoSy. (3) Uterine — 3D ultrasound/sonohysterography.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Committee Opinion (2021)

fichas.titulo: Tubal patency — HyFoSy, HSG and hysteroscopy
fichas.texto: HyFoSy (echogenic foam instillation under transvaginal ultrasound, no radiation or iodinated contrast) and HSG show comparable sensitivity/specificity for tubal patency (2024 meta-analysis, 2025 agreement study) — HyFoSy with better tolerability (less pain) and no radiation exposure. Foam vs. saline (Piccioni 2017): saline medium (classic sonohysterography/SIS) disperses quickly and is limited for assessing the tubal course; foam, more viscous and echogenic, allows visualization of tubal passage and peritoneal spill — this is why it replaced saline when the goal is tubal assessment, while saline remains preferable when the goal is only the endometrial cavity (polyps, submucosal fibroids). Hysteroscopy does not assess tubal patency (uterine cavity only) — reserved for confirming/treating already-suspected intracavitary findings, not as a first-line tubal-factor study. Algorithm: HyFoSy = first line (tubal screening + cavity, no radiation) · HSG = valid alternative depending on resources · laparoscopy with chromopertubation = reserved for suspected associated pelvic pathology or an inconclusive result.
fichas.fuentes: Piccioni et al. (2017), J Clin Ultrasound · RBMO meta-analysis (2024) · HyFoSy vs. HSG diagnostic agreement study (2025)

fichas.texto: WHO 6th ed. minimum values: volume≥1.4mL, concentration≥16M/mL, progressive motility≥30%, morphology≥4%. TMSC: >3-5M → IUI · 1-3M → IVF · <1M → direct ICSI.
fichas.fuentes: WHO Semen Manual (6th ed., 2021) · ASRM/ESHRE

fichas.texto: Basic labs + serologies + Pap/mammogram as appropriate. Folic acid: standard 400mcg/day · high risk 4-5mg/day (prior NTD, diabetes, obesity, anticonvulsants). MTHFR: replace with methylfolate (400-800mcg standard, up to 5000mcg high risk). Paraguay context (MSPyBS): the official public health communication from Paraguay's Ministry of Public Health and Welfare (MSPyBS) recommends 0.5mg (500mcg)/day as the standard preconception/gestational folic acid dose — slightly higher than the international 400mcg standard cited above, without changing the high-risk dose (4-5mg/day) in the risk scenarios already described. The MSPyBS Manual de Cuidados Perinatales (Resolución S.G. N.º 1078/2022, already cited elsewhere in this guide section for the PBF re-evaluation window) structures the preconception visit as "traffic-light" (semáforo), i.e. tiered by risk level — confirmed that this scheme exists in the official document. ⚠️ What could not be verified in this round is the specific detail of the risk/dose cutoffs for folic acid within that traffic-light scheme (beyond the binary standard/high-risk scheme already described above) — reviewing that specific section of the Manual remains pending before reproducing the exact 3 tiers.
fichas.fuentes: USPSTF (2023) · ACOG CO 762 (2019)

fichas.texto: Careful history/exam to choose studies. Essential female evaluation in parallel. Counseling on tobacco+STIs. Document outcomes. Psychosocial support.
fichas.fuentes: WHO Guideline (2025) — WHO's first guideline on the subject

fichas.texto: Unexplained infertility: a complete work-up with normal female and male factors (ovulation, ovarian reserve, tubal patency, uterine cavity, semen analysis) with no identifiable cause, after ≥12 months of trying (or 6 months if ≥35 years). Stress and unexplained infertility: recent evidence shows an association (not proven causation) between psychological distress measured by validated scales and unexplained infertility — but not with single-time endocrine stress markers (e.g., isolated cortisol), suggesting a phenomenon more complex than a simply hyperactivated HPA axis measurable in one sample. Clinical implication: psychological support can be offered as an adjunct (well-being/treatment adherence), but it does not replace or delay the standard diagnostic-therapeutic algorithm (ovulation induction, IUI, IVF as appropriate).
fichas.fuentes: ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023) · Prospective case-control study, Frontiers in Endocrinology (2025)

fichas.titulo: Ovulation induction — Therapeutic choice: Letrozole vs. Clomiphene vs. Gonadotropins
fichas.texto: Letrozole (aromatase inhibitor) — first-line in PCOS/WHO Type II anovulation, especially with overweight/obesity (BMI≥25-30). Higher cumulative ovulation, clinical pregnancy and live-birth rates than clomiphene (PPCOS II trial). Does not block endometrial or cervical estrogen receptors (preserves endometrial thickness and cervical mucus quality). Short half-life (~48h): favors monofollicular development, lower multiple-pregnancy rate. Clomiphene citrate (SERM): first-line alternative when letrozole is unavailable/not tolerated, or in unexplained infertility (timed intercourse/IUI). Drawback: prolonged peripheral antiestrogenic effect (half-life >2 weeks) — refractory thin endometrium (<7mm) and hostile mucus; higher multifollicular/multiple-pregnancy rate (5-10%, mostly twins) than letrozole. Exogenous gonadotropins (recombinant FSH / hMG): failure or resistance to oral agents (after 3-6 ovulatory cycles without conception); or Hypogonadotropic Hypogonadism (WHO Type I — hypothalamic-pituitary axis not intact, clomiphene/letrozole do NOT work, requires hMG or FSH+hCG/LH microdose); or as an adjunct in low-complexity/IUI cycles.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · Teede et al., Int'l PCOS Guideline (2023), Fertil Steril 120(4):767-793 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025

fichas.titulo: Ovulation induction — Dosing regimens and stimulation protocols
fichas.texto: Letrozole: 2.5mg/day PO x5 days, starting cycle day 2-5. If no ovulation, escalate to 5.0mg/day the next cycle; maximum dose 7.5mg/day x5 days. Clomiphene citrate: 50mg/day PO x5 days, day 2-5. If no response, increase to 100mg/day; usual maximum 150mg/day x5 days (higher doses do not improve pregnancy rates and worsen the endometrial antiestrogenic effect). Limit: 6 ovulatory cycles. Gonadotropins — "Low-Dose Step-Up" protocol: strict goal of monofollicular development and OHSS prevention. Starting dose 37.5-50-75 IU/day SC/IM from cycle day 2-3, holding the fixed dose for 7-14 days. If after 14 days there is no follicular selection (no follicle ≥10mm), increase 50% weekly (e.g. 37.5→75 IU/day) until a response is seen, then maintain that dose through the trigger.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · MSPyBS Paraguay (2025), Res. S.G. Nº 050/2025

fichas.titulo: Ovulation induction — Baseline and serial ultrasound monitoring
fichas.texto: Baseline transvaginal ultrasound + Antral Follicle Count (AFC), cycle days 2-4 — mandatory before starting any inducing agent: thin, shed endometrium (<5mm); rule out functional cysts/persistent follicles from the previous cycle (start if no follicles/cysts >10mm; postpone/cancel if a residual cyst or growing follicle ≥10-15mm is found, usually with baseline E2 >50-60pg/mL). AFC (bilateral 2-9mm follicles): <5-7 suggests low ovarian reserve · 8-15 normal reserve · ≥20 (or ovarian volume ≥10mL) polycystic ovarian morphology — maximum alert for hyperresponse and OHSS risk. Serial follow-up: first post-stimulation scan on cycle day 8-10, then every 48-72h depending on follicular growth rate (expected physiologic growth 1.5-2mm/day). Record the mean diameter in 2 perpendicular planes per ovary, and endometrial thickness/pattern (optimal: periovulatory trilaminar "triple line" ≥7-8mm).
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034

fichas.titulo: Ovulation induction — Follicular size for the hCG trigger
fichas.texto: The hCG trigger mimics the endogenous LH surge: it resumes oocyte meiosis, luteinizes the granulosa cells, and times follicular rupture (36-40h after administration). Trigger agents: Recombinant hCG (r-hCG) 250mcg SC · urinary hCG (u-hCG) 5,000-10,000 IU IM. Follicular size by inducing agent: Clomiphene citrate: trigger when the dominant follicle reaches a mean diameter of 18-20mm (tolerated up to 21-22mm — follicles under clomiphene tend to mature at slightly larger diameters). Letrozole: trigger with the leading follicle at 18-20mm. Gonadotropins (FSH/hMG): trigger with the leading follicle at 16-18mm (oocyte maturity is reached at slightly smaller sizes under direct gonadotropins; triggering above 19-20mm increases oocyte senescence). Concurrent endometrial status: ideally ≥7mm with a trilaminar pattern before ordering the trigger. Timing of intercourse/insemination: timed intercourse — the night of the trigger and again 36h later (or on alternating days: trigger day and the next). IUI — sperm preparation and insemination at 36h (range 34-38h) post-hCG.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282 · ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034

fichas.titulo: Ovulation induction — Cancellation criteria and OHSS prevention
fichas.texto: In low-complexity techniques (timed intercourse/IUI), the safety threshold requires strictly avoiding high-order multiple pregnancy and Ovarian Hyperstimulation Syndrome (OHSS). Immediate cancellation criteria — do NOT give hCG: ≥3 mature follicles (≥15-16mm) in women <35 years, or >3-4 mature follicles in any low-complexity patient. More than 4-6 intermediate follicles (11-14mm) that could respond to the trigger. Serum estradiol >1,000-1,500pg/mL (if measured). Management on cancellation: cancel and withhold the hCG trigger (it is the direct trigger for the VEGF cascade and capillary hyperpermeability of OHSS). Advise strict coital abstinence or mandatory condom use for ≥7-10 days. Do not give hCG for luteal support. Rescue option at a high-complexity center: convert the cycle to IVF with follicular aspiration, GnRH-agonist trigger, and total embryo cryopreservation ("freeze-all").
fichas.fuentes: ESHRE Female Infertility Guideline (2023), Hum Reprod Open 2023(3):hoad034 · ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282

fichas.titulo: Ovulation induction — Treatment failure and drug resistance
fichas.texto: Drug resistance: persistent absence of recruitment, or no follicles ≥15mm despite maximum doses. Clomiphene resistance: anovulation after 150mg/day x5 days. Letrozole resistance: anovulation after 7.5mg/day x5 days. Management: switch therapeutic line (CC→Letrozole, add Metformin in PCOS with insulin resistance, or move to low-dose gonadotropins). Failed induction (treatment failure): confirmed regular ovulatory cycles (optimal follicular development, follicular rupture and adequate luteal phase with progesterone ≥10ng/mL) without pregnancy after 4-6 consecutive ovulatory cycles. Management: full couple re-evaluation (tubal patency by HSG if not yet done, repeat semen analysis with TMSC) and escalation to high-complexity ART (IVF/ICSI). Endometrial failure (antiestrogenic effect): adequate follicular growth but persistently thin endometrium (<6-7mm) in the preovulatory window (common with clomiphene). Management: switch to letrozole or add exogenous estrogen support.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2020), Fertil Steril 113(2):274-282

fichas.titulo: Natural timed intercourse — Calendar, ovulation tests and cervical mucus
fichas.texto: Calendar: ovulation≈N-14, window N-18 to N-11. LH test: start 3-4 days before, ovulation 24-36h post-positive. Billings method: elastic/clear mucus near ovulation, peak day ≈13-14.
fichas.fuentes: ASRM Practice Committee (2020) · ESHRE PCOS (2023)

fichas.texto: Normal PRL <20-25. Micro <10mm (50-150) · Macro ≥10mm (>200-250). Dx: morning serum level, rule out macroprolactin/hook effect, MRI if PRL>100. Tx: Cabergoline (1st line) 0.25-1.0mg/week · Bromocriptine (if seeking pregnancy) 2.5-7.5mg/day.
fichas.fuentes: Endocrine Society (Melmed et al., 2011) · Vilar et al. (2019)

fichas.titulo: Cervicovaginal microbiota — CST profiles (Community State Types)
fichas.texto: Ravel classification: CST I (L. crispatus, optimal) · CST II (L. gasseri, protective) · CST III (L. iners, transitional/vulnerable) · CST IV (polymicrobial dysbiosis/vaginosis, pH>4.5) · CST V (L. jensenii, protective).
fichas.fuentes: Ravel J, et al. PNAS (2011)

fichas.titulo: Microbiota, cervical stroma and carcinogenesis — Impact on HPV/cervical cancer
fichas.texto: Mechanism: dysbiosis degrades mucin → TLR-4 inflammation (IL-1β/6/8, TNF-α) → MMP-2/9 → facilitates HPV entry and delays clearance → accelerates LSIL→HSIL→cancer. Biomarkers: ↑Sneathia/Fusobacterium, ↓D-lactic/L-lactic acid ratio.
fichas.fuentes: Mitra A, et al. Lancet Oncology (2016/2021)

fichas.titulo: Microbiota and stroma — Impact on fertility, implantation and management
fichas.texto: Dysbiosis alters cervical mucus and causes chronic endometritis (αvβ3 integrins). Implantation failure/recurrent miscarriage via Th1/Th17. Favorable marker: L. crispatus >90%. Management: Metronidazole/Clindamycin (CST IV) · topical lactic acid · probiotics (L. crispatus/gasseri) · pre-fertility work-up with culture/hysteroscopy+CD138.
fichas.fuentes: Moreno I, et al. AJOG (2016/2022)

fichas.titulo: Estrobolome — Definition and hepato-enteric axis of estrogens
fichas.texto: Gut bacteria with Beta-Glucuronidase/Glucosidase that deconjugate estrogens inactivated in the liver → reabsorption → circulation → ERα/ERβ receptors.
fichas.fuentes: Baker JM, et al. Maturitas (2017) · Ervin SM, et al. Acta Pharm Sinica B (2019)

fichas.texto: Hyperactivity (Bacteroides, Clostridium, E.coli) → hyperestrogenism → endometriosis, fibroids, endometrial hyperplasia/cancer, breast cancer risk, PCOS. Hypoactivity (antibiotics, ultra-processed diet) → hypoestrogenism → worse climacteric symptoms, bone mineral density loss, infertility from implantation failure.
fichas.fuentes: Kwa M, et al. J Natl Cancer Inst (2016)

fichas.texto: Nutrition: fiber 25-30g/day, cruciferous vegetables (DIM), ↓alcohol/saturated fat. Supplementation: Calcium D-Glucarate 500-1,500mg/day (hyperestrogenism) · probiotics (L. acidophilus/rhamnosus, Bifidobacterium) · prebiotics (inulin, FOS, GOS).
fichas.fuentes: Baker JM et al. (2017) · Ervin SM et al. (2019)

fichas.texto: Healthy woman, BMI 18.5-24.9, BP<120/80, normal history, normal labs/serologies/Pap, complete vaccination. Folic acid 0.4-0.5mg/day from ≥3 months preconception. Education (diet, exercise, cessation of toxic exposures). Fit to attempt pregnancy.
fichas.fuentes: Preconception fitness traffic-light system

fichas.texto: Underweight/overweight/class I obesity, treatable infections, mild-moderate anemia, rubella/Hep B seronegativity, interpregnancy interval<18-24mo. Temporary contraception + correction of the cause + immunization (⚠️ live vaccine → delay ≥4 weeks). Reassess in 3-6 months.
fichas.fuentes: Preconception fitness traffic-light system

fichas.texto: Pregestational DM with HbA1c>7%, severe chronic hypertension, heart disease, CKD, active SLE, uncontrolled epilepsy, HIV with detectable viral load, history of NTD/severe preeclampsia/recurrent loss, active teratogenic drugs. Immediate LARC contraception + mandatory referral + replacement of teratogenic drugs. Clearance only after ≥6 months of stability.
fichas.fuentes: Preconception fitness traffic-light system

fichas.texto: Pap at 1st/2nd prenatal visit. <30: Pap only. ≥30: co-testing/primary HPV. Colposcopy only if high-risk HPV+ or abnormal Pap.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS Paraguay 2024 · PAHO/WHO

fichas.texto: Not during pregnancy, yes during preconception. Average risk: from age 40. Family history: 30-35. BRCA+: 25-30.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 179 (2024)

fichas.titulo: Cervical cancer — Screening and management algorithm (ASCCP)
fichas.texto: Age: <21 no screening · 21-29 Pap/3years · 30-65 high-risk HPV/5years (preferred) · >65 stop if adequate prior screening. Pap: ASC-US→HPV triage · LSIL→colposcopy · ASC-H→mandatory colposcopy · HSIL→colposcopy+biopsy · AGC→+endocervical curettage.
fichas.fuentes: 2019 ASCCP Consensus (Perkins et al., 2020)

fichas.texto: I confined to the cervix (IA<5mm, IB visible) · II upper vagina/parametria · III lower vagina/pelvic wall/nodes · IV bladder/rectal/metastasis.
fichas.fuentes: Bhatla et al., FIGO Guidelines (2021)

fichas.titulo: HPV vaccination — Paraguay PAI schedule and WHO/SAGE corroboration
fichas.texto: Group 1 — Girls and boys aged 9 to 14 (routine schedule): 1 dose, administered at first contact. Group 2 — Women aged 15 to 24 with no vaccination history (catch-up schedule): ages 15-20 → 1 dose at first contact. Ages 21-24 → 2 doses (at contact and at 6 months, minimum interval of 6 months). Group 3 — People aged 15 to 45 with risk criteria (includes men and women except item 5): HIV: 3 doses — at contact, at 1 month and at 6 months after the first dose. Solid-organ or hematopoietic-component transplant recipients: 3 doses — same schedule (0-1-6 months). Immunosuppressive treatment: 3 doses — at 6 months after the first dose, per the PAI schedule. Survivors of sexual abuse: 2 doses — at contact and at 6 months after the first dose. Women with cervical pathology (carriers of high-risk oncogenic HPV by HPV testing, or diagnosed with CIN 1/CIN 2 by Pap smear or biopsy): 3 doses (at contact, 1 month and 6 months) — preferably before conization/LEEP; if not possible, up to 1 year after excisional treatment. The vaccine is free and available at health services (USF) under the Paraguay PAI schedule. Recording the dose in the vaccination card is recommended. WHO/SAGE corroboration (December 2022): the SAGE position endorses 1-dose schedules for the general population aged 9-20 (non-inferior efficacy vs. 2 doses in compared immunogenicity trials), and maintains a 2-3 dose schedule for immunocompromised individuals (including HIV) — consistent with the 3-dose reinforcement that the Paraguayan schedule maintains for the Group 3 risk categories. There is no contradiction between the two sources; the PAI schedule is, if anything, more conservative (2 doses at ages 21-24) than the minimum SAGE allows.
fichas.fuentes: MSPyBS/PAI Paraguay. HPV vaccine — official material from the Expanded Program on Immunization · WHO SAGE. Human papillomavirus vaccines: WHO position paper, December 2022, Wkly Epidemiol Rec

fichas.titulo: Ovarian tumor — IOTA rules and O-RADS system
fichas.texto: IOTA: B rules (benign) vs. M rules (malignant) — only B=benign, only M=malignant, both/neither=indeterminate. O-RADS: 1 physiological (0%) · 2 almost certainly benign (<1%) · 3 low risk (1-<10%) · 4 intermediate (10-<50%) · 5 high (≥50%, mandatory referral). Markers: CA-125, HE4 (more specific), ROMA index.
fichas.fuentes: ACR O-RADS (Andreotti et al., 2020) · IOTA (Timmerman et al., 2008/2016) · ESGO/ISUOG Consensus (2021)

fichas.texto: Categories: NILM (negative) · Squamous: ASC-US, ASC-H, LSIL (CIN1), HSIL (CIN2/3), invasive carcinoma · Glandular: AGC, AGC favor neoplasia, AIS, invasive adenocarcinoma.
fichas.fuentes: Nayar R, Wilbur DC (3rd ed., 2015)

fichas.texto: TZ: Type 1 fully visible ectocervical · Type 2 visible endocervical component · Type 3 not fully visible. Abnormal: Grade 1 (thin acetowhite, fine mosaic/punctation) · Grade 2 (dense acetowhite, rag sign/inner border/ridge sign) · Suspect invasion (atypical vessels, mass, necrosis). Triad: Pap (cytological) → Colposcopy (topographic) → Biopsy (histopathological).
fichas.fuentes: Bornstein J, et al. (2012) · ACOG PB 224 (2020)

fichas.titulo: ASCCP algorithms — Risk-based principle and management by cytology
fichas.texto: HSIL/CIN3 risk: <0.55% routine · 0.55-4% co-test in 1 year · 4-24% colposcopy · 25-59% colposcopy or immediate treatment · ≥60% direct immediate treatment. By result: NILM+HPV16/18→colposcopy · ASC-US+HPV(+)→colposcopy · LSIL≥25yo→colposcopy · ASC-H→colposcopy always · HSIL≥25yo→excision/biopsy · AGC→colposcopy+mandatory endocervical curettage.
fichas.fuentes: Perkins RB, et al. J Lower Genital Tract Disease (2020) · ACOG (2021)

fichas.titulo: ASCCP algorithms — Management by biopsy (CIN 1, CIN 2/3)
fichas.texto: CIN 1: observation, co-test at 12 months. No routine LEEP unless persistent >2 years. CIN 2/3: excision (LEEP/conization) or destructive (TZ1 only). Conservative exception: selected young patients, p16-negative CIN2, follow-up every 6mo up to 24mo.
fichas.fuentes: Perkins RB, et al. (2020)

fichas.texto: Test of cure (HPV/co-test) at 6 months. Negative → annual x3 years, then every 3 years, minimum age 25 (even >65 years). Positive → immediate colposcopic re-evaluation.
fichas.fuentes: Perkins RB, et al. (2020)

fichas.titulo: Mammography and BI-RADS — Breast density and categories 0-3
fichas.texto: Complementary ultrasound: dense breasts (ACR c/d), <30-35 years with a palpable mass, differentiate cyst/solid. Density (ACR): a (fatty) · b (scattered) · c (heterogeneously dense, consider ultrasound) · d (extremely dense, ultrasound indicated). BI-RADS: 0 incomplete · 1 negative (0%, routine) · 2 benign (0%, routine) · 3 probably benign (>0-≤2%, 6/12/24mo follow-up).
fichas.fuentes: ACR BI-RADS Atlas 5th ed. · ACOG PB 223/179 · USPSTF 2024 · NCCN 2023

fichas.titulo: Mammography and BI-RADS — Categories 4-6 and management
fichas.texto: BI-RADS 4 (>2-<95%, biopsy mandatory): 4a (>2-≤10%) · 4b (>10-≤50%) · 4c (>50-<95%). BI-RADS 5 (≥95%): spiculated mass, branching pleomorphic microcalcifications → immediate biopsy + oncology. BI-RADS 6: previously proven malignancy → definitive treatment.
fichas.fuentes: ACR BI-RADS Atlas 5th ed. · ACOG PB 223

fichas.titulo: Thickened endometrium — Management in reproductive-age women
fichas.texto: Values by phase: proliferative 4-8mm, periovulatory 8-12mm, secretory up to 14-16mm. AUB ≥45yo: biopsy mandatory. <45yo without risk factors: progestins/OCPs. With risk factors or failure: biopsy.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG PB 128 · ACOG CO 557

fichas.texto: With PMB: ≤4mm expectant · >4mm biopsy mandatory. Asymptomatic: ≤11mm no routine biopsy · >11mm individualize. Continuous HRT target ≤4-5mm.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG CO 734 · SOGC 249/390

fichas.texto: Almost always functional (anovulation). Transabdominal ultrasound. Biopsy/curettage contraindicated as 1st line. Progestins in the 2nd half of the cycle. Rule out coagulopathies if bleeding since menarche.
fichas.fuentes: ACOG · RCOG/BSGE 67

fichas.titulo: IETA classification — Endometrial thickness and echogenicity
fichas.texto: Measurement: sagittal plane, double layer. Echogenicity: uniform (trilaminar/hyperechogenic) vs. non-uniform (suggestive of pathology). Endometrial-myometrial interface regular vs. irregular (suspicious for invasion).
fichas.fuentes: Leone FP, et al. IETA Consensus (2010)

fichas.texto: Color Score 1-4. Single dominant vessel → polyp. Multiple disorganized vessels → malignancy. Scattered vessels without a dominant one → hyperplasia.
fichas.fuentes: Epstein E et al. (2018) · Van den Bosch T et al. (2021)

fichas.texto: PPH (operational definition): blood loss ≥300 mL with any abnormal hemodynamic sign (HR>100, shock index>1, SBP<100, DBP<60), or blood loss ≥500 mL — whichever occurs first, within 24 h postpartum. Enhanced surveillance during the first 2 h. Massive hemorrhage: loss/replacement of 50% of blood volume in 3 h, OR ≥150 mL/min, OR ≥1.5 mL/kg/20 min, OR ≥4 units in 24 h. Activation rule: meet the PPH criterion (≥300 mL with any abnormal sign, or ≥500 mL) or any sign of shock → initiate MOTIVE and ACTIVATE CODE RED. Maternal decompensation signs carry more weight than blood loss volume. Definition Criterion Status WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025 (rec. 22) ≥300 mL measured + HR >100, SI >1, SBP <100, or DBP <60; or ≥500 mL measured. All modes of delivery, within 24 h, enhanced surveillance during the first 2 h Current — used by the calculator reVITALize / ACOG PB 183 (2017) ≥1000 mL cumulative, or blood loss with signs or symptoms of hypovolemia, within 24 h (any mode of delivery) Variant Classic (WHO 2012 and traditional texts) ≥500 mL in vaginal delivery; ≥1000 mL in cesarean delivery No longer current The WHO 2025 applies the same criterion to cesarean delivery and warns against normalizing greater blood loss with this route. Always measure objectively (calibrated drape or weighing). Source: WHO/FIGO/ICM, Consolidated guidelines on PPH, 2025. Before and now — why it is no longer 500 or 1000 mL Before (classic definition, no longer current) Now (WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025) Definition ≥500 mL in vaginal delivery; ≥1000 mL in cesarean delivery ≥300 mL with any abnormal sign, or ≥500 mL, for all modes of delivery Activation Code Red with >1000 mL and/or signs of shock When criteria are met: initiate MOTIVE and activate Code Red Measurement Visual estimation, which underestimates blood loss Objective measurement: calibrated drape or weighing What matters more Volume The sign of maternal decompensation (HR >100, SI >1, SBP <100, DBP <60) Why it changed: with high thresholds and visual estimation, diagnosis was delayed. Objective measurement and action at the first sign of decompensation allow treatment to begin earlier. For cesarean delivery, the WHO advises against normalizing greater blood loss. Source: WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025, recommendation 22 and observations. Shock index (HR/SBP): >0.9 marker of severity; ≥1.4 urgent need for intervention; ≥1.7 high probability of an adverse outcome.

Important: Vélez grades shock severity; it does not define hemorrhage. For activation, use WHO 2025: 300 mL with any abnormal sign is already postpartum hemorrhage, even if Vélez classifies it as compensated (500-1000 mL). Team: Coordinator, Assistant 1, Assistant 2, Circulator (roles defined, Colombia Ministry of Health CPG 2013).

fichas.texto: Active management of the 3rd/4th stage (6 steps, WHO 2025): 1. Drying / initial assessment 2. Uterotonic (oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV, or carbetocin 100 µg if cold chain is unavailable, or misoprostol 400-600 µg orally) 3. Delayed cord clamping 1-3 min + skin-to-skin contact 4. Controlled cord traction + countertraction 5. Verify intact placenta + contracted uterus without massage 6. Monitoring every 15 min for 2 h Time zeroStabilize and decide 1-20 minDiagnose and treat the cause (4T's) 20-60 minImprovement? Level II-III? 60 minLevel III and conditions? Resuscitation targets: normal mental status, capillary refill <3 s, SBP>90, SpO2≥95%, shock index<0.9, T°>35°C, lactate<2 mmol/L, fibrinogen>200 mg/dL.

fichas.titulo: Obstetric Early Warning Scale: EAPO 2025/2022, MAMÁ Score and CaVeSal® Alert
fichas.texto: For every patient on admission and at each assessment. EAPO is not a score: each parameter has a color and a single red activates the obstetric emergency, which is then directed to the code according to the cause (hemorrhage → Code Red · hypertension → HDP · infection → Code Yellow — Sepsis · cardiac arrest → Obstetric Code Blue). EAPO MSPBS 2025/2022: parameters by color Parameter Red Yellow Green RR (breaths/min) ≥22 · ≤11 20-21 12-19 SpO₂ (%) <95 — 95-100 Temperature (°C) ≥39 · ≤35 38 36-37 HR (bpm) ≥100 · ≤59 — 60-99 SBP (mmHg) ≥160 · ≤70 140-159* · 71-99 100-139 DBP (mmHg) ≥110 · 51-59 90-109 60-89 Neurological Only responds to pain · unconscious Disoriented Alert Appearance Pale · cyanotic · jaundiced Diaphoretic Normal Urine output No urine output in 6 h or >30 mL/h — Yes Proteinuria (dipstick) +++ or more — + / ++ Genital bleeding Heavy Spotting Absent Purulent discharge · headache with visual or auditory disturbance · seizures Yes — No Abdominal pain With peritoneal irritation Without irritation No * Note: the 2025 sheet is used, and gaps are supplemented with the 2022 version (the 2025 sheet does not include the SBP 140-159 row). fichas.texto: TXA: 1 g IV over 10 min (1 mL/min), second dose of 1 g if bleeding continues at 30 min or recurs within 24 h. DO NOT use more than 3 h after birth. Heat-stable carbetocin: ONLY for prevention when the cold chain fails — NOT for treatment of established uterine atony. 4 Ts (causes): Tone 70% (atony), Trauma 20% (lacerations), Tissue 10% (retained products), Thrombin 1% (coagulopathy). E-MOTIVE: Early detection, uterine Massage, Oxytocics, Tranexamic acid, IV fluids, physical Examination and escalation.

fichas.titulo: Tranexamic acid: from WOMAN to the present
fichas.texto: Key message: TXA is treatment for diagnosed postpartum hemorrhage, given as soon as possible and always within 3 h of birth. The sooner it is given, the greater the benefit: most deaths from PPH occur within the first 2-3 h. It is not used for routine prophylaxis (WHO 2025, recommendations 14 and 15, new). Trials of tranexamic acid in postpartum hemorrhage Trial Population Primary outcome What changed WOMAN 2017 20,060 women with established PPH, 21 countries Death from bleeding 1.5 % vs 1.9 % (RR 0.81; CI 0.65-1.00). Within 3 h: 1.2 % vs 1.7 % (RR 0.69; CI 0.52-0.91). No reduction in hysterectomy. No increase in thrombosis TXA becomes standard treatment when given early TRAAP 2018 4,079, vaginal birth, prophylaxis PPH ≥500 mL 8.1 % vs 9.8 % (RR 0.83; CI 0.68-1.01), not significant Does not support routine prophylaxis for vaginal birth TRAAP2 2021 4,551, cesarean, prophylaxis Calculated blood loss >1000 mL or transfusion 26.7% vs 31.6% (adjusted RR 0.84; CI 0.75-0.94); no differences in secondary clinical outcomes Less measured blood loss, no clear clinical benefit MFMU 2023 11,000 cesarean deliveries, 31 hospitals in the US Death or transfusion 3.6% vs 4.3% (adjusted RR 0.89; CI 0.74-1.07) Does not support prophylaxis at cesarean delivery WOMAN-2 2024 15,068 women with moderate or severe anemia, vaginal birth Clinical PPH 7.0% vs 6.6% (RR 1.05; CI 0.94-1.19). No thromboembolic events Prophylaxis does not prevent PPH even in women with anemia IPD meta-analysis 2024 54,404 women, 5 trials Life-threatening bleeding 0.65% vs 0.85% (OR 0.77; CI 0.63-0.93), with no increase in thrombosis Small and safe benefit; still does not change the WHO recommendation Administration: 1 g (ampoule 100 mg/mL, 10 mL) IV at 1 mL/min, i.e., over 10 min. Avoid rapid bolus: it may cause hypotension. A second dose of 1 g if bleeding continues at 30 min or recurs within 24 h of the first dose. Safety: IV route only; never intrathecal or epidural (documented wrong-route error causing seizures and death). No trial showed an increase in thromboembolic events. Beyond 3 h: no benefit and the estimate points toward harm; the WHO does not recommend it after this time.

fichas.texto: Tone (70%) — atony: oxytocin 5 U IV over 3 min + infusion 30 U/500 cc at 125 cc/h, methylergonovine, TXA, uterine massage, bimanual compression, balloon. Trauma (20%) — lacerations: inspect the birth canal, repair, TXA. Tissue (10%) — retained tissue: inspect the uterine cavity, remove retained tissue/placenta, TXA. Thrombin (1%) — coagulopathy: coagulation tests, manual clot formation test in a tube for 7 min, correct with plasma/cryoprecipitate/platelets. Control maneuvers: bimanual compression, external aortic compression, manual removal of the placenta, uterine inversion maneuver, hydrostatic balloon (Bakri), non-pneumatic anti-shock garment. Escalation of response: Level 0 = E-MOTIVE (early detection); Level 1 = TXA + bimanual uterine compression; Level 2 = 2nd-line pharmacologic agents + intrauterine balloon + transfusion; Level 3 = surgery (B-Lynch, Hayman, Cho sutures; O'Leary, Posadas, Tsirulnikov or hypogastric artery ligations; hysterectomy). The Zea technique (vaginal clamping of the uterine arteries) serves as a bridge, and arterial embolization is an option in the stable patient.

fichas.titulo: Perineal tears — classification and repair (RCOG GTG 29)
fichas.texto: Sultan classification (RCOG 2015) Grade Structures involved 1 Perineal skin and/or vaginal mucosa 2 Perineal muscles, without involving the anal sphincter 3a <50% of the external anal sphincter (EAS) thickness 3b >50% of the EAS thickness 3c EAS and internal anal sphincter (IAS) 4 Anal sphincter (EAS + IAS) and anorectal mucosa If uncertain between 3a and 3b, classify as 3b (higher grade). A rectal buttonhole tear with an intact sphincter is not grade 4: repair it and document it separately. Systematic examination with digital rectal examination for every tear before repair. Grades 3-4: repair in the operating room under regional or general anesthesia, with good lighting and an assistant; if there is active bleeding, vaginal packing while transferring the patient. Full-thickness EAS tear: overlap or end-to-end technique; 3a / partial tear: end-to-end. IAS: separate end-to-end repair. Avoid figure-of-eight (hemostatic) sutures, which cause ischemia. Digital rectal examination at the end (to rule out transfixing sutures). Postoperative care: broad-spectrum antibiotics, laxatives; avoid suppositories and enemas; follow-up with pelvic floor physiotherapy (6-12 weeks). Grades 1-2: continuous layered repair with rapidly absorbing polyglactin 910. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: RCOG Green-top Guideline No. 29 (2015) · Sultan AH. fichas.titulo: Placental abruption with fetal death — mode of delivery and amniotomy
fichas.texto: Essential prerequisite: the mother must be hemodynamically stable (no shock or cardiovascular instability). If the mother is unstable → immediate cesarean delivery, regardless of whether the fetus is alive or dead (WHO). Amniotomy in this context: perform as early as possible (not delayed) — unlike the general rule of delayed amniotomy in the physiological partograph. Objectives: (1) reduce intrauterine pressure (decompress the retroplacental hematoma and potentially halt progressive separation), and (2) allow internal monitoring if vaginal birth is attempted. Guideline recommendations for fetal death + placental abruption (stable mother) Source Recommendation WHO Vaginal delivery (induction with misoprostol) if the mother is stable; cesarean delivery only in the event of maternal hemodynamic instability, regardless of fetal status. RCOG Green-top No. 63 Attempt vaginal delivery if the maternal condition is stable, with induction of labor. Cesarean delivery only for a maternal indication (uncontrolled hemorrhage, failed induction). MSF Guidelines Urgent uterine evacuation (vaginal delivery or cesarean delivery) regardless of gestational age; cesarean delivery becomes imperative if labor progresses very slowly, even in the event of fetal demise. PubMed (J Obstet Gynaecol Res, PMID 28370793) Case series of 16 patients: vaginal delivery was attempted in 15 and achieved in 14 (93.3%). Feasible and safe following fetal demise due to placental abruption, regardless of gestational age, parity, cervical maturity, or duration of labor, when intensive medical resources are available. Why vaginal delivery is preferred in this scenario: severe placental abruption with fetal demise is frequently associated with consumptive disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)—cesarean delivery in a coagulopathic patient increases the risk of intraoperative hemorrhage due to atony/coagulopathy and peripartum hysterectomy. Vaginal delivery avoids a surgical wound in the presence of a coagulation disorder. Management protocol: Maternal stabilization: two large-bore IV lines (16-18G), Ringer's lactate, consider type and crossmatch, fibrinogen/PT/aPTT/platelet count. Activate the massive obstetric hemorrhage protocol if bleeding is heavy. Early amniotomy to decompress the uterus and allow internal monitoring. Labor induction: oral or vaginal misoprostol (WHO recommendation for fetal demise/anomaly in the 3rd trimester) + oxytocin if needed. Monitor progress: if labor progresses very slowly despite induction, cesarean delivery becomes imperative even in the event of fetal demise. There is no fixed time limit as long as maternal-fetal monitoring shows no progression of the placental abruption. Correction of coagulopathy if cesarean delivery is required: thrombocytopenia <50,000/µL or hypofibrinogenemia <100-200 mg/dL with cryoprecipitate/platelets/fresh frozen plasma before or during surgery. Postpartum: monitor for PPH and residual coagulopathy; emotional support and bereavement care. Absolute contraindications to vaginal delivery: uncontrolled hemorrhage, placental abruption with maternal hemodynamic instability, suspected uterine rupture, classic obstetric indication for cesarean delivery (placenta previa, vasa previa). General note on amniotomy (WHO): amniotomy alone is not recommended as the sole method of labor induction (moderate-quality evidence, weak recommendation)—it is considered only when prostaglandins and oxytocin are unavailable. This is the only documented exception for an emergency maternal hemorrhagic indication.

fichas.titulo: Prevention of Postpartum Hemorrhage — a three-moment framework
fichas.texto: Conceptual framework (Pregnancy → Childbirth → Postpartum): PPH results from accumulated factors across 6 categories—social determinants, maternal conditions/diseases, pregnancy factors, childbirth factors, placental factors, and health system factors (antenatal and intrapartum). The pathway to morbidity and mortality progresses as follows: normal/complicated birth → PPH → severe PPH → death/complications—with a specific intervention possible at each stage: preventive measures → early diagnosis → first-response treatment → treatment of refractory cases → post-PPH supportive care.

Correcting anemia antenatally reduces morbidity and mortality associated with blood loss during childbirth.

fichas.titulo: Massive Transfusion Protocol — two valid variants
fichas.texto: Activation: anticipated massive hemorrhage (replacement of ≥ 50% of blood volume in 2h) or active bleeding after 4 units of PRBCs in 1-2h. Blood component Effect per unit Indication / target Packed red blood cells (PRBCs) Increases hematocrit by 3-4% Based on estimated blood loss Fresh frozen plasma (FFP) Increases fibrinogen by +10mg/dL 15mL/kg or 1U/20kg; PT/aPTT>1.5× control Platelets Increases by 5,000-10,000/µL Target 50,000-100,000/µL Cryoprecipitate — 1-2mL/kg (threshold depends on variant — see below) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Pacheco LD et al. Am J Perinatol 2013;30:1-4 · WHO 2025 (PPH).

fichas.titulo: Variant A — Pacheco 2013 protocol (6 rounds, 100mg/dL threshold)
fichas.texto: Round PRBCs FFP Platelets Cryoprecipitate 1 6U 6U 6U 10U 2 6U 6U — 20U 3 Recombinant factor VIIa 40µg/kg — 4 6U 6U 6U 10U 5 6U 6U 10U — 6 Recombinant factor VIIa 40µg/kg — CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Pacheco LD, Saade GR, Costantine MM, Clark SL, Hankins GD. The Role of Massive Transfusion Protocols in Obstetrics. Am J Perinatol 2013;30(1):1-4. Cryoprecipitate threshold: fibrinogen <100 mg/dL. If bleeding is not controlled after round 6, restart from round 1.

fichas.titulo: Variant B — WHO 2025 protocol (no fixed round table, 200mg/dL threshold)
fichas.texto: Fibrinogen replacement threshold: <2 g/L (=200 mg/dL), target ≥ 2g/L. Typically 3-4g of fibrinogen ≈ 8-10 units of cryoprecipitate. No fixed round table — guided by ongoing clinical and laboratory assessment (unlike the rigid round-based Pacheco 2013 protocol). After the 2nd round/reassessment: administer tranexamic acid (TXA) 1g IV if not already administered.

fichas.titulo: Quantification of blood loss: calibrated drape and visual chart
fichas.texto: Operational recommendation: use a calibrated blood collection drape when available (an objective method recognized by WHO 2025); otherwise, use the visual equivalency chart. The chart supplements, but does not replace, objective measurement. Volumetric equivalents by pad/surface (Bose et al., BJOG 2006) Item Estimated volume Stained sanitary pad 30 mL Saturated sanitary pad 100 mL Soaked 10×10 cm gauze 60 mL Incontinence brief 250 mL 45×45 cm gauze pad 350 mL Full kidney dish (basin) 500 mL Spill on floor, 100 cm diameter 1000 mL PPH confined to the bed 1500 mL PPH with spill on the floor 2000 mL CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO 2025 · Bose et al., BJOG 2006. Calibrated drape (BRASSS-V drape): simple, low-cost, accurate, and objective; usable in a wide range of settings, with a hygienic surface for childbirth. In its trial, visual estimation underestimated actual blood loss by 33% compared with the calibrated drape (correlation with spectrophotometry 0.92).

PLoS ONE 2016;11(2):e0148729 · CC BY 4.0 License (use permitted with attribution). The shock index was evaluated as a predictor of three levels of adverse outcomes: death; severe outcome (death or severe organ dysfunction); and a composite of critical interventions (death, severe end-stage organ dysfunction, ICU admission, transfusion of ≥5 units of red blood cells, emergency hysterectomy).

fichas.titulo: Drugs and fluids in PPH: differences that matter (WHO 2025)
fichas.texto: Misoprostol: dose and route vary by indication Indication Dose and route WHO 2025 recommendation Prevention of PPH 400 or 600 µg ORAL Recommendation 7.3 — for all births Treatment of PPH (2nd line) 800 µg SUBLINGUAL Recommendation 25 — if IV oxytocin is unavailable or bleeding does not respond (with IV ergometrine or an oxytocin+ergometrine combination) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO 2025 (PPH) · FIGO 2022 · Zheng 2014 · Chen et al. 2013. Crystalloids over colloids (Recommendation 28): isotonic crystalloids are recommended over colloids for IV fluid resuscitation in PPH; this applies to the 500 mL boluses of warmed crystalloids in the first 20-minute flowchart. Reaffirmed by FIGO 2022 as part of the PPH care bundle. Controlled cord traction (Du, Ye & Zheng 2014): meta-analysis of 30,532 patients; reduces manual removal of the placenta (RR 0.70; 95% CI 0.58-0.84) with no difference in severe PPH (RR 0.94; 95% CI 0.88-1.01). Sustained uterine massage: not routinely recommended after prophylactic oxytocin (Chen et al., ACOG 2013); monitor uterine tone. Non-pneumatic anti-shock garment (NASG): a temporizing measure while transfer is underway or definitive treatment is being prepared (FIGO 2022, Escobar, Nassar, Theron et al.).

fichas.titulo: Balloon tamponade and uterine compression sutures
fichas.texto: Intrauterine balloon tamponade devices (same principle: hydrostatic pressure) Device Characteristic Bakri Obstetric-specific design; up to 500 mL Ellavi Less expensive; similar design to Bakri Condom + Foley/Nelaton catheter Low-cost adaptation for resource-limited settings Rusch catheter Adapted hydrostatic balloon Sengstaken-Blakemore Double balloon (gastric + esophageal); designed for esophageal varices and adapted for uterine tamponade Uterine compression sutures Technique Particularity B-Lynch Classic, “suspender” suture; requires open hysterotomy Hayman Simplified modification; does not require hysterotomy (uterus closed) Pereira Multiple transverse and vertical sutures; closed uterus Ho-Cho Multiple square sutures; particularly indicated for placenta accreta Uterine sandwich Simultaneous intrauterine balloon + external compression suture (B-Lynch + Bakri) Devascularization and vascular control Technique Particularity Zea (vaginal) Vaginal clamping of the uterine arteries with ring forceps in the lateral parametrium of the cervix; bridging measure while preparing the operating room or addressing the cause. Also useful before evacuating a cervical ectopic pregnancy O'Leary Bilateral ligation of the uterine arteries via laparotomy; first-line conservative surgical option Posadas Selective devascularization: posterior ligation of the uterine arteries and internal tubal arteries, without opening the broad ligament; 96.4% success in 750 cases Tsirulnikov Triple stepwise ligation: round ligaments, utero-ovarian ligaments, and uterine arteries Hypogastric arteries Internal iliac artery ligation; more complex (ureteral and venous risk), reserved for failure of the preceding procedures Arterial embolization Interventional radiology in a hemodynamically stable patient; fertility-preserving CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: INPer — Zea technique · IMSS Clinical Practice Guideline 162 · Ginecol Obstet Méx — Posadas technique · Series of 750 cases. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO 2021 · MSPBS Code Red 2022. Bakri: success rate 79.5-85.9% in systematic reviews; in a meta-analysis of 28 studies, 82% with balloon alone (95% CI 78-86%) and 95% with additional procedures. Lower success after cesarean delivery (69-78%) than after vaginal birth (90%). Sutures: no technique demonstrated clear superiority; efficacy ~75% after failure of medical treatment and ~80% as second-line treatment after failed vascular ligation; risk of synechiae 5-10%. Combined balloon + suture: success rate >91.7% in refractory PPH; avoids hysterectomy in up to 75% of cases that would otherwise require it. Condom/Foley balloon (improvised): WHO 2021 recommends its use only where other treatments, including immediate surgery, are already available. Assembly: 16-18 Foley catheter with the distal tip cut off, inserted into a condom, secured with silk about 5 fingers from the end (without obstructing the lumen); fill with 500 cc of 0.9% normal saline, with vaginal packing to prevent expulsion. In a comparative study of 12 patients (6 per group), the improvised balloon achieved 100% success (6/6), with no complications or associated surgeries, comparable to the SOS Bakri balloon, although time to hemostasis was slightly longer (6.8 vs. 4.6 min, not statistically significant). Source: Jiménez L, Veroes J, Vera M, Colmenares M, Di Muro J, Márquez D. Rev Obstet Ginecol Venez. 2020;80(3):227-235. Comparative reference; the surgical step-by-step is beyond the scope of a quick-reference guide. Included in the Code Red Level 2-3 escalation — in our setting (Paraguay), where Bakri/Ellavi are not always available, the improvised balloon is the usual and clinically equivalent option.

fichas.titulo: “Diamond of Death”: why calcium should be corrected during massive transfusion
fichas.texto: Evolution of the classic lethal triad (hypothermia, acidosis, coagulopathy) with a fourth vertex: hypocalcemia. All four components reinforce one another: each worsens the other three. Hypothermia ↔ Hypocalcemia ↔ Acidosis ↔ Coagulopathy. This is the pathophysiologic framework behind the practical recommendation to replace calcium IV during massive transfusion (see protocol, subcards 10-13). In PPH, low ionized calcium is associated with greater bleeding severity (Epstein et al., Br J Anaesth 2021).

fichas.titulo: Blood volume, allowable blood loss, and quantification of bleeding
fichas.texto: Estimated blood volume: 100 mL/kg in healthy pregnancy; 70 mL/kg in obesity or volume contraction (severe preeclampsia). Maximum allowable blood loss: (initial Hb − minimum Hb) × blood volume ÷ [(initial Hb + minimum Hb) × 0.5]. Usual minimum Hb 7 g/dL. Quantify, do not estimate by eye: 1 g = 1 mL. Wet weight − dry weight (pads, gauze, drapes) + suction volume − amniotic fluid − irrigation. Separate amniotic fluid before placental delivery (change the canister or record the volume). Express blood loss as a % of blood volume and compare it with the Vélez shock classification (subcard 2). Methods for estimating blood volume Method Use 100 / 70 mL/kg (SOGC 431) Used by the calculator “Rule of 30”: 100 mL/kg SA Health PPH 30–60% increase over nonpregnant blood volume Williams Obstetrics (Pritchard) Nonlinear formula by BMI (obese women have fewer mL/kg) Lancaster University, nonlinear proposal Nadler (height and weight, nonpregnant) Nadler, PubMed 30252333 CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: SOGC Guideline No. 431 (J Obstet Gynaecol Can 2022) · ACOG Committee Opinion No. 794 (2019).

fichas.titulo: Coagulopathy based on conventional laboratory tests: thresholds and DIC scores
fichas.texto: Replacement during ongoing PPH Laboratory Management Fibrinogen <2 g/L Cryoprecipitate, 2 pools (10 U) or fibrinogen concentrate Platelets <75,000 1 pool or apheresis; target >50,000 Prolonged PT / aPTT FFP 12–15 mL/kg; if >1.5× normal, more is usually required (TACO risk) No active bleeding Do not transfuse based on an isolated value; repeat Concentrate dose (mg/kg) = (target − measured, mg/dL) ÷ 1.7 (RiaSTAP FDA label). DIC scores available in the calculator Score Variables Cutoff ISTH 2025 (preferred) Platelets, D-dimer (>3× and >7× ULN), prolonged PT, fibrinogen ≥5 ISTH 2001 Same, with a qualitative “fibrin marker” ≥5 Erez 2014 (pregnancy) PT difference, platelets, fibrinogen ≥26 JSOG 2024 (obstetric) Baseline condition, fibrinogen, FDP or D-dimer ≥8 In pregnancy, normal fibrinogen levels are higher (3.5–6.5 g/L): a “normal” non-pregnant value may already be low. Therefore, obstetric scores give greater weight to fibrinogen. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: RCOG GTG 52, BJOG 2017;124:e106-49 · Collins P et al. fichas.titulo: ROTEM in obstetric hemorrhage: quick interpretation
fichas.texto: What to look at and what to do Parameter Finding Management FIBTEM A5 <12 mm with bleeding, or <7 mm Fibrinogen: g = target increase (mm) × weight ÷ 160 FIBTEM A5 >12 mm No fibrinogen required EXTEM CT >100 s with corrected FIBTEM FFP 15 mL/kg (or PCC according to protocol) EXTEM A5 <35 mm with FIBTEM at target Platelet component: confirm platelet count EXTEM ML >15 % Hyperfibrinolysis: tranexamic acid 1 g IV EXTEM reference: CT 38–79 s; ML <15 %. 10 units of cryoprecipitate ≈ 2 g of fibrinogen. Threshold variants: FIBTEM A5 >8 mm and EXTEM CT <75 s (All Wales PPH Guideline); EXTEM CT >80 s (Görlinger K et al. Korean J Anesthesiol 2019;72:297-322general algorithm). The calculator lets you choose. Repeat ROTEM 10–15 min after each intervention. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Curry NS et al. BSH 2018, Br J Haematol 2018;182:789-806 · Collins PW et al. fichas.texto: Pregnancy >20 weeks + 2 BP readings 15 min apart if severe (≥160/110) or 4 h apart if mild (140-159/90-109) + evidence of end-organ damage (clinical: headache, visual changes, right upper quadrant pain, pulmonary edema; laboratory: AST/ALT≥70, LDH≥600, platelets<100,000, bilirubin≥1.2) OR proteinuria (≥300 mg/24h, protein/creatinine ratio≥0.3, albumin/creatinine ratio≥0.8, dipstick≥2+) OR angiogenic tests sFlt1/PlGF>38. Proteinuria is NOT required for the diagnosis of severe preeclampsia. Prevention: calcium 1-2 g/day in all pregnant patients; aspirin 150 mg/day based on risk factors (1 high-risk factor or 2 moderate-risk factors).

fichas.texto: Code activation: SBP>160 or DBP>110 or eclamptic seizures. Team: Coordinator, Assistant, Circulating Nurse. Post-target monitoring: every 10 min for the 1st hour, every 15 min for the 2nd hour, every 30 min for the 3rd hour, every hour from the 4th hour for an additional 4 h. Sustained severe-range BP for >15 min = life-threatening emergency.

fichas.texto: SSSAO mnemonic: Support, Safety, magnesium sulfate (loading dose 4-6 g IV, maintenance 1-2 g/h until 24 h postpartum), Antihypertensives (reduce by 20-25% over 24-48 h, target 135/85 per NICE), Obstetric management (fetal maturation at 24-34 weeks, fetal well-being, delivery: non-severe PE at 37 weeks, severe PE at 34 weeks). Stepwise hypertensive emergency algorithm: IV labetalol 20→40 mg / oral nifedipine 10→20→20 mg / IV hydralazine 10 mg, reassessing every 10-20 min. Fluid management: no bolus, total 80 mL/h or 1 mL/kg/h, max 125 mL/h. Eclampsia: seizure control with a 4-6 g IV MgSO4 bolus (or 2 g IV if already receiving it), maintenance 2 g/h, second 2 g IV bolus if seizures recur. Intubate if: unconscious after seizure, status epilepticus, aspiration, hypoxia. Continue MgSO4 for at least 24 h postpartum or from the last seizure.

fichas.titulo: Expanded classification and additional severity criteria (ACOG PB 222 / FIGO / ISSHP)
fichas.texto: Chronic hypertension with superimposed preeclampsia: new-onset proteinuria, or sudden loss of blood pressure control, or end-organ dysfunction after 20 weeks of gestation in a patient with hypertension predating pregnancy. Additional severity criterion — Progressive renal insufficiency: serum creatinine >1.1 mg/dL or doubling of baseline creatinine (not previously included alongside LDH/bilirubin — added as an independent laboratory criterion). Urine output — alternative weight-based threshold: <0.5 mL/kg/h, as an alternative to the absolute threshold of <30 mL/h already used for MgSO4 toxicity monitoring.

fichas.texto: Nifedipine in hypertensive crisis: swallow with water; DO NOT administer sublingually. MgSO4 antidote: Calcium gluconate 10% 1g (10mL) slow IV. Two administration-rate options: 3-5 min (MSPBS/CaVeSal regimen) or 10 min (ACOG/WHO). Monitoring for MgSO4 toxicity: discontinue if RR <12 breaths/min; some guidelines use <12-16 breaths/min (CaVeSal regimen) and others <12-14 breaths/min (ACOG). Patellar reflex present and urine output ≥30 mL/h in all regimens.

fichas.texto: The Calculator uses the Pritchard/MSPBS regimen by default. The Zuspan IV regimen is the intravenous alternative and is preferred for neuroprotection; the University of Antioquia uses a larger dilution volume with the same total dose. Regimen Loading dose Maintenance Pritchard / MSPBS 14 g total: 10 g IM (5 g = 10 cc in each buttock) + 4 g IV (8 cc + 12 cc of NS in a 20 cc syringe, over 20 min) IV 1-2 g/h in a 100 cc Volutrol, or IM 5 g every 4 h, for 24 h Zuspan (IV) 4 g IV over 20-30 min 1-2 g/h IV for 24 h (preeclampsia); for neuroprotection, until delivery or for 12 h University of Antioquia Same total dose with a larger dilution volume (see source protocol) IM maintenance — how to administer (clarification to prevent underdosing): each dose is 5 g PER SCHEDULED DOSE (10 cc total). Option 1 (official text): 10 cc in one buttock, alternating buttocks at each scheduled dose. Option 2 (administration variant proposed by CaVeSal®): 5 cc (2.5 g) in each buttock at the same scheduled dose, repeated at the next scheduled dose (every 4 h). The frequent error is to administer a TOTAL of 5 cc per scheduled dose (2.5 g): the full dose is 10 cc (5 g). Typical sequence of toxicity: 1st, decreased urine output (<30 mL/h, risk of accumulation); 2nd, loss of the patellar reflex; 3rd, respiratory depression (RR <12-16 breaths/min). Rescue: calcium gluconate 10%, 1 g (10 cc) slow IV over 3-5 min, in the event of respiratory depression or instability (this is not gram-for-gram neutralization). The regimen may be repeated (repeat regimen) according to clinical course.
