fichas.titulo: HELLP syndrome: ACOG, Tennessee, and Mississippi criteria
fichas.texto: Comparison of the 3 diagnostic systems System Platelets Transaminases Hemolysis / LDH Use ACOG PB 222 (2020) <100.000/µL AST and ALT >2 times the upper limit of normal LDH ≥600 U/L Clinical diagnosis; no subdivision by class Tennessee (Sibai) <100.000/µL AST ≥70 U/L LDH ≥600 U/L (or bilirubin >1.2 mg/dL with abnormal smear: schistocytes) Complete HELLP = 3 criteria; partial = 1-2 criteria Mississippi — Class 1 (severe) ≤50.000/µL AST or ALT ≥70 U/L LDH ≥600 U/L Higher risk of DIC and hemorrhage Mississippi — Class 2 (moderate) >50.000 a ≤100.000/µL AST or ALT ≥70 U/L LDH ≥600 U/L Intermediate risk Mississippi — Class 3 (mild) >100.000 a ≤150.000/µL AST or ALT ≥40 U/L LDH ≥600 U/L Detects early forms not included in ACOG/Tennessee CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 (2020) · tabla Tennessee vs Mississippi (PMC2654858) · Clin Liver Dis 2019 (PMC6448736) · StatPearls, HELLP Syndrome. ACOG management: because of its morbidity and mortality, many authors recommend delivery in HELLP syndrome regardless of gestational age, after maternal stabilization. ACOG considers the evidence insufficient to use corticosteroids to attenuate the disease (they are used for fetal lung maturation according to gestational age). Neuraxial anesthesia (ACOG): acceptable with platelets ≥70,000/µL if the count is stable, there is no other coagulopathy, platelet function is normal, and the patient is not taking antiplatelet or anticoagulant agents (risk of epidural hematoma <0.2%). Practical difference: ACOG sets the <100,000/µL cutoff for diagnosis; Mississippi subdivides by platelet nadir to grade bleeding risk and guide transfusion planning. Correction of attribution: bilirubin >1.2 mg/dL and schistocytes belong to the Tennessee criteria (Sibai), not the diagnostic text of ACOG PB 222. In the Calculator the default criterion is Mississippi, with a selector for ACOG and Tennessee. Sources: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 222 (2020) · tabla Tennessee vs Mississippi (PMC2654858) · Clin Liver Dis 2019 (PMC6448736) · StatPearls, HELLP Syndrome.

fichas.texto: Interpretation (Roche Elecsys assay; cutoffs depend on the platform) Ratio <34 weeks ≥34 weeks Interpretation ≤38 Rules out Rules out Rules out PE in the following week (NPV >99%) 38-85 / 38-110 38-85 38-110 Intermediate zone: repeat in 1-2 weeks >85 / >110 >85 >110 High suspicion or diagnostic support for PE >655 / >201 >655 >201 Extreme angiogenic imbalance: high probability of delivery within 48 h CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Verlohren S et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol 2012;206(1):58.e1-8 (cited in PMC11012921) · Villalaín C et al. J Am Heart Assoc 2020;9:e015548 (ratio >655) · Sá CPN et al. Rev Bras Ginecol Obstet 2020;42(11). Spanish cohort, J Am Heart Assoc 2020 (237 pregnancies with a ratio >655, 20-37 weeks): median time to delivery was 4 days with established PE and 7 days without PE at the time of testing; 60.5% were still pregnant at 48 h with PE (compared with 29.4% in the original series, in which clinicians were blinded to the result). High frequency of FGR (85-90% at delivery) and severe features. Some authors propose >1000 as a better predictor of adverse perinatal outcome (Stolz et al.). The ratio quantifies the biological severity of placental and systemic disease; it does not replace clinical assessment when deciding timing of delivery. The Calculator replicates the logic of the CaVeSal prenatal calculator (≤38 / 85 or 110 depending on GA / >655). Sources: Verlohren S et al. fichas.texto: Key index: systolic peak ratio PSV2/PSV1 (peak ratio). In normal pregnancy it is usually <0.6; in PE, the second peak approaches or exceeds the first. UOG 2018;51(6):731-737 · Vaz de Melo PFM et al. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth 2023;23:343 · PMC12844109 review. fichas.titulo: sFlt-1/PlGF vs ophthalmic artery Doppler in established severe preeclampsia
fichas.texto: Complementary tools, not competitors Characteristic sFlt-1/PlGF ratio Ophthalmic artery Doppler Nature Biochemical marker of antiangiogenesis and placental dysfunction Functional hemodynamic measurement of the maternal orbital/cerebral vascular territory Strength Quantifies systemic/multiorgan damage and the severity of placental disease Reflects in real time the loss of maternal cerebral vascular autoregulation Use in established disease Helps estimate the urgency of delivery (values >655 associated with delivery within days) Warning sign in the presence of neurovisual symptoms; supports monitoring of neurological risk Limitation Cutoffs depend on the platform; availability and cost Operator-dependent; no universal cutoffs; limited evidence for eclampsia CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG PB 222 (2020) · FIGO 2019 · ISSHP 2021 · Kalafat E et al. UOG 2018. In summary: the ratio quantifies overall biological severity; ophthalmic artery Doppler measures the immediate hemodynamic impact on the maternal cerebral microvasculature. Neither replaces clinical criteria for severe features (BP, symptoms, laboratory findings).

fichas.texto: Formula: MAP = (SBP + 2 × DBP) / 3. Variant A — CaVeSal prenatal calculator logic (used by the Calculator) Condition Level Management Source cited MAP ≥105 (any GA) High — warning sign Suspected gestational hypertension/preeclampsia, especially >20 weeks. Assess proteinuria, sFlt-1/PlGF, liver and renal function. Close monitoring. WHO / NICE / ISUOG MAP >90 and GA ≤14 weeks Moderate Higher risk of PE. Consider prophylactic aspirin based on combined risk. FMF / ACOG / Cochrane MAP >90 outside the 1st trimester Low Mildly elevated. Routine BP monitoring. NICE / CDC MAP ≤90 No alert — — Variant B — predictive performance (Cnossen et al., BMJ 2008; 34 studies, 60,599 women) Population / measure Cutoff Sens. Spec. LR+ LR− Low risk — 2nd-trimester MAP (AUC 0.76) ≥90 mmHg 62% 82% 3,5 0,46 High risk — DBP at 13-20 weeks ≥75 mmHg — — 2,8 0,39 CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Cnossen JS et al. fichas.titulo: Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy (ICP) — liver profile and timing of delivery
fichas.texto: Clinical presentation: predominantly nocturnal itching of the palms and soles, in the 2nd-3rd trimester, with no primary skin lesions. Pruritus may precede laboratory abnormalities by days. Laboratory cutoffs used by the CaVeSal prenatal calculator Parameter Normal Abnormal Meaning AST/ALT <40 IU/L >40 IU/L (>70 IU/L: suspect HELLP) Elevated enzymes = criterion for ICP LDH — >400 moderate · >600 IU/L >600 suggests hemolysis/HELLP, not ICP Total bilirubin ≤1.2 mg/dL >1.2 mg/dL Defines the icteric form Alkaline phosphatase — >300 moderate · >500 IU/L high Poorly specific (placental origin) Total bile acids (TBA) <10 µmol/L 10-39 · ≥40 severe · ≥100 very severe Specific marker; optional (not available at many centers) Variant A — Regional classification (CaVeSal prenatal calculator; MINSAL Chile 2015) Form TBA* Accessible criterion Delivery Risk Normal <10 µmol/L No symptoms — No risk Anicteric 10–39 Pruritus + elevated enzymes · normal bilirubin 38 weeks Stillbirth · meconium Icteric 40–99 Pruritus + elevated enzymes + bilirubin >1.2 36 weeks (36–37 if TBA ≥40 only) ↑↑ stillbirth · meconium Severe ≥100 Any form + severe symptoms 34–36 weeks Max. sudden stillbirth risk *TBA = total serum bile acids, optional. In all cases: UDCA 10–15 mg/kg/day orally in 2–3 doses (first-line) + oral vitamin K if cholestasis is prolonged. Monitoring: weekly NST from 32 weeks and liver panel every 2 weeks. Deliver if fetal well-being is compromised, regardless of gestational age. fichas.titulo: Acute fatty liver of pregnancy (AFLP) — Swansea criteria
fichas.texto: Diagnosis: ≥6 of the 14 criteria in the absence of another cause to explain them. Swansea criteria (Ch'ng et al. 2002) # Criterion Cutoff 1 Vomiting — 2 Abdominal pain — 3 Polydipsia / polyuria — 4 Encephalopathy — 5 Elevated bilirubin >0.8 mg/dL (>14 µmol/L) 6 Hypoglycemia <72 mg/dL (<4 mmol/L) 7 Elevated uric acid >5.7 mg/dL (>340 µmol/L) 8 Leukocytosis >11.000/µL 9 Ascites or bright liver on ultrasound — 10 Elevated transaminases (AST/ALT) >42 IU/L 11 Elevated ammonia >47 µmol/L 12 Renal failure Creatinine >1.7 mg/dL (>150 µmol/L) 13 Coagulopathy PT >14 s or aPTT >34 s 14 Microvesicular steatosis on liver biopsy — CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Ch'ng CL et al. Gut 2002;51:876-80 · Knight M et al. Gut 2008;57:951-6 · StatPearls — Acute Fatty Liver of Pregnancy · PMC3503387. Validation (Knight 2008, UKOSS): PPV 85%, NPV 100%, sensitivity ≈100%, specificity 57% versus biopsy. Antithrombin III <65%: suggestive finding, not part of the 14 criteria. Management: maternal stabilization and immediate delivery, regardless of gestational age; ICU care (monitoring of glucose, coagulopathy, renal and liver function). Wording variant: some lists (Radiopaedia, NGO) write “urea >340 µmol/L” in criterion 7; the original article refers to urate (uric acid). Sources: Ch'ng CL et al. Gut 2002;51:876-80 · Knight M et al. fichas.titulo: MAP/HR index: hemodynamic phenotype in hypertension
fichas.texto: MAP ÷ HR approximates peripheral vascular resistance at the bedside, without echocardiography or noninvasive monitoring. MAP/HR Phenotype Suggested first-line approach >1,4 Hypodynamic: high resistance, normal or low cardiac output; more associated with FGR Calcium channel blocker (nifedipine) 1,1–1,4 Normodynamic Methyldopa <1,1 Hyperdynamic: high output, low resistance Labetalol or methyldopa Guides drug selection only for non-severe hypertension or maintenance therapy. fichas.texto: Definition (WHO 2017): "maternal sepsis is a life-threatening condition defined as organ dysfunction resulting from infection during pregnancy, childbirth, postabortion, or the postpartum period." Suspected or confirmed infection + organ dysfunction = maternal sepsis. Sepsis-3 framework adapted to obstetrics: the focus shifts from the inflammatory response (SIRS) to organ dysfunction. WHO calls for two sets of criteria: early identification ("presumed maternal sepsis") to enable immediate action, and diagnostic confirmation for epidemiological purposes. Prevention: handwashing, universal urine culture, clean birthing areas, sterile instruments, vector protection, disposal of contaminated materials, vaccination, education, STI screening/treatment. Criteria for suspected sepsis (WHO GLOSS 2020; labeled "OTAS" in the reference handout, but not the OTAS triage scale): temperature>38°C or <35°C, SpO2<95%, SBP<90, HR>100, RR>25, altered mental status, uterine tenderness with suspected source.

Antonio Heras G. · SOMANZ Sepsis Guidelines 2017 · Medicina Fetal Barcelona — Sepsis and Septic Shock · DSI: MDCalc — Diastolic Shock Index.

fichas.texto: Suspected infection + 2 of 4: temp<36 or >38°C, HR>110, RR>24, WBC>15,000 or <4,000 or 10% bands = SEPSIS → start 1-2 L crystalloids + antibiotics + monitoring. If MAP remains <65 after a 30 mL/kg bolus = SEPTIC SHOCK. MSPBS, Code Red Guide, 2nd ed. 2022 (p. 76): septic shock = need for vasopressors to maintain MAP ≥65 mmHg with lactate ≥2 mmol/L (18 mg/dL) despite adequate fluid resuscitation. This set (T, HR>110, RR>24, WBC with >10% bands) is the one used in the UdeA/UNFPA workshop, adapted from the CMQCC Toolkit. It is stricter than classic SIRS (HR>90, RR>20, WBC >12,000; see subcard 10). A slide from the same workshop states "MAP <60"; this is excluded because it lacks its own citation: the current cutoff is 65 (MSPBS + CMQCC + SOMANZ). Adapted EAPO (MEOWS, reference from the handout): 7 parameters (temp, SBP, DBP, pulse, RR, SpO2, mental status, urine output). Score: 0=routine; 1-3=observation every 4h + notify charge nurse; ≥4 with a single "red 3" or total≥4="THINK SEPSIS" (observation every 4h + urgent notification); ≥6="THINK SEPSIS" (continuous monitoring + emergency notification). Note: this reference EAPO-MEOWS differs from the official MSPBS EAPO used in the Full module — shown here only as an additional reference; do not confuse them.

fichas.texto: Take 4: cultures, laboratory tests for organ dysfunction + lactate, vital signs, imaging. Give 5: O2 FiO2≥50%, crystalloids 20-30 mL/kg bolus + maintenance 1-2 mL/kg/h, broad-spectrum antibiotics, treatment of hyper/hypothermia, vasopressors if MAP<65 after bolus. Consider 3: fetal well-being if >26 weeks, infection source control, thromboprophylaxis. Targets: urine output>0.5 mL/kg/h or >30 mL/h, MAP ≥65 (MSPBS 2022; Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2021), PaO2>60 or SpO2>95%, Glasgow Coma Scale 15. UdeA/UNFPA variant (slide "Therapeutic targets"): MAP >60 or SBP >85 mmHg, urine output >0.5 mL/kg/h or >30 mL/h, SpO2 >95%, normal mental status. Stabilize and refer: review at 3 h (diagnosis/treatment/labs, repeat lactate, reassess source) and at 6 h (review diagnosis/treatment, close monitoring; ideally transfer to a tertiary care center by 6 h).

fichas.texto: Urinary: piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g q8h or gentamicin 3-5 mg/kg q24h. Respiratory: ampicillin-sulbactam 3g q6h + clarithromycin 500mg q12h (+ oseltamivir if at risk for influenza). Puerperal infection: clindamycin 900mg q8h + gentamicin 240mg q24h or amikacin 1g q24h; or ampicillin-sulbactam 3g q6h; or crystalline penicillin + metronidazole + gentamicin regimen. Vasopressor: norepinephrine 0.05 µg/kg/min until MAP ≥65, via central line or 14-16G access. UdeA: dopamine 5 µg/kg/min via peripheral line as an alternative, only after volume repletion.

fichas.texto: Level Tool What it detects Rapid screening Shock Index (SI) = HR/SBP, cutoff ≥ 0.9 Initial alert for hemodynamic compromise Severity reinforcement Diastolic Shock Index (DSI) = HR/DBP, cutoff ≥ 2.2 Vasoplegia / poor prognosis — more sensitive than SI alone in septic shock Reinforcement, only if already receiving a vasopressor Vasoactive-Diastolic Index (VDI) = DBP ÷ (vasopressor dose × HR), risk if ≤ 6.7 Degree of vasopressor dependence — refractory shock CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MD Antonio Heras G. — Obstetric Coagulopathy and Sepsis Calculator · SOMANZ Sepsis Guidelines 2017 · MDCalc — Diastolic Shock Index. DSI: general sepsis literature more commonly cites the rounded cutoff ≥2.0; 2.2 is used as the primary cutoff (Heras source), with this note on the variant most cited in the non-obstetric literature. VDI: the classic intensive care formula uses MAP in the denominator (VIS/MAP); the variant recorded here (DBP ÷ dose × HR) is specific to the Heras source.

fichas.titulo: SIRS, qSOFA, and maternal early warning in pregnant women — diagnostic performance
fichas.texto: When is each tool activated? Tool Activated by Parameters SIRS (Bone 1992) ≥2 criteria T >38 or <36 °C · HR >90 · RR >20 or PaCO₂ <32 · leukocytes >12,000 or <4,000 qSOFA (Sepsis-3, Singer 2016) ≥2 criteria RR ≥22 · SBP ≤100 · altered mental status Maternal early warning criteria (Mhyre 2014) 1 criterion is sufficient SBP <90 or >160 · DBP >100 · HR <50 or >120 · RR <10 or >30 · SpO₂ <95 % on room air · urine output <35 mL/h for ≥2 h · agitation, confusion, or unresponsiveness · preeclampsia with persistent headache or dyspnea How well do they detect maternal sepsis? Tool Sens. Spec. Use SIRS ≥2 93 % 63 % Screen (many false alarms) Maternal early warning criteria (≥1) 82 % 87 % Intermediate qSOFA ≥2 50 % 95 % Severity (a negative result does not rule it out) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Bauer ME et al. Risk Factors, Etiologies, and Screening Tools for Sepsis in Pregnant Women: A Multicenter Case-Control Study. Anesth Analg 2019;129(6):1613-1620 Most useful individual criteria: HR >90 is almost always present (sensitivity 96 %) but has low specificity (45 %); by contrast, RR >30 and altered mental status are virtually absent in controls (specificity close to 100 %), although they are absent in more than half of sepsis cases. Clinical interpretation: Use SIRS or maternal early warning criteria for screening; qSOFA to stratify severity; SOFA and lactate to confirm. The operational scores remain those in subcards 5-9. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Analysis based on Bauer ME et al. Anesth Analg 2019;129(6):1613-1620 (multicenter case-control study: 82 cases, 328 controls). Rounded values; confidence intervals and details by criterion are in the original article. Original definitions: Bone RC et al. Chest 1992;101:1644-55 · Singer M et al. JAMA 2016;315:801-10 · Mhyre JM et al. Obstet Gynecol 2014;124:782-6. The UdeA/UNFPA workshop cites this study for obstetric qSOFA (sensitivity 36-50 %, specificity 70-95 %).

fichas.titulo: Causes, pathogens, mortality, and risk factors with ORs
fichas.texto: Most common causes: chorioamnionitis 24.4%; endometritis 23.2%; pneumonia 11.0%. Most common pathogens: E. coli 14.6%; other gram-negative bacilli 9.8%; group A Streptococcus 7.3%. Mortality: 12.2% overall; 8.3% if antibiotics are started in <1 h versus 20% if >1 h. Factors associated with maternal sepsis (approximate crude OR) Group Factor and magnitude of association Childbirth and puerperium Cesarean delivery during labor ~21 · cesarean delivery before labor ~16 · fetal demise ~15 · retained products of conception ~13 · PROM >24 h ~9 · preterm delivery ~6 · multiple pregnancy ~6 · antenatal corticosteroids ~5 · GBS positive ~2 · nulliparity ~2 Chronic disease Liver disease ~15 · heart failure ~10 · chronic kidney disease ~10 Other BMI ≥40 ~4 · smoking ~3 · African American or Asian ethnicity ~4 (US population) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Bauer ME et al., Anesth Analg 2019;129(6):1613-1620 · WHO Statement on Maternal Sepsis (WHO/RHR/17.02)Delivery variables exclude cases of sepsis prior to delivery (reverse causality). fichas.titulo: MEOWS — Maternal Early Obstetric Warning Score (complete table)
fichas.texto: Cumulative score (0-3 per parameter) for early detection of maternal physiological deterioration — does not diagnose sepsis by itself, but identifies deterioration that warrants escalation of the response, whatever the cause. Complements SIRS/qSOFA/SOFA (subcards 5-13). Scoring by parameter (highest recorded value counts) Parameter 3 2 1 0 1 2 3 Temperature (°C) ≤35 35-35,9 36-37,4 37,5-37,9 38-38,9 ≥39 Systolic BP (mmHg) ≤70 71-79 80-89 90-139 140-149 150-159 ≥160 Diastolic BP (mmHg) ≤49 50-89 90-99 100-109 ≥110 Pulse (bpm) ≤40 40-49 50-99 100-109 110-129 ≥130 Respiratory rate (breaths/min) ≤10 11-20 21-24 25-29 ≥30 O₂ saturation (%) ≤94 ≥95 Mental status Alert Responds to voice Responds to pain Unconscious Urine output (mL/h) ≤10 ≤30 Not measured Total score → response level Score Response level 0 Routine observation 1-3 Observation at least every 4 h · call the nurse in charge A single red 3 or aggregate score ≥4 — THINK SEPSIS Observation at least hourly · urgent call to the responsible medical team and staff with expertise in managing acute illness Aggregate score ≥6 — THINK SEPSIS Continuous vital sign monitoring · emergency call to the team with critical care expertise and diagnostic skills Sensitivity 89%, specificity 79% for severe maternal morbidity (not specific to sepsis). Available as a mini-calculator in the Calculator mode. fichas.texto: Gibbs criteria: fever + ≥2 of the following Criterion Cutoff Maternal fever (mandatory) ≥37.8 °C (Gibbs 1982); many guidelines use ≥38.0 °C Maternal tachycardia >100 bpm Fetal tachycardia >160 bpm Uterine pain / tenderness — Foul-smelling / purulent amniotic fluid or discharge — Maternal leukocytosis >15,000/mm³ (without recent corticosteroids) The current designation «Triple I» (NICHD 2015, ACOG CO 712) is detailed in the PROM tab, subcard 8. Intrapartum antibiotic regimen (ACOG CO 712) Drug Dose Ampicillin 2 g IV every 6 h + Gentamicin 2 mg/kg IV loading dose, then 1.5 mg/kg every 8 h, or 5 mg/kg IV every 24 h Mild penicillin allergy Cefazolin 2 g IV every 8 h + gentamicin Severe allergy Clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 h or vancomycin 1 g IV every 12 h + gentamicin If cesarean delivery Add clindamycin 900 mg IV or metronidazole 500 mg IV (anaerobic coverage) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Chorioamnionitis: An Update on Diagnostic Evaluation (Gibbs 1982, J Infect Dis 145:1-8) · Management of Clinical Chorioamnionitis — PMC8315154 · ACOG Committee Opinion No. 712 (2017).

fichas.texto: Mnemonic (Knapp C & Bhatia K, Br J Hosp Med 2022): Accidents/anesthetic complications/asthma; Bleeding (hemorrhages); Cardiovascular; Drugs/medications (magnesium sulfate); Embolic (amniotic fluid, pulmonary); Fever (sepsis, septic shock); General (6Ts and 6Hs); Hypertension (HDP, HELLP). “Perpetuates cardiac arrest” — 6Hs: Hypoxia, hypo-/hyperkalemia, H+ acidosis, hypothermia, hypovolemia, hypoglycemia. 6Ts: Cardiac tamponade, pulmonary thrombosis, coronary thrombosis, tablets/toxins, pneumothorax, trauma.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: Knapp C & Bhatia K, Br J Hosp Med 2022;83(12):1-12; 2020 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (updated 2025); Bennett Terri-Ann, Critical Care Obstetrics 2024:199-208; Sumer, Emergency Medicine Clinics of North America 2023;41(3):485-508.

fichas.texto: Unresponsive/unconscious patient → activate Obstetric Code Blue → check pulse for 10 seconds → if no pulse, initiate CABD (Circulation: compressions; Airway: open; Breathing: positive-pressure ventilation; Defibrillate if shockable rhythm). Chest compressions 30:2, ventilations every 2 min or 5 cycles → aortocaval decompression (left uterine displacement) → open the airway → epinephrine 1mg IV every 3-5 min. Modifications in pregnancy: deeper chest compressions, left uterine displacement, early endotracheal intubation + cricoid pressure. Airway: O2 100% at 15L/min → intubation attempt 1 and 2 → if unsuccessful, supraglottic airway device attempt 1 and 2 → if unsuccessful, bag-mask ventilation → if ineffective, cricothyrotomy. 8-10 ventilations/min, monitor CO2, minimize time without compressions, 6.0-7.0mm tube.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: Knapp C & Bhatia K, Br J Hosp Med 2022;83(12):1-12; 2020 AHA Guidelines for CPR and ECC (updated 2025); Bennett Terri-Ann, Critical Care Obstetrics 2024:199-208; Sumer, Emergency Medicine Clinics of North America 2023;41(3):485-508.

fichas.texto: VF/pulseless VT: initial shock 150J biphasic or 360J monophasic + 2 min CPR (30:2); if there is no response, another shock + amiodarone 300mg IV (150mg additional if VT persists). Asystole/PEA: continue compressions and ventilation, verification protocol. Epinephrine 1mg IV every 3-5 min: for a nonshockable rhythm, administer immediately once IV access is obtained; for a shockable rhythm, after the 2nd shock. 4-minute rule: preparation for hysterotomy begins when cardiac arrest is recognized. If there is no return of spontaneous circulation by minute 4, initiate resuscitative hysterotomy (perimortem cesarean delivery) on site, without transferring the patient or stopping CPR, to achieve delivery by minute 5 → alert the neonatal team if GA>24 weeks. Timer on the calculator, Obstetric Code Blue. Minute 0Unresponsive → activate code Minutes 0-4CABD + aortocaval decompression + prepare for hysterotomy Minute 4Initiate hysterotomy Minute 5Birth

fichas.titulo: Perimortem cesarean delivery and MgSO4 toxicity
fichas.texto: Perimortem cesarean delivery: <20 weeks NO; 20-24 weeks depending on suspected aortocaval compression; >24 weeks ALWAYS. Magnesium sulfate toxicity: calcium gluconate 10% 30mL, or calcium chloride 10% 10mL (1g).

fichas.titulo: Maternal collapse: sepsis vs PE vs amniotic fluid embolism (POCUS + ROTEM)
fichas.texto: Septic shock Massive PE Amniotic fluid embolism Context Progressive onset; fever or source; sudden collapse is rare Sudden dyspnea, chest pain; VTE risk factors Labor, cesarean delivery or first 30 min postpartum POCUS: heart Hyperdynamic LV (or late septic cardiomyopathy) Dilated RV (RV/LV >1), “D-shaped” septum, McConnell sign; sometimes intracardiac thrombus Dilated and hypokinetic RV, “D-shaped” septum, small LV; then biventricular failure POCUS: IVC / veins / lung Small, collapsible IVC; look for a source (consolidation, collections) Dilated IVC; deep vein thrombosis on lower-extremity compression ultrasound Dilated IVC; pulmonary edema possible Coagulation / ROTEM Late coagulopathy; SIC score ≥4 (ISTH 2025) No inherent consumptive coagulopathy Early and disproportionate coagulopathy: very low FIBTEM, possible hyperfibrinolysis (high EXTEM ML) Key action Antibiotics within the first hour, guided crystalloid fluids, norepinephrine Anticoagulation; thrombolysis if cardiac arrest or shock High-quality CPR, avoid fluid overload, RV support, early massive transfusion, tranexamic acid A dilated RV does not distinguish PE from AFE. Severe early coagulopathy points to AFE; its absence points to PE. No laboratory test confirms AFE: it is a clinical diagnosis of exclusion. Practice the three cases in the simulator: Septic shock · Massive PE · Amniotic fluid embolism. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: SMFM Clinical Guideline #9, Pacheco LD et al. Am J Obstet Gynecol 2016 · APSF Newsletter, amniotic fluid embolism · StatPearls, Amniotic Fluid Embolism · POCUS + ROTEM in amniotic fluid embolism (case report, PMC11800665) · Iba T et al. fichas.texto: For all patients (pregnancy, labor or postpartum): adequate hydration and early ambulation. Mandatory anticoagulation (regardless of the risk scale) if there is: active venous thromboembolic disease (DVT, PE, cerebral venous sinus thrombosis), high-risk cardiac conditions (arrhythmias, prosthetic valves, cardiomyopathy with reduced LVEF, intracardiac thrombi, pulmonary hypertension), or known thrombophilia.

fichas.texto: LMWH: strong recommendation in favor, low-quality evidence — no preference for a specific type. Unfractionated heparin: alternative when LMWH is not feasible (strong recommendation in favor). Fondaparinux: consider only if heparins are contraindicated (good practice point). Antiplatelet agents: weak recommendation against use for VTE prevention (very low-quality evidence). Intermittent pneumatic compression + pharmacological prophylaxis: weak recommendation against — no clear additional benefit and more bleeding. Regional anesthesia preferred over general anesthesia: weak recommendation in favor, associated with lower VTE risk (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.55-0.79 for DVT). Graduated compression stockings: reduce DVT OR 0.33 (0.26-0.41), proximal DVT OR 0.26, PE OR 0.38 — strong recommendation in favor, very low-quality evidence. Hydration: “avoid dehydration” is a weak recommendation in favor, with very low-quality evidence. Vigorous hydration/hemodilution increased the risk of postoperative DVT in a controlled trial (RR 4.50, 95% CI 1.06-19.11) — never recommend “aggressive hydration” as a thromboprophylaxis measure.

fichas.texto: Clinical presentation: pain along the course of the vein, unilateral edema, increased local temperature, difference in limb circumference, superficial collateral circulation. Test of choice: venous Doppler ultrasound of the lower extremities (loss of compressibility or absence of flow). If negative and suspicion persists (especially for iliac vein thrombosis): repeat at 3 and 7 days or consider MRI. Management: confirmed DVT → therapeutic-dose LMWH (enoxaparin 1 mg/kg every 12 h).

fichas.titulo: Pulmonary embolism (PE) — YEARS algorithm adapted for pregnancy
fichas.texto: Clinical presentation: sudden or progressive dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, cough, hemoptysis, tachypnea, tachycardia, cyanosis, syncope. If leg symptoms are present: Doppler ultrasound first; if DVT is confirmed → anticoagulate without further testing. YEARS criteria: signs of DVT · hemoptysis · PE as the most likely diagnosis YEARS criteria D-dimer Management 0 <1000 ng/mL (1.0 µg/mL) PE ruled out; do not anticoagulate 0 ≥1000 ng/mL CT pulmonary angiography ≥1 <500 ng/mL (0.5 µg/mL) PE ruled out ≥1 ≥500 ng/mL Pulmonary CT angiography (or V/Q scan) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: van der Pol LM et al. NEJM 2019;380:1139-49 (Artemis) · Medicina Fetal Barcelona (2021). The D-dimer cutoff differs by branch (1000 vs 500 ng/mL); it is not simplified to a single value. This algorithm avoided CT pulmonary angiography in 32-65% of pregnant patients, depending on trimester. Source: van der Pol LM et al. NEJM 2019;380:1139-49 (Artemis) · Medicina Fetal Barcelona (2021).

fichas.texto: Indication for testing: Personal history of VTE or adverse obstetric history (≥3 miscarriages <10 weeks, fetal death ≥10 weeks with a morphologically normal fetus, severe FGR <34 weeks, severe preeclampsia <34 weeks). Hereditary: factor V Leiden, prothrombin G20210A, protein C, protein S, or antithrombin III deficiency, factor XII mutation. Acquired/mixed: hyperhomocysteinemia, APS. APS criteria Type Criterion Clinical (≥1) ≥1 documented vascular thrombosis or ≥1 criterion for obstetric morbidity Laboratory (2 tests 12 weeks apart) Lupus anticoagulant · anticardiolipin IgG/IgM >40 GPL/MPL · anti-β2-glycoprotein I IgG/IgM CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Medicina Fetal Barcelona 2021 · ACOG PB 196 and 197 (2018) · RCOG GTG 37a. Treatment during pregnancy: Aspirin 100 mg/night from preconception or diagnosis until week 36 + prophylactic LMWH from ultrasound confirmation of fetal heartbeat until delivery. Postpartum: aspirin + prophylactic LMWH for 42 days. Do not confuse with aspirin 150 mg/night for preeclampsia prevention (HDP tab): these are different indications and doses. Sources: Medicina Fetal Barcelona 2021 · ACOG PB 196 and 197 (2018) · RCOG GTG 37a.

fichas.texto: Normal risk (1/6000): no antepartum thromboprophylaxis, except if hospitalized with ≥4 of: BMI >30 kg/m², age ≥35 years, smoking, preeclampsia, multiple pregnancy, significant varicose veins. High risk (>3/1000): rule out APS and thrombophilias; multidisciplinary management. COVID-19: thromboprophylaxis if hospitalized for moderate, severe, or critical illness; continue for 14 days after discharge (moderate) or 1 month (severe/critical). Postpartum: according to the postpartum score (previous section); continue during hospitalization and decide with hematology whether to continue. Source: MSPBS draft «Thromboembolism and pregnancy. Thromboprophylaxis» (corrected, unpublished version).

fichas.titulo: Protocol for suspected VTE — 15 steps (MSPBS draft)
fichas.texto: Triage: identity, gestational age/postpartum status, reason for presentation, and warning signs (sudden dyspnea, chest pain, tachypnea, cyanosis, syncope, tachycardia, painful and swollen lower limb). Assess hemodynamic stability; if there is severe compromise or suspected PE: oxygen, monitoring, and transfer to a higher level of care with referral form and perinatal record. Complete the perinatal medical history, with emphasis on thromboembolic risk factors. Clear information and emotional support throughout the process. Vital signs: BP, HR, RR, temperature, SpO₂. Determine gestational age or postpartum day (LMP, delivery date, perinatal record). Obstetric assessment: fundal height, FHR, uterine activity, fetal movements. Focused history: symptoms, dyspnea, pleuritic pain, cough/hemoptysis, leg pain/swelling, personal or family history of VTE/thrombophilia, immobilization, surgery, cesarean delivery, trauma, obesity. Focused physical examination: respiratory and cardiovascular systems, and lower extremities (unilateral edema, pain, warmth, difference in circumference, collateral veins). Studies as available: venous duplex ultrasound, ECG, blood gas analysis, chest radiograph with abdominal shielding, CT pulmonary angiography or V/Q scan. Presumptive or confirmed diagnosis of DVT/PE. Weight-adjusted LMWH (subcard 3 of block 1), unless contraindicated. Additional measures: early mobilization, compression stockings >20 mmHg, intermittent pneumatic compression (if LMWH is contraindicated, cesarean delivery/high risk, prior VTE, travel >4 h). Education for the patient and family: adherence, warning signs, seek immediate care if symptoms worsen. Detailed documentation in the medical record and follow-up scheduling.

fichas.texto: Risk factors for dystocic labor — maternal: maternal age <18 or >35 years, multiparity/nulliparity, non-gynecoid pelvis, concomitant uterine injury, congenital pelvic defects, maternal history of dystocia, prior cesarean delivery, post-term pregnancy, prior stillbirth, prolonged or instrumented labor, induction with prostaglandins, weight gain >12kg, height <155cm. Fetal: weight >4000g, non-cephalic presentation. Causes of dystocia by component P Main causes Power Inadequate uterine contractions; insufficient pushing effort (maternal exhaustion, sensory and motor effects of epidural anesthesia) Passenger Abnormal fetal head position (occiput posterior, deep transverse arrest, asynclitism); fetal abnormalities (hydrocephalus, cervical or sacral masses) Pelvis Pelvic narrowing–uterine dysfunction: the most common cause of dystocia. Cephalopelvic disproportion, pelvic deformities, cervical stenosis CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Valenti EA, Andina E, Rey A, et al. Clinical practice guidelines: Shoulder dystocia. fichas.texto: Definition: inability of one or both shoulders to pass through the pelvic inlet. It is the obstetric condition most strongly associated with birth trauma (20-50%). Obstetric emergency. Mechanism: the biparietal diameter exceeds the diameter of the pelvic inlet; pressure at the level of the pubic symphysis from endogenous forces 4-9 times greater than exogenous forces. Rubin maneuver (rotation of the more accessible shoulder toward the oblique diameter, adducting the shoulders). Jacquemier maneuver (delivery of the posterior shoulder: the posterior arm is moved backward, the forearm is flexed over the arm, the hand is grasped, and the posterior shoulder is disengaged). Posterior axillary traction. Gaskin maneuver (maternal position on all fours — changes pelvic geometry without direct fetal manipulation).

fichas.titulo: ACOG criteria for attempted vaginal delivery
fichas.texto: All criteria must be met — failure to meet any one indicates cesarean delivery: Estimated fetal weight <3,500 g. Biparietal diameter <96 mm (range 90-100mm, Williams Obstetrics citing Giuliani 2002 and Roman 2008 — not a specific ACOG cutoff). Clinically adequate pelvis. Frank or complete breech (footling breech excluded). Flexed fetal head. Absence of fetal anomalies. No contraindications to vaginal delivery. Absence of concomitant pathology. fichas.texto: General management of breech labor, not a specific maneuver: the infant should be delivered by maternal pushing, supported only by the bony parts (hips and sacrum), without traction, without pulling on the legs, without touching the infant until the scapulae appear (to avoid triggering the respiratory reflex before the head is delivered). ⏱️ Once the umbilicus is out: complete delivery within a maximum of 3 minutes (risk of cord compression). Ensure the back does not rotate to a posterior position.

fichas.texto: Pinard: insert two fingers into the vagina and “hook” the leg from medial to lateral just above the knee; flex at the hip and abduct to release the foot. Repeat with the other leg if the breech is complete. Lovset: place the thumbs over the sacrum, grasp the hips, and rotate 90°; release the anterior arm; counter-rotate 180° and release the posterior arm. Bracht: hold the hips and lift with both hands toward the maternal abdomen without traction; the neck pivots over the symphysis. An assistant applies suprapubic pressure. Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit (modified): kneel at a 45° downward angle; support the infant on the hand and forearm; place the index and middle fingers on the maxilla (NOT inside the mouth — risk of mandibular fracture); place the other hand on either side of the neck; lower the head, bringing the subocciput beneath the symphysis; use a sweeping motion, bringing the back toward the maternal abdomen. Apply suprapubic pressure along the pelvic axis. Suzor: rotate the back 90°; pull downward; insert one hand along the back to locate the anterior arm; place the thumb in the axilla and the middle finger along the arm; lower the anterior arm; lift by the feet to release the posterior shoulder.

fichas.texto: Verify the criteria for vaginal delivery (subcard 4) — if not met, cesarean delivery. Confirm the type of presentation (subcard 2) — frank/complete breech are candidates; footling breech is highly unfavorable. Delivery: hands off — allow descent with maternal pushing. Legs (if not delivered spontaneously): Pinard. Arms: Lovset (or Suzor if it fails). Head: Bracht → if unsuccessful, Mauriceau-Smellie-Veit → if unsuccessful, forceps for the aftercoming head. Timer: from delivery of the umbilicus, a maximum of 3 minutes to deliver the head. Document maneuvers and times (medicolegal).

fichas.texto: Clinical: clear fluid leaking from the vagina — reliability >90% if visualized at the external cervical os on speculum examination. Confirmatory tests: Fern test. Nitrazine test (pH>6.5 turns blue). Commercial biomarkers (PAMG-1/AmniSure, IGFBP-1/Actim PROM). Measurement of urea and creatinine in vaginal secretions — urea 94%/82% and creatinine 98%/90% (sensitivity/specificity, Alao 2023); low cost, useful in resource-limited settings. See comparative table in subcard 7. Diagnostic amniocentesis (gold standard in equivocal cases): ultrasound-guided instillation of indigo carmine, vaginal tampon, confirmation of staining at 20-30 min. Methylene blue CONTRAINDICATED for intra-amniotic use — teratogenic; causes neonatal jejunal/ileal atresia, severe hyperbilirubinemia, fetal methemoglobinemia, and hemolysis. Safe alternatives: indigo carmine or fluorescein. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Alao AI et al. Arch Gynecol Obstet 2023;307(2):447-452. Microbiological analysis of amniotic fluid: Gram stain, culture (aerobes/anaerobes/Mycoplasma/Ureaplasma), amniotic fluid glucose (<14 mg/dL suggests intra-amniotic infection), leukocyte count.

fichas.texto: Gestational age Management Previable (<22-24 wk) Expectant management as an outpatient/inpatient; counseling on the risk of pulmonary hypoplasia, deformities, and stillbirth. No corticosteroids, tocolysis, or routine antibiotics. Preterm, remote from term (24⁰/⁷-33⁶/⁷ wk) Expectant inpatient management; complete course of antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone/dexamethasone); magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection if delivery is imminent and GA<32 wk; mandatory latency antibiotic prophylaxis; tocolysis contraindicated or limited to 48h to complete corticosteroid treatment (if no infection). Late preterm (34⁰/⁷-36⁶/⁷ wk) ACOG/FIGO recommendation: delivery/induction at diagnosis. Exception: expectant management until 37 weeks only if there are no signs of infection + close monitoring. At term (≥37⁰/⁷ wk) Induction (oxytocin or misoprostol if the cervix is unfavorable) within 12-24h to reduce the risk of intrauterine infection. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG · FIGO.

fichas.texto: Standard ACOG/NICHD regimen (7 days): Days 1-2 IV: Ampicillin 2g q6h + erythromycin 250mg q6h (or azithromycin 1g PO as a single dose). Days 3-7 PO: Amoxicillin 250mg q8h + erythromycin base 333mg q8h (MSPBS 2018 uses amoxicillin 500mg; see card 17). Alternative regimen (with azithromycin, widely used): Ampicillin 2g IV q6h x48h → amoxicillin 250mg PO q8h x5 days + azithromycin 1g PO as a single dose at admission (ACOG: an appropriate substitute for erythromycin). Avoid amoxicillin + clavulanic acid — risk of neonatal necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC). CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG.

fichas.texto: PROM: rupture of membranes occurring at least 2 hours before the onset of labor, regardless of GA (FASGO 2018 consensus). Latency period: time between rupture and onset of labor; inversely proportional to GA (longer when rupture occurs earlier). Subtypes by site of rupture (widely used teaching terminology in Spanish-language obstetric education) Subtype Characteristic High rupture of membranes Rupture above the internal cervical os; scant or intermittent fluid leakage. Low rupture of membranes Rupture near the internal cervical os; frank fluid leakage. False rupture of membranes Rupture of only one membrane (amniochorion) with persistence of the other; difficult to diagnose, with confirmatory tests that may yield false-negative results. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: FASGO. 2018 Obstetrics Consensus: Premature rupture of membranes. These subtypes are not included in the 2018 FASGO Consensus and are presented without specific attribution to that source.

Vaginal urea (cutoff 1.25 mg/dL) 94% 82% Low cost; useful in resource-limited settings (Alao 2023). fichas.titulo: Triple I (clinical chorioamnionitis): criteria for suspected infection
fichas.texto: “Triple I” (Intrauterine Inflammation, Infection or both) is the modern term proposed by the 2015 NICHD workshop and adopted by ACOG/SMFM; it replaces “clinical chorioamnionitis” (classic Gibbs 1982 criteria: fever ≥37.8 °C + ≥2 signs; many guidelines use ≥38.0 °C). Definition in ACOG Committee Opinion 712 (2017) Category Criterion Suspected intra-amniotic infection (Triple I) — highest priority Maternal temperature ≥39.0 °C isolated, or 38.0-38.9 °C sustained (confirmed on repeat measurement at 30 min) plus 1 additional factor: maternal leukocytosis, purulent cervical drainage, or fetal tachycardia. Isolated maternal fever Temperature 38.0-38.9 °C without other factors, whether persistent or not. Management of Triple I: broad-spectrum antibiotics, delivery, and maternal resuscitation. In PROM, monitoring uses the same obstetric qSOFA (SBP <90, RR ≥25, altered mental status) used in the sepsis module; ≥2 points = high risk of deterioration. fichas.texto: Patient at risk of MDR = 1 major criterion or 2 or more minor criteria (comorbidities count as one criterion). Major criterion: previous infection or colonization with MDR bacteria. Minor criterion 1: comorbidity (CKD, pregestational diabetes, heart disease, COPD) or immunosuppression (neutropenia, transplant, corticosteroids >20 mg/day of prednisone or equivalent for >2 weeks, immunosuppressants/cytotoxic agents, HIV with CD4 <200, primary immunodeficiencies). Minor criterion 2: indwelling urinary catheter. Minor criterion 3: hospital admission in the previous 3 months, regardless of duration. Minor criterion 4: systemic antibiotic (oral or IV) in the previous 3 months, regardless of duration (common in recurrent UTIs). Minor criterion 5: origin from an endemic area (Latin America, the Caribbean, Asia, non-EU Mediterranean) and <6 months in the country, or >6 months in the country but travel to or visits from family from that country in the previous 6 months. fichas.titulo: Decision tree: immediate delivery vs expectant management
fichas.texto: Confirmed preterm PROM ▼ Is there any criterion for immediate delivery? ▼ YES — deliver immediately Triple I / clinical chorioamnionitis · placental abruption · acute fetal compromise · cord prolapse · active labor · active maternal bleeding NO — expectant management according to gestational age ▼ Inpatient admission, monitoring (subcard 12), corticosteroids, latency antibiotics, and magnesium sulfate according to GA Gestational age category for expectant management Previable (<24 wk) Counseling (pulmonary hypoplasia, deformities, fetal demise). No routine corticosteroids, tocolysis, or antibiotics. 24⁰/⁷-33⁶/⁷ wk Inpatient expectant management; corticosteroids, latency antibiotics, magnesium sulfate if <32 wk and delivery is imminent. 34⁰/⁷-36⁶/⁷ wk Delivery at diagnosis (ACOG/FIGO); expectant management until 37 wk only in the absence of infection and with close monitoring. ≥37 wk Induction within 12-24 h. fichas.titulo: Regional context: outpatient management vs continuous hospitalization
fichas.texto: Conditional golden rule: without active remote monitoring (continuous temperature sensor, outpatient CTG with remote transmission) or emergency access to a hospital within <15 min, continuous hospitalization is the only standard that safeguards the mother and fetus and provides medico-legal safety. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: RCOG · ACOG · NICE. Outpatient management should only be considered if all these requirements are met: Patient at low risk of infection, strictly selected. Guaranteed maternal adherence and stable connectivity. 24/7 monitoring by a specialized team. Immediate access to obstetric and neonatal ICU care. Response in <15 min to a critical alarm. Recommendation to use regional clinical judgment, consistent with RCOG #73, ACOG, and NICE NG25 (inpatient expectant management by default).

fichas.texto: GA Management Antibiotics Less than 24 weeks (previable) Expectant management; decision made jointly with the parents. No group B streptococcus prophylaxis, corticosteroids, tocolysis, or MgSO4 before viability Consider from 20⁰/⁷ weeks 24⁰/⁷ a 33⁶/⁷ Inpatient expectant management (or refer to a Level III facility); IV crystalloids; CBC and CRP every 48 h; temperature monitoring. Corticosteroids at 24-34 weeks; MgSO4 if <32 weeks and delivery is likely within 24 h; tocolysis only to complete corticosteroid administration or for 48 h. Deliver if contractions, infection, or fetal compromise persist One of: ampicillin 2 g IV, then 1 g every 4 h · amoxicillin 500 mg PO every 8 h · clindamycin 900 mg IV every 8 h (allergy) · erythromycin 250 mg PO every 6 h · amoxicillin + sulbactam 1.5 g every 8 h; 7 days or until delivery + azithromycin 1 g PO once 34⁰/⁷ a 36⁶/⁷ Consider delivery by the most appropriate route Same options. Alternative if available: ampicillin 1-2 g IV every 6 h + erythromycin 500 mg PO every 6 h (48 h), then amoxicillin 500 mg PO every 6 h + erythromycin 500 mg PO every 8 h (5 days) 37⁰/⁷ or more Deliver by the most appropriate route according to cervical status Group B streptococcus positive: ampicillin 2 g IV q4 h until delivery. More than 18 h without infection: penicillin G 5 M IU, then 2.5 M q4 h, or ampicillin 2 g, then 1 g q4 h Chorioamnionitis (any GA) Delivery regardless of GA; notify neonatology Ampicillin 2 g IV q6 h + gentamicin 2 mg/kg, then 1.5 mg/kg q8 h (or 5 mg/kg q24 h); for cesarean delivery, add metronidazole 500 mg q8 h or clindamycin 900 mg q8 h; until 48 h without signs Difference from ACOG PB 217 (2020): amoxicillin 250 mg q8 h + erythromycin 333 mg q8 h during the oral phase, and no latency antibiotics from 34⁰/⁷ onward (only Group B streptococcus prophylaxis). The calculator uses ACOG as the preferred regimen at 24-33⁶/⁷ and allows selection of the MSPBS and NICE regimens. fichas.titulo: Corticosteroids after 34 weeks: benefit versus harm
fichas.texto: CaVeSal® approach: antenatal corticosteroids are suggested from 24⁰/⁷ to 34⁰/⁷ (MSPBS), in the absence of chorioamnionitis. Other guidelines extend the limit: ACOG through 36⁶/⁷ and NICE to consider through 35⁶/⁷. Study Design Outcome ALPS (NEJM 2016) Randomized trial, 34⁰/⁷-36⁵/⁷ Benefit: composite respiratory outcome 11.6% vs 14.4% (RR 0.80; 95% CI 0.66-0.97). Harm: neonatal hypoglycemia 24.0% vs 15.0% (RR 1.60; 1.37-1.87) ALPS follow-up (JAMA 2024) 949 children, median age 7 years No difference in cognitive impairment (17.1% vs 18.5%; adjusted RR 0.94; 0.73-1.22) Ninan (JAMA Pediatr 2022) Observational cohort, more than 1.25 million children Among late preterm and term infants exposed: more neurocognitive visits (HR 1.12) and mental or behavioral disorders in infants born at term (HR 1.47). Low certainty: does not prove causality Aviram (Arch Dis Child Fetal Neonatal Ed 2022) Population-based retrospective cohort (Ontario), 25,668 infants born at 34⁰/⁷ to 36⁶/⁷; 2,689 exposed to corticosteroids before 34⁰/⁷ At 5 years: higher suspicion of neurocognitive disorder (adjusted HR 1.12; 95% CI 1.05-1.20) and more audiometric assessments (adjusted HR 1.20) and vision assessments (adjusted HR 1.06). Observational: does not prove causality Cutoff variations Guideline Limit Conditions MSPBS 2018 (calculator) 24⁰/⁷-34⁰/⁷ No chorioamnionitis NICE NG25 Consider through 35⁶/⁷ Risk of preterm birth ACOG CO 713 Up to 36⁶/⁷ Delivery likely within 7 days, no prior course, no chorioamnionitis; caution in pregestational diabetes European guideline on perinatal care 2023 34⁰/⁷-34⁶/⁷ only in selected cases; 35⁰/⁷-36⁶/⁷ only in trials At 35-36⁶/⁷, reduces transient tachypnea, with no effect on RDS and more hypoglycemia If corticosteroids are given after 34 weeks: neonatal glucose monitoring. Chorioamnionitis: ALPS showed no increase in chorioamnionitis or sepsis, and neither did a meta-analysis (RR 0.86) (WAPM, J Perinat Med 2022). The citation "Li G et al. Lancet Neurol 2022;21:948-962" (>16,000 women) does not exist in PubMed or Lancet Neurology; the title corresponds to Aviram 2022, whose data are shown above. fichas.texto: Objective: delay delivery 48-72h to complete fetal lung maturation, provide neuroprotection, and transfer to a Level III center. Use: weeks 22/24 to 33⁶/⁷. Drug Regimen Maintenance schedule Nifedipine (1st-line ACOG/FIGO) Loading dose 10-20mg orally every 20min (max 40mg in 1st hour); maintenance 10-20mg orally every 6-8h for 48h. c/6-8h Atosiban (NICE/RCOG first line) 6.75mg IV bolus over 1min; infusion 300mcg/min for 3h, then 100mcg/min until 48h are completed. Continuous infusion (0-3h / 3-48h phases) Indomethacin (preferred before week 32) 50-100mg rectal/oral initial dose, then 25-50mg orally every 6h for a maximum of 48h. c/6h Isoxsuprine (beta-agonist) 100 mg (10 ampoules of 10 mg) in 500 cc of 5% dextrose or normal saline; start at 10 drops/min (100 mcg/min), increase by 10 drops every 15 min up to 40 drops/min (400 mcg/min); 12 h (max 24 h). fichas.titulo: Rescue course, benefits and long-term risks of corticosteroids
fichas.texto: Do not repeat routinely. Single rescue course if risk of delivery recurs, the previous course was >14 days ago, and gestational age is <34 weeks (risk of delivery within 7 days). Benefits: reduces neonatal RDS by 34%, neonatal mortality by 31%, intraventricular hemorrhage by 46%, and necrotizing enterocolitis by 54%. Betamethasone vs dexamethasone (ASTEROID, Crowther 2019): no difference in the primary outcome (death or neurodevelopmental disability at 2 years: 33% vs 32%; RR 0.97). With dexamethasone: fewer cesarean deliveries (43% vs 52%; RR 0.84) and less hypertension at 2 years (32% vs 41%; RR 0.78). Intraventricular hemorrhage did not differ (RR 1.09; p=0.72). Long-term risks and benefits by gestational age at birth (Ninan 2022: 30 studies, >1.25 million children) Group Outcome Measure Extremely preterm ↓ neurodevelopmental impairment aOR 0.69 (0.57-0.84) — ~31% lower Extremely preterm ↓ cerebral palsy aOR 0.60 (0.43-0.83) — ~40% lower Late preterm ↑ neurocognitive disorders aHR 1.12 (1.05-1.20) — ~12% higher Term (≥37 weeks) ↑ mental/behavioral disorders aHR 1.47 (1.36-1.60) — ~47% more Term (≥37 weeks) ↑ neurocognitive disorders aHR 1.16 (1.10-1.21) — ~16% more CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Crowther CA et al. ASTEROID, Lancet Child Adolesc Health 2019;3(11):769-780 · Ninan K et al. JAMA Pediatr 2022;176(6):e220483. Supports the rule against routine use of corticosteroids in late preterm/term infants or repeating courses. Räikkönen et al., JAMA 2020 (670,097 children): HR 1.33 (1.26-1.41) for any mental/behavioral disorder.

fichas.titulo: Cerebral palsy: risk by gestational age at birth
fichas.texto: Approximate relative risk compared with term birth Gestational age at birth Relative risk 34-36 weeks ~3× 30-33 weeks ~8× 28-30 weeks ~46× <28 weeks ~80× CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Petrini JR et al. Increased risk of adverse neurological development for late preterm infants. J Pediatr 2009;154(2):169-76 · Stanley FJ. Survival and cerebral palsy in low birthweight infants: implications for perinatal care. Paediatr Perinat Epidemiol 1992;6:298-310 · Moster D et al. NEJM 2008;359(3):262-273. Prevalence of cerebral palsy: 2-2.5/1000 live births, inversely proportional to gestational age. Prematurity accounts for 75% of perinatal deaths and 50% of neurological abnormalities (excluding malformations). Justifies prioritizing neuroprotection at the earliest gestational ages. Citation chain: Petrini 2009 (J Pediatr; HR 3.39 at 34-36 weeks), Stanley 1992 (Paediatr Perinat Epidemiol), Moster 2008 (NEJM; RR 78.9 at 23-27 weeks). The 8× value has no specific primary reference identified.

fichas.texto: MgSO4 regimens described in the literature (Doyle, Cochrane 2007; Magee, SOGC No. 376, 2019) Regimen Loading dose Maintenance Pritchard 4 g IV over 5 min + 5 g IM in each buttock 5 g IM every 4 h for 24 h after birth or the last seizure Zuspan 4 g IV over 20 min 1-2 g IV per hour Sibai 6 g IV over 20-30 min 2 g IV per hour (some educational sources: 2-3 g/h) Neuroprotection: two regimens with different timing Regimen Loading and maintenance Timing A — standard (FIGO 2021, SOGC 2019, NICE) — used in the calculator 4 g IV over 20-30 min + 1 g/h Start as close as possible to 4 h before delivery; continue until delivery or 24 h; do not repeat the loading dose B — high dose (Sibai / Rouse) 6 g over 20-30 min + 2 g/h Stop at 12 h if delivery is no longer imminent; if risk recurs after ≥6 h, repeat the loading bolus CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Doyle, Cochrane 2007 · SOGC · FIGO 2021 · SOGC 2019 · NICE · Martínez Gallegos 2024. The sequence “4 h before, 12 h, repeat at 6 h” mixes the two regimens. Alternative dose (Martínez Gallegos 2024): loading dose 5 g IV in 100-200 cc of 5% dextrose over 30 min; maintenance 20 g in 500 cc of 5% dextrose at 7 drops/min.

fichas.titulo: Magnesium toxicity: correlation with serum magnesium concentration
fichas.texto: Serum concentration and clinical effect (ACOG PB 222, 2020) Level mmol/L mEq/L mg/dL Effect Therapeutic 2-3,5 4-7 5-9 Therapeutic range Early toxicity >3,5 >7 >9 Loss of deep tendon reflexes Moderate toxicity >5 >10 >12 Respiratory paralysis Severe toxicity >12,5 >25 >30 Cardiac arrest Hourly monitoring: blood pressure and pulse, respiratory rate, deep tendon reflexes, and urine output. Antidote: calcium gluconate 1 g IV slowly (over 3-4 min; some sources indicate up to 10 min). Serum magnesium measurement is optional, depending on availability; clinical monitoring remains the mainstay. Thresholds vary slightly between sources (e.g., StatPearls places respiratory paralysis at 12-15 mg/dL).

HG (Hyperemesis Gravidarum): severe and intractable form, 0.3-2% of pregnancies. Classic triad: Intractable vomiting. Weight loss >5% of prepregnancy weight. Ketonuria/ketonemia + electrolyte abnormalities (hypokalemia, hypochloremia, metabolic alkalosis).

fichas.titulo: Active-phase onset — three sources, not combined
fichas.texto: Source Active-phase onset Expected progression Ministry CLAP — MSPBS partograph (PAHO/WHO-CLAP) 4 cm Alert line (1 cm/h) and action line 4 h later WHO 2020 — Labour Care Guide 5 cm Maximum time per centimeter; no 1 cm/h rule if mother and fetus are well ACOG 2024 — CPG 8 (ratifies the ACOG/SMFM 2014 consensus) 6 cm Hours without cervical change, no fixed cm/h CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS · WHO · CLAP · FIGO · Labour Care Guide 2018 · ACOG. The three sources are shown separately, without merging. The Calculator’s dynamic partograph (Childbirth tab) lets you choose the model: Ministry CLAP (default), WHO 2020 or ACOG 2024. How to use each: cards 9 to 12.

fichas.texto: Prolonged latent phase (>20h nulliparous, >14h multiparous in the 2014 consensus; ACOG 2024: >16 h in nulliparous patients) should NOT be an indication for cesarean delivery on its own. Slow but progressive active phase (not arrested) should not be an indication for cesarean delivery. Operative vaginal delivery (forceps/vacuum) in the 2nd stage by trained personnel: a reasonable alternative to cesarean delivery — training should be encouraged. Fetal monitoring: appropriate use of CTG categories (ACOG/NICHD classification) to reduce unnecessary cesarean deliveries for suspected fetal compromise, including intrauterine resuscitation measures before cesarean delivery. External cephalic version for breech presentation from 36 0/7 weeks, when there is no contraindication. Elective induction only with a favorable cervix, or after considering the risk of failure if the cervix is unfavorable. Fetal macrosomia: elective cesarean delivery for suspected macrosomia should be limited to an estimated fetal weight ≥ 5000g (or ≥ 4500g if diabetes is present) — do not perform routine cesarean delivery for suspected macrosomia without reaching that threshold (weak recommendation, lower-quality evidence).
fichas.fuentes: Source: ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No. 1 (2014) — Safe Prevention of the Primary Cesarean Delivery. · ACOG CPG 8 (2024) · MSPBS — Standards of Care · WHO Labour Care Guide (2020).

fichas.texto: Diagnose only if: Dilation ≥ 6 cm, AND Ruptured membranes, AND No cervical progress despite ≥ 4 h of adequate uterine activity (more than 200 MVUs with an intrauterine pressure catheter), or ≥ 6 h of inadequate activity with oxytocin Source: ACOG CPG 8 (2024). Detail and flowchart in sheet 11.

fichas.texto: Parity ACOG 2024 (current) Traditional definition (no longer current) Nulliparous More than 3 h of pushing 3 h with an epidural · 2 h without an epidural Multiparous More than 2 h of pushing 2 h with epidural · 1 h without epidural CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG CPG 8 (2024) · ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No. 1 (2014). Beyond these time limits, ACOG recommends an individualized approach (progress of descent, epidural, occiput posterior position, patient preference) before diagnosing arrest. The traditional definition is shown for historical reference only.

Recording frequency: FHR, contractions and maternal pulse every 30 min · temperature every 2 h · BP every 4 h · at each vaginal examination: dilatation, descent and molding. Amniotomy: not routine; only for abnormal progress. The manual does not name Friedman: it is cited as the WHO/CLAP partograph (alert/action line, 1994). Sources: MSPBS — Standards for Preconception, Prenatal, Labor, Birth and Postpartum Care · WHO partograph, Lancet 1994;343:1399-404 · CLAP/SMR 1577 (2011).

fichas.texto: Active phase from 5 cm; do not apply the 1 cm/h rule to justify interventions if the mother and fetus are stable. Companion of choice and freedom of position. Vaginal examination every 4 h in uncomplicated active labor. Intermittent auscultation (Pinard/Doppler): every 15-30 min during dilatation, every 5 min or after each contraction during the second stage. Second stage: non-supine positions, spontaneous pushing, perineal protection or warm compresses, restrictive episiotomy. Third stage: oxytocin 10 IU IM/IV, controlled cord traction, cord clamping at 1-3 min. Newborn: skin-to-skin contact for 60-90 min, breastfeeding in the first hour; defer anthropometric measurements, eye prophylaxis and vitamin K; bathing after 24 h. Practices NOT routinely recommended: enema, pubic shaving, admission pelvimetry, prophylactic IV access in low-risk patients, early amniotomy, oxytocin to shorten labor, routine episiotomy, Kristeller maneuver (prohibited). Sources: WHO Intrapartum care for a positive childbirth experience (2018) · WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) · FIGO 2019 (third stage, IJGO 145:256-8) · Lalonde A. IJGO 2012;119:84-7.

fichas.titulo: Labor pain, analgesia, cord clamping, and bonding
fichas.texto: Labor pain is physiological; nonpharmacological pain relief: warm water, movement, breathing, massage, and continuous support. In the absence of contraindications, maternal request alone is a sufficient indication for an epidural. Delayed cord clamping (1-3 min): less neonatal anemia and fewer transfusions, improved transition, and placental blood transfer (Edmonds 2013). Skin-to-skin contact: warmth, bonding and attachment, greater breastfeeding success; requires continuous support from the team. Sources: WHO 2018 · Edmonds P. Midwifery Today 2013;(108):58-62 · UdeA workshop.
fichas.fuentes: Source: ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No. 1 (2014) — Safe Prevention of the Primary Cesarean Delivery. · ACOG CPG 8 (2024) · MSPBS — Standards of Care · WHO Labour Care Guide (2020).

fichas.titulo: How to use the Ministry CLAP Partograph — flowchart
fichas.texto: Admission in labor: vaginal examination, FHR, contractions, vital signs ▼ Cervical dilation of 4 cm or more? ▼ NO — latent phase (2-3 cm) Do not open the partograph. Ambulation, oral hydration, monitoring of FHR and contractions; reassess according to progress. YES — open the partograph Mark the first point (X for dilation) on the alert line; the action line is 4 h to the right. ▼ Record: Every 30 min: FHR, contractions (number and duration in 10 min) and pulse · temperature every 2 h · BP every 4 h · at each vaginal examination: membranes and fluid, molding, dilation (X) and descent (O) · urine at each void. ▼ Where is the dilation curve? ▼ On or to the left of the alert line Normal progress: continue the plan (ambulation, oral hydration, light meals, position changes). To the right of the alert line Assess causes (uterine activity, fetal position, possible cephalopelvic disproportion) and correct them. The 4 h until the action line are for timely referral if birth is not imminent. On the action line Final assessment and decision on the safest mode of delivery. ▼ Full dilation → second stage: duration up to 2 h according to the MSPBS guideline. How to shade a contraction (intensity by duration) Intensity Duration CaVeSal® Calculator Classic paper form Mild Less than 20 s Light shading Points Moderate 20 a 40 s Medium shading Dashed Bold Greater than 40 s Dark tone Solid shading CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS — Care Standards (PAHO/WHO-CLAP partograph) · MSPBS — Safe Birth Protocol · shading by duration: Bettercare — Maternal Care y J Obstet Gynecol India. Descent: the calculator allows it to be recorded in Hodge planes (default) or in palpable fifths by abdominal examination. In the calculator: Labor → Dynamic partograph → “Ministry CLAP” model.

fichas.titulo: How to use the WHO 2020 Guide (Labour Care Guide) — flowchart
fichas.texto: Admission: cervical dilation of 5 cm or more (active phase)? ▼ NO — latent phase Do not open the guide; do not apply active-phase thresholds. YES — open the guide One column per assessment: supportive care, baby, woman, labor, medication, plan. ▼ Intervals: FHR every 30 min (every 5 min in the second stage) · contractions every 30 min (every 15 min in the second stage) · vaginal examination and descent every 4 h · pulse, BP, temperature, and urine every 4 h · supportive care at each assessment. ▼ Does any value reach the alert threshold in its row? ▼ NO Continue care. Progress slower than 1 cm/h, by itself, does not indicate intervention. YES — alert Circle it, notify the most experienced obstetrician or physician, document the assessment and plan, and share them with the woman. Alert thresholds in the WHO 2020 Guide Section Alert if… Cervix (time at the same cm) 5 cm ≥6 h · 6 cm ≥5 h · 7 cm ≥3 h · 8 cm ≥2,5 h · 9 cm ≥2 h Second stage ≥3 h nulliparous · ≥2 h multiparous Baby Baseline FHR <110 or ≥160 · late decelerations (L) · amniotic fluid M+++ or blood-stained (B) · occiput posterior or transverse position · caput +++ · molding +++ Woman Pulse <60 or ≥120 · SBP <80 or ≥140 · DBP ≥90 · temperature <35 or ≥37,5 °C · protein or acetone in urine ++ Contractions ≤2 or >5 in 10 min · duration <20 or >60 s Supportive care No birth companion, no pain relief, or no oral fluids (N) · supine position (SP) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO Labour Care Guide (2020) · Jhpiego — LCG Participant ManualOriginal design; does not reproduce the form (CC BY-NC-SA). Variable decelerations (V) are recorded but are not alerts. The guide has no alert or action lines. In the calculator: Labor → Dynamic partograph → “WHO 2020” model (dynamic table with alerts marked).

fichas.titulo: ACOG 2024 (CPG 8) — active phase begins at 6 cm and criteria for arrest
fichas.texto: Cervical dilation of 6 cm or more? ▼ NO — latent phase Do not apply active-phase criteria. Prolonged latent phase: >16 h (nulliparous women). There is no definition of latent-phase arrest: avoid cesarean delivery for this reason if the mother and fetus are well. YES — active phase ▼ Are the membranes ruptured? ▼ No: arrest is not diagnosed; consider amniotomy if there is no progress. Yes: count the time without cervical change. ▼ Adequate contractions No cervical change for ≥4 h → active-phase arrest. Inadequate contractions with oxytocin No cervical change for ≥6 h → active-phase arrest. Inadequate contractions without oxytocin Consider augmentation before measuring. ACOG 2024 criteria Item What ACOG says Onset of the active phase 6 cm (strong recommendation). There may be a range between 4 and 6 cm, but active-phase standards do not apply before 6 cm. Active-phase arrest ≥6 cm with ruptured membranes and no progress despite 4 h of adequate uterine activity, or 6 h of inadequate activity with oxytocin. Adequate contractions More than 200 Montevideo units (MVU) measured with an intrauterine pressure catheter. Prolonged second stage More than 3 h of pushing in nulliparous patients and more than 2 h in multiparous patients. Beyond these time limits, use an individualized approach (descent progress, epidural, occiput posterior position, patient preference). CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 8 — First and Second Stage Labor Management (2024). In the calculator the “ACOG 2024” model has a selector: with a catheter (textual criterion, MVU >200) or without a catheter, with a contraction counter (clinical adaptation: strong contractions every 3 min or less, according to FPQC/USF PROVIDE). Intensity is marked as mild, moderate, or strong by palpation.
fichas.fuentes: CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ACOG Clinical Practice Guideline No. 8 — First and Second Stage Labor Management (2024).

fichas.seccion: First-Half Pregnancy Hemorrhage — Miscarriage, Ectopic Pregnancy, Cervical Insufficiency/Cerclage
fichas.texto: General measures: relative rest, sexual abstinence, avoid repeated vaginal examinations. Progesterone — CaVeSal recommends: micronized progesterone 400 mg vaginally every 12 h until week 16, even without a history of miscarriage. Variants: MSPBS 2018 not routinely indicated · NICE NG126 only with ≥1 prior miscarriage (PRISM trial) · in favor: RANZCOG, FOGSI 2024, Cochrane 2018 y Cochrane 2021. Micronized progesterone 400mg vaginally every 12h until week 16. Alternative: Dydrogesterone 40mg orally initially, then 10mg every 8h. Anti-D prophylaxis: if Rh-negative, unsensitized, with clinically significant bleeding → anti-D immunoglobulin 120-300mcg IM within the first 72h.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 200 — Early Pregnancy Loss (2018, reaffirmed 2021) · ACOG Practice Bulletin No. 142 — Cerclage for the Management of Cervical Insufficiency (2014, reaffirmed 2021) · NICE Guideline NG126 — Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage (2019, updated 2023).

fichas.seccion: First-Half Pregnancy Hemorrhage — Miscarriage, Ectopic Pregnancy, Cervical Insufficiency/Cerclage
fichas.texto: Definition: inability of the cervix to retain the pregnancy in the absence of contractions/clinical abruption, with painless dilation/effacement in the 2nd trimester (16-24 weeks) → recurrent fetal loss or extreme preterm birth. Types: History-indicated (prophylactic/elective): ≥2-3 prior unexplained painless 2nd-trimester losses or preterm births. Timing: week 12⁺⁰-14⁺⁶ (after confirming viability and ruling out aneuploidy). Ultrasound-indicated (therapeutic): prior spontaneous preterm birth <34 weeks + cervical length <25mm on transvaginal ultrasound surveillance before week 24. Emergency/rescue: painless dilation with membranes protruding into the vagina/external cervical os between weeks 16-24, without active labor, chorioamnionitis, or placental abruption. Classification: primary (congenital, malformations, collagen disorders) or secondary (conization, dilations, lacerations). Prophylactic cerclage (based on history), therapeutic cerclage (based on ultrasound), or emergency cerclage (based on physical examination) (Ginecol Obstet Méx 2020). By history — variants: RCOG GTG 75: ≥3 losses or preterm births in the 2nd trimester; with 1-2, serial ultrasound at 16-24 weeks and cerclage if ≤25 mm. ACOG: may be offered after 1 typical loss. Short cervix without prior history (≤20 mm): vaginal progesterone; cerclage is not indicated. Cerclage techniques Technique Particularity McDonald Submucosal purse-string without dissection, nonabsorbable suture (Mersilene); most commonly used Shirodkar Vesicocervical dissection, higher suture placement Espinosa Flores (Mexico, 1966) Simple transcardinal ligature without mucosal dissection; short procedure and easy removal Abdominal (Benson-Durfee) By laparotomy or laparoscopy, preconceptionally or at 10-14 weeks, after failed vaginal cerclage or with a very short cervix; delivery by cesarean CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: GPC IMSS 539 · UNAM (Espinosa Flores) · FASGO 2021 · ACOG PB 142. Contraindications: active labor, intra-amniotic infection, active bleeding, PROM, placental abruption, lethal fetal anomaly, or fetal demise. Fetal fibronectin: does not diagnose cervical insufficiency; predicts preterm birth in preterm labor (high negative predictive value). Cerclage removal: scheduled electively at 36-37 weeks (or immediately if active labor/chorioamnionitis).
fichas.fuentes: CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: GPC IMSS 539 · UNAM (Espinosa Flores) · FASGO 2021 · ACOG PB 142.

fichas.texto: Management according to abortion type Type <13 weeks 13-22 weeks Threatened miscarriage (incipient) Expectant ± progesterone (see card 2); anti-D if Rh(-) In progress: imminent (dilated cervix) or inevitable (PROM) MVA Expulsion (oxytocin/misoprostol) + D&C Incomplete MVA, or misoprostol 600 µg PO / 400 µg SL (WHO); MSPBS: 400-800 µg vaginally D&C after cervical preparation Complete No evacuation; clinical follow-up Missed (fetal demise confirmed on ultrasound) Misoprostol 800 µg vaginally every 3 h ×2 or 600 µg SL every 3 h ×2 → MVA Misoprostol 200 µg every 4-6 h up to 5 doses (every 6 h with uterine scar); oxytocin 16-22 wk → D&C CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS 2018 (p. 63) · WHO 2022 · NICE NG126. Evacuation: WHO recommends aspiration and advises against sharp curettage before 14 weeks; MSPBS uses MVA before 13 and D&C from 13 to 22. The calculator ends at 13 weeks.

fichas.texto: With sepsis or septic shock: IV antibiotics within the 1st hour + immediate evacuation for source control (Code Yellow — Sepsis, Rule 4-5-3; SSC 2021). Without sepsis: IV antibiotics and evacuation 6-8 h after initiation (Clinical Practice Guideline IMSS-088, Ecuador Clinical Practice Guideline). Other guidelines: 12 h or 24-48 h. MSPBS regimens (72 h): ampicillin + metronidazole · cefazolin + metronidazole · ceftriaxone + metronidazole · gentamicin + metronidazole · gentamicin + clindamycin · ampicillin/sulbactam + clindamycin · ampicillin 2 g + gentamicin 5 mg/kg + metronidazole.

fichas.titulo: Pregnancy of unknown location and ectopic pregnancy
fichas.texto: PUL: do not treat without ultrasound confirmation; βhCG at 48 h with a minimum rise of 49 % (<1500), 40 % (1500-3000) or 33 % (>3000) (AAFP 2020). Complicated (free fluid, severe pain, instability): emergency surgery + Code Red; salpingectomy is preferred. Tubal ectopic pregnancy — criteria by source Management CaVeSal (calculator) MSPBS 2018 NICE NG126 Expectant β-hCG <1000 and declining, no criteria β-hCG <5000, mass ≤35 mm, fluid ≤300 mL, no heartbeat ≤1000 offer; 1000-1500 consider Methotrexate 50 mg/m² IM β-hCG 1000-<5000, mass <35 mm, no heartbeat β-hCG <6000, mass ≤40 mm <1500 first-line; 1500-5000 either option Surgery ≥5000, mass ≥35 mm, heartbeat or pain Outside criteria; salpingectomy ≥5000, ≥35 mm, heartbeat or pain CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS 2018 · NICE NG126 (ectopic pregnancy). Methotrexate follow-up: β-hCG on days 4 and 7; decline ≥15 % → weekly until negative; otherwise, second dose or surgery. Anti-D if Rh(-). Non-tubal ectopics (RCOG GTG 21): cervical → methotrexate; for evacuation, uterine artery embolization or vaginal uterine artery clamping (Zea technique) · cesarean scar → neither expectant management nor systemic methotrexate alone; aspiration or resection · interstitial/cornual → methotrexate or cornual resection · abdominal → early laparoscopy; advanced, laparotomy with the placenta left in situ.

fichas.texto: Diagnosis: complete (snowstorm appearance, enlarged uterus, very high β-hCG, diploid) vs. partial (fetus, placenta with cysts, triploid). Chest X-ray in all cases. Treatment: suction evacuation with oxytocin started at the time of aspiration; histopathology in all cases; contraception. β-hCG follow-up Source Regimen Ministry (MSPBS) — by default Weekly → every 2 weeks → monthly until 3 negative results; monthly for 6 months and every 2 months for 6 months (1 year). Chest X-ray at 14 days, 6 and 12 months RCOG 2020 Complete: normal before 56 days → 6 months from evacuation; otherwise, 6 months from normalization. Partial: 2 normal samples 4 weeks apart CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS 2018 · RCOG 2020.

fichas.titulo: Differential diagnosis of the 4 main causes
fichas.texto: Cause Bleeding Pain / uterine tone Fetal status Context Placental abruption Dark Sudden, severe abdominal pain, uterine hypertonia/boardlike uterus Rapid onset of acute fetal distress Common with preeclampsia/trauma Placenta previa Bright red, painless Normal uterine tone (soft uterus) Fetal heart rate initially normal Insidious onset Uterine rupture Variable Acute, lacerating intrapartum pain, abrupt cessation of uterine contractions Maternal shock + extreme fetal bradycardia History of cesarean delivery/myomectomy common; loss of fetal station Vasa previa Immediately after rupture of membranes, 100% of fetal origin — Bradycardia/severe decelerations High immediate fetal mortality 🚫 DIGITAL VAGINAL EXAMINATION IS PROHIBITED if placenta previa is suspected — it may precipitate massive hemorrhage. fichas.titulo: Management of Placenta Previa and Placental Abruption (ACOG/RCOG)
fichas.texto: Placenta previa: Diagnosis by transvaginal ultrasound — placenta previa if it covers the internal os; low-lying placenta if <20mm from the internal os. Stable/no active bleeding: fetal lung maturation at 34-36⁺⁶ weeks; elective cesarean delivery at 36⁺⁰-37⁺⁶. Severe active hemorrhage: stabilization + immediate emergency cesarean delivery, regardless of gestational age. Placental abruption: immediate delivery. Emergency cesarean delivery: general rule if the fetus is alive with compromise or the mother is unstable. Fetal demise: MSPBS recommends cesarean delivery for grades II and III; RCOG GTG 63 and the 2013 Colombian CPG accept vaginal delivery with a stable mother, early amniotomy, and oxytocin (see card 9).

fichas.seccion: Second-Half Pregnancy Hemorrhage — Placental Abruption, Placenta Previa, Uterine Rupture, Vasa Previa
fichas.titulo: Paraguayan variant: MSPBS/SPGO + Code Red 2021 (additional variant)
fichas.texto: Timing definition: bleeding in the second half of pregnancy = vaginal bleeding from 22.0 weeks until before birth. Initial stabilization protocol: O2 via non-rebreather mask at 10 L/min, target SpO2 >95%. 2 large-bore peripheral IV lines (14G or 16G). Tube color code: blue (coagulation: PT/aPTT/fibrinogen), red/brown (chemistry), lavender (CBC + crossmatch/blood bank). Warm crystalloids at 37-39°C in 250-500 mL boluses, target SBP ≥90 mmHg while avoiding fluid overload. Check vital signs every 15 min with EAPO + Foley catheter, target urine output ≥30 mL/h. Expectant management (placenta previa only) — eligibility: GA <34 weeks + scant/self-limited bleeding + stable mother + normal fetal well-being. Strict bed rest in the left lateral position. Lung maturation: Betamethasone 12mg IM every 24h ×2 doses or dexamethasone 6mg IM every 12h ×4 doses (if <34 weeks). Neuroprotection with MgSO4 if preterm labor is threatened at <32 weeks. Serial CBCs + strict monitoring of blood loss. Indications for emergency cesarean delivery (regardless of GA): active moderate-to-severe bleeding unresponsive to conservative measures; hemodynamic instability/shock; acute fetal distress; confirmed placental abruption or uterine rupture/strong suspicion; complete placenta previa at term ≥37.0 weeks. ACOG/RCOG vs. MSPyBS/SPGO comparison Point ACOG/RCOG MSPyBS/SPGO Elective cesarean delivery for stable placenta previa 36⁺⁰-37⁺⁶ weeks ≥37.0 weeks (at term) Temporal definition of the condition >20-22 weeks ≥22.0 exact weeks CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS/SPGO · Code Red 2021 · ACOG · RCOG · SPGO.

fichas.texto: Activate the obstetric emergency team + notify the obstetrician on call. Left lateral position + supplemental oxygen by face mask; stop oxytocin infusion if running. 2 large-bore IV lines (16G), samples for CBC + coagulation studies + crossmatch for 6 units. Crystalloids/blood products as needed; continuous monitoring of vital signs + CTG. Prepare the operating room for emergency cesarean delivery — birth within 30 minutes of the decision (Category 1), anticipating neonatal resuscitation. In hemodynamic instability: fluid resuscitation/transfusion in parallel with surgical preparation, without waiting for complete stabilization before operating.

fichas.texto: Incision: Pfannenstiel incision provides good exposure of the lower uterine segment/pelvis; a vertical midline incision provides better exposure for exploring the entire abdominal cavity (including the uterine fundus)—preferred when fetal distress and maternal instability coexist. Repair vs. hysterectomy: depends on the extent of the injury, patient stability, desire for future fertility, and surgeon experience — if adequate closure and hemostasis cannot be achieved → hysterectomy (usually subtotal). Complications to manage: concomitant uterine atony (uterotonics + hemostatic sutures + intrauterine balloon); bladder injury if the laceration extends to the bladder, or suspected ureteral injury → consult urology. Hemorrhage control after delivery if bleeding persists: abdominal packing, uterine artery ligation, internal iliac artery ligation, topical hemostatic agents, cesarean hysterectomy as a last resort. General anesthesia is usual; regional/spinal anesthesia is contraindicated in cases of severe bleeding diathesis.

fichas.texto: Antenatal diagnosis by ultrasound (color Doppler along the cervical route) allows elective cesarean delivery to be scheduled before the onset of labor — fetal survival >95% with antenatal diagnosis + planned cesarean delivery, vs. fetal mortality ≥60% when diagnosed intrapartum. Timing of elective cesarean delivery: SMFM Consult Series #37 recommends scheduled cesarean delivery between 34⁺⁰ and 37⁺⁶ weeks (GRADE 2C). Antenatal corticosteroids: consider between 28-32 weeks if there is a risk of urgent preterm delivery (GRADE 2C), not routinely in asymptomatic patients; a 2023 review suggests administering them within the 7 days before scheduled delivery. Antenatal hospitalization: proposed from 30-34 weeks in some series (GRADE 2C), but evidence is insufficient to make it a mandatory standard — individualized decision. 🚫 Undiagnosed vasa previa: high risk of rupture when membranes rupture — immediate emergency cesarean delivery in the event of bleeding + bradycardia/acute deceleration after amniotomy.
