Ultrasound signs (ISUOG 2016): loss of the retroplacental clear zone, placental lacunae, myometrial thinning <1 mm, disruption of the bladder line, placental bulge, focal exophytic mass; Doppler: uterovesical or subplacental hypervascularity and bridging vessels. Timing of scheduled cesarean delivery Source Window ACOG/SMFM Obstetric Care Consensus No. 7 (2018) 34+0 to 35+6 weeks RCOG Green-top 27b (2018) 35+0 to 36+6 weeks Management: level III-IV center with a multidisciplinary team and blood bank; corticosteroids if <37 weeks; tranexamic acid at onset; uterine incision away from the placenta and cesarean hysterectomy with the placenta in situ (do not attempt placental separation). Activate Code Red in the event of bleeding. CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Jauniaux E et al. fichas.texto: Classification: complete, partial, marginal, lateral (>2 cm from the internal os). Definitive diagnosis from 32 weeks. Expectant management <34+0 weeks with mild bleeding; from 34+0, cesarean delivery with recurrent bleeding. MSPBS mentions 35 weeks in one chapter; CaVeSal uses 34+0 for consistency. Asymptomatic complete previa: admission at 36 and cesarean at 37 (ACOG/SMFM: 36+0-37+6). Marginal previa in labor: amniotomy and trial of vaginal birth with the operating room ready; lateral previa: vaginal delivery may be possible. Tocolysis (hybrid): nifedipine only with preterm labor, light bleeding, and stability; avoid with heavy bleeding, instability, or fetal compromise (RCOG GTG 63). Prior cesarean: rule out placenta accreta (calculation in the CaVeSal prenatal calculator).

fichas.texto: Grades (MSPBS) and management Grade Findings Management I <11 %, normal FHR <34 weeks: monitored expectant management + antenatal corticosteroids; ≥34: delivery II ~50 %, uterine hypertonus, fetal compromise Emergency cesarean delivery III >50 %, tetany, fetal death, shock, DIC Cesarean delivery (MSPBS) + correction of coagulopathy CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS 2018 (p. 83). Fetal death — expectant management: RCOG GTG 63, Colombia CPG 2013 y Universidad Nacional de Colombia: vaginal delivery if the mother is stable, with early amniotomy and oxytocin. Tocolysis: optional in mild abruption <34 weeks with a stable mother and no fetal compromise, at the discretion of the senior obstetrician, to complete fetal maturation (observational studies). ≥34 weeks in advanced labor: vaginal delivery may be possible with amniotomy and continuous monitoring (NHS Worcestershire).

fichas.texto: Signs of impending rupture Sign Description Bandl Pathological retraction ring rising toward the umbilicus (hourglass uterus) Frommel Taut round ligaments, palpable like cords Pinard Scant, dark vaginal bleeding (Paraguayan and classical literature); some sources describe it as cervical edema Other Uterine hyperactivity (oxytocin/misoprostol), hematuria, abnormal FHR CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Clínica Universidad de Navarra · Medway. Impending: discontinue uterotonics, initiate acute uterine inhibition, and perform urgent cesarean delivery. Established: laparotomy; uterine repair if the rupture is not extensive and the patient is stable, hysterectomy if irreparable; evaluate the bladder if hematuria occurred.

fichas.titulo: PAS and vasa previa — timing and conservative management
fichas.texto: Timing of delivery Table MSPBS ACOG/SMFM FIGO/RCOG SBP Hospitalization at 32 weeks; delivery at 36-37 34+0-35+6 35+0-36+6 Vasa previa — 34+0-37+0; hospitalization at 30-34 individualized — CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS 2018 · ACOG/SMFM · SMFM CS 44 · FIGO 2018. Planned PAS: TXA 1 g, incision away from the placenta, no traction or uterotonics, cesarean hysterectomy with the placenta left in situ. Conservative (focal, in centers with experience): placenta in situ, one-stage resection, arterial embolization (FIGO 2018 conservative management). MSPBS includes methotrexate; FIGO does not recommend it. Prophylactic iliac balloons: not routinely. Vasa previa with bleeding after PROM or a sinusoidal pattern: immediate cesarean delivery.

fichas.texto: Immediate (first 24h): highest risk of PPH/4Ts — monitor vital signs, uterine tone (Pinard’s safety globe) and bleeding every 15 min for the first 2 h (MSPBS), then every 6 h — see flowchart in sheet 5. Early (day 2 to 7-10): onset of lactogenesis II, progressive intra-pelvic uterine involution (~1cm/day), red/serous lochia. Late (day 11 to 42/6 weeks): return of the genital organs to the pre-pregnancy state, resolution of lochia (alba), resumption of ovulation if not exclusively breastfeeding.

fichas.texto: Uterine involution: the uterine fundus should not be palpable above the pubic symphysis from postpartum day 10-12. Lochia — chronological progression Type Days Characteristics Red / bloody 1-3/4 Blood + decidual remnants Serous 4-10 Pink/brown, exudate + leukocytes White / alba 10-28/42 Whitish/yellowish, mucus + epithelial cells ⚠️ Warning sign: foul odor (suspected puerperal endometritis) or persistent heavy bloody lochia after day 14 (suspected retained placental tissue/subinvolution). CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO 2022 (postnatal care) · ACOG CO 736 (2018). Perineal/surgical wound care: wash with water and mild soap, pat dry, monitor for infection/dehiscence of episiotomy repair or cesarean incision.

fichas.titulo: Third stage of labor — placental delivery
fichas.texto: Definition (MSPBS): from the birth of the newborn until expulsion of the placenta. A period with potential risk of hemorrhage. Phases (third-stage ultrasound) Phase What happens Median duration Latent From birth until the onset of placental separation; myometrial-placental blood flow ceases. This phase determines the total duration ~2 min (5 s – 13 min) Separation The placenta separates from the myometrium ~50 s Expulsion From complete separation to passage through the vagina ~80 s Signs of placental separation: lengthening of the cord · sudden gush of blood · the uterus rises and becomes globular (Schröder) · the cord does not retract with suprapubic pressure (Küstner). Both signs were positive in 98 % of placentas with ultrasound-confirmed separation. Mechanisms of placental expulsion Mechanism How it is expelled Frequency and implications Schultze Central separation, expelled like an inverted umbrella: fetal surface first; the clot remains within the membranes ~80 % · less visible bleeding before expulsion Duncan Separation from the edge, expelled sideways: maternal surface first ~20 % · more bleeding and risk of retained membranes: inspect carefully Ultrasound shows that separation usually begins at the lower pole; the observed mechanism is determined as the placenta exits through the vulva. Birth — oxytocin 10 IU IM within the first minute (after ruling out a second fetus) ▼ Controlled cord traction with a contraction and suprapubic counterpressure, only with signs of placental separation ▼ Placenta delivered at 15 min and no PPH? ▼ YES Check placental and membrane integrity · uterine massage · checks every 15 min for 2 h NO Controlled cord traction, mobilize or squat, empty the bladder. Monitor bleeding ▼ 30 min without delivery → prepare for manual removal with analgesia and antibiotic prophylaxis · with PPH at any time → uterotonic + manual removal without waiting, Code Red Third-stage duration — variations Source Criterion Status WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025 (rec. 30) Without PPH: intervene at 15 min; at 30 min, prepare for manual removal. With PPH: uterotonic and removal Used by the calculator NICE NG235 (1.10.20) Prolonged: >30 min with active management; >60 min with physiological management Variant MSPBS 2022 Active management: oxytocin 10 IU IM <1 min, controlled cord traction, massage; no routine intrauterine examination National guideline CaVeSal® original table · Based on: MSPBS, Normas de Cuidados 2022, p. 69 · WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025, rec. 16, 30 and 31 · NICE NG235 (2023) · Herman et al., ultrasound and clinical findings in the third stage · El-Mowafi, GFMER — Schultze 80 % / Duncan 20 %. fichas.titulo: Immediate postpartum period — first 2 hours and beyond
fichas.texto: Placenta delivered — uterine massage, examination of the birth canal, and repair of lacerations ▼ First 2 h, in the delivery room or recovery area — every 15 min: contracted uterus and Pinard safety globe (massage if needed) · measured blood loss · HR and BP · EAPO ▼ Blood loss ≥300 mL with HR >100, shock index >1, SBP <100 or DBP <60, or ≥500 mL, or EAPO alert? ▼ YES Postpartum hemorrhage: MOTIVE and Code Red. Do not transfer until stabilized NO at 2 h Mother and newborn to the inpatient ward (no bleeding, no infection, normal vital signs, nonhemorrhagic, non-foul-smelling lochia) ▼ Then every 6 h: vital signs · Pinard safety globe · lochia · vulvoperineal abnormalities (hematomas, urinary retention) · lower extremities · bodily functions (urination, bowel movements) · emotional status (Edinburgh) ▼ Discharge from 48 h no hemorrhage, no infection, and normal vital signs · follow-up at 8 days Postpartum monitoring — variations Source Frequency and parameters Length of stay MSPBS 2022 Every 15 min for 2 h (uterus, Pinard, EAPO); then every 6 h Discharge from 48 h onward WHO 2018 (rec. 52 and 55) Uterine tone in all women; routine assessment of bleeding, uterine contraction, fundal height, temperature, and pulse during the first 24 h, starting in the first hour; BP shortly after birth and, if normal, again within 6 h; documented urination within 6 h Minimum 24 h after uncomplicated vaginal birth (rec. 56) WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025 (rec. 22) PPH criterion within 24 h, with special monitoring during the first 2 h — CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: MSPBS, Normas de Cuidados 2022, pp. 69-71 · WHO 2018, intrapartum care, rec. 52, 55 and 56 · WHO/FIGO/ICM 2025, rec. 22. fichas.texto: Hormonal axis: prolactin (production through suckling) + oxytocin (milk ejection through myoepithelial contraction). Correct latch: mouth wide open, lower lip everted, covering most of the lower areola, chin against the breast, nose unobstructed. Physiological breast engorgement: manually express a few drops beforehand to soften the areola, frequent on-demand feeds, brief warm compresses before feeding + local cold after feeding.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine (ABM) Clinical Protocol #36 — The Mastitis Spectrum (revised 2022) · WHO — Mastitis: Causes and Management · ABM Clinical Protocol #4 (PMC 2014).

fichas.texto: Etiology: milk stasis + bacterial superinfection; most common pathogen Staphylococcus aureus (and S. epidermidis). Clinical presentation: severe unilateral breast pain, wedge-shaped/well-demarcated erythema, local warmth, induration, fever ≥38.5°C, flu-like symptoms.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine (ABM) Clinical Protocol #36 — The Mastitis Spectrum (revised 2022) · WHO — Mastitis: Causes and Management · ABM Clinical Protocol #4 (PMC 2014).

fichas.texto: Initial management (ALL cases): NEVER stop breastfeeding — frequent and effective emptying of the affected breast is the mainstay; breast milk poses no infectious risk to a term infant. Warm compresses before feeding + cold after feeding. Analgesia: Ibuprofen 400-600mg orally every 8h or acetaminophen 500-1000mg orally every 6-8h. Maternal hydration and rest. Reassess at 12-24h — start antibiotics ONLY IF there are systemic symptoms (fever >38.5°C, chills, myalgia) OR there is no clinical improvement after 12-24h of optimized nonpharmacological management. Antibiotic regimen (10-14 days) if the above criterion is met: Scenario Medications and doses 1st line (methicillin-susceptible, outpatient) Cephalexin 500mg orally every 6h; Cloxacillin/Dicloxacillin 500mg orally every 6h; Amoxicillin + Clavulanic acid 875/125mg orally every 8-12h Penicillin/beta-lactam allergy Clindamycin 300mg orally every 6h; Erythromycin 500mg orally every 6h Suspected MRSA Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 160/800mg orally every 12h (avoid if infant is <1 month old with jaundice) or IV vancomycin if hospitalization is required CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ABM Clinical Protocol #36 (2022) · WHO — Mastitis.

fichas.titulo: Breast abscess: suspicion and ultrasound diagnosis
fichas.texto: Clinical suspicion: persistent painful fluctuant mass with erythema that does not resolve after 48-72h of antibiotics. Criteria for referral to the emergency department/surgery: Treatment failure (persistence/worsening after 48-72h of appropriate antibiotics + effective milk drainage). Signs of a collection (fluctuant mass, induration, overlying skin thinned/shiny). Severe systemic involvement (refractory fever >38.5°C, tachycardia, hypotension, marked leukocytosis, suspected sepsis/SIRS). Local complications (ischemia, skin necrosis, rapid spread of erythema, suspected granulomatous mastitis/inflammatory breast cancer — oncologic red flag). Technical difficulty (image-guided percutaneous drainage not feasible at the facility). Ultrasound diagnosis (gold standard): hypoechoic/anechoic collection, irregular/microlobulated margins, thickened wall with Doppler hypervascularity; heterogeneous contents with mobile internal echoes, septa, sometimes fluid-fluid levels or gas bubbles; posterior acoustic enhancement; color Doppler shows no flow in the center with increased peripheral vascularity (inflammatory halo); perilesional edema.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine (ABM) Clinical Protocol #36 — The Mastitis Spectrum (revised 2022) · WHO — Mastitis: Causes and Management · ABM Clinical Protocol #4 (PMC 2014).

fichas.texto: Ultrasound-guided fine-/large-bore needle aspiration (first line): collections <3-5cm, intact skin without necrosis. 16G-18G needle + 10-20mL syringe under ultrasound guidance, complete aspiration + saline irrigation. May be repeated every 48-72h if recurrence (success rate >85-90%). Always send for culture (aerobes, anaerobes, susceptibility testing). Percutaneous catheter drainage: abscesses ≥3-5cm or rapid recurrence after simple aspiration. Ultrasound-guided 8-12Fr pigtail catheter, daily irrigation, removal when output is <10-15mL/24h and the cavity has collapsed. Open surgical incision and drainage: failure of percutaneous drainage/repeated aspiration, extensive multiloculated abscesses, or skin compromise with necrosis/ischemia. Curvilinear incision respecting Langer’s lines (or periareolar), gentle digital debridement, irrigation + passive drainage (Penrose drain or iodoform gauze) for healing by secondary intention.
fichas.fuentes: Sources: Academy of Breastfeeding Medicine (ABM) Clinical Protocol #36 — The Mastitis Spectrum (revised 2022) · WHO — Mastitis: Causes and Management · ABM Clinical Protocol #4 (PMC 2014).

fichas.texto: Do not stop breastfeeding; continue emptying the affected breast. If the infant’s mouth does NOT come into direct contact with the wound/drain/infected area → direct breastfeeding is safe. If the incision/drainage involves the areola or nipple → express milk mechanically/by hand; breastfeed from the unaffected breast while visible pus contamination persists.

fichas.titulo: “Time is life”: survival curve and 3 delays
fichas.texto: Survival by time to treatment Timing Survival Time zero (identify) 100% 1-20 min (stabilize) ~60% 20-60 min (treat/transfer) <15% >60 min <10% CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: Cresswell et al., Lancet Glob Health 2025 · WHO, Trends in Maternal Mortality 2000-2023 Delay 1: in seeking help. Delay 2: in reaching care. Delay 3: in receiving appropriate treatment. They correspond to delays in identifying, stabilizing and treating/transferring, each associated with declining survival. Pathophysiology: hypovolemic shock with DIC and peripheral redistribution (cardiothoracic due to sympathetic activity; peripheral due to parasympathetic activity). Global context: causes of maternal death — hemorrhage ~27%, hypertensive disorders ~14%, sepsis ~11% (Cresswell et al., Lancet Glob Health 2025). In 2023, there were ~260,000 maternal deaths (≈1 every 2 minutes), global MMR 197/100,000 live births, 40% lower than in 2000 (WHO, Trends in Maternal Mortality 2000-2023). Three-delays model: Thaddeus & Maine 1994. Official graphic version, MSPBS/DGPS Paraguay.

fichas.texto: Apply the Early Obstetric Warning Score (EAPO) and start the timer. Look for signs of MODS (multiple organ dysfunction syndrome): severe, acquired functional abnormality of at least 2 organ systems; an early detection criterion for extreme maternal morbidity/near-miss. Determine the cause: hemorrhage (4 Ts), severe hypertensive disorder, or infection. Definition of MODS adopted from the Latin American obstetric literature (Rev Méd IMSS).

fichas.seccion: ICT Model and Resuscitation — Code Red ABCDE
fichas.texto: 5 basic steps: call for help · 2 peripheral IV lines · oxygen therapy · urinary catheterization · prevent hypothermia. Detailed version (8 steps): Call for help. Ensure airway patency. Administer oxygen. Insert 2 intravenous catheters, No. 14, 16, or 18 gauge. Parenteral hydration with normal saline: maintain systolic BP >90 mmHg and urine output >30 mL/h (or >0.5 mL/kg/h); in hypertension, maintain diastolic BP >90 mmHg. Urinary catheter and urine output monitoring. Cover with a blanket to prevent hypothermia. Monitor vital signs using the Code Red Alert Scale every 5-10 min. Urine output target: >0.5 mL/kg/h (international clinical standard, WHO/StatPearls) or >30 mL/h (MSPBS/DGPS); both are shown with their source.

fichas.titulo: Response to the initial crystalloid bolus (500 mL boluses)
fichas.texto: ATLS classification adapted to obstetrics (Plaat) Response Clinical findings % blood loss / volume Transfusion requirement Rapid Returns to normal 10-25% or 500-1500 mL (compensated/mild shock) Transfusion unlikely; type-compatible blood with crossmatch testing (45-60 min) Transient Recurrent hypotension (SBP <90), impaired mental status, weak radial pulse, tachycardia 26-40% or 1500-2000 mL (moderate shock) Likely: emergency packed red blood cell package, 2 units PRBCs, or emergency transfusion package, 4 units PRBCs / 6 units FFP / 6 units platelets, ABO-compatible No response Abnormal parameters or targets not achieved at any time >40% or >2000 mL (severe shock) Immediate: group-specific packed red blood cells without crossmatch (15 min), or O-/O+ if unavailable; O-/O+ FFP; O Rh-compatible platelets CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: ATLS · Plaat F (classification adapted to obstetrics) · WHO 2025. Intervention according to response: sustained improvement → no further intervention; partial improvement → fluid challenges; no improvement → blood products + surgery; no response → immediate surgical control. Do not administer predetermined 1-2 L fluid loads or use replacement formulas. IV isotonic crystalloid boluses of 500 mL at 39 °C; assess radial pulse and mental status. Isotonic crystalloids over colloids (WHO 2025, Rec. 28).

fichas.titulo: ICT — Stage 3: Treat/Transfer. Control bleeding by Tone (sequence 1-5)
fichas.texto: Continuous external uterine massage throughout management, until bleeding stops. Bimanual massage for ≥20 min or until bleeding stops if external massage is ineffective; additional uterotonics, Pinard safety balloon, and tranexamic acid. Continue bimanual compression until bleeding stops (no bleeding when compression is released and uterus is contracted). Abdominal aortic compression: closed fist (thumb out), pressing downward just above the umbilicus and slightly to the left. Immediate surgical intervention if uterine tone is not restored: B-Lynch compression suture or obstetric hysterectomy. Technique consistent with WHO, Managing Complications in Pregnancy and Childbirth, 2nd ed. 2017.

fichas.titulo: Oxytocin for atony (microdrip) and ergometrine as second-line treatment
fichas.texto: Oxytocin IM: 10 IU if no IV line is in place. Oxytocin IV: 5 IU slowly over 5 min; may be repeated after 5 min up to a maximum of 10 IU. IV maintenance: 20 IU in 500 cc of normal saline over 4 h (80 mIU/min = 42 drops/min = 126 cc/h by pump). Misoprostol 800 µg SL as a 3rd option if oxytocin or ergonovine is unavailable. Ergometrine / methylergonovine 0.2 mg: three evidence-based variants Variant Interval to 2nd dose Continuation Maximum WHO (2012 / MCPC 2017) — IM or slow IV 15 min 0.2 mg every 4 h 5 doses (1 mg) in 24 h FIGO 2022 / ACOG / FDA — IM or slow IV No intermediate dose 0.2 mg every 2-4 h 5 doses (1 mg) in 24 h Regional adaptation for Latin America (Colombia/Peru/Panama) — IM 20 min (one additional dose only) 0.2 mg every 4-6 h 5 ampoules in 24 h CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: WHO · FIGO 2022 · ACOG. Contraindicated in hypertension, preeclampsia/eclampsia, and heart disease. Indicated if oxytocin is unavailable or the response is insufficient after 30 min.

fichas.seccion: ICT Model and Resuscitation — Code Red ABCDE
fichas.texto: Antibiotic prophylaxis after correction (single dose, together with oxytocin to prevent recurrence): Ampicillin 2 g IV + metronidazole 500 mg IV, or Cefazolin 1 g IV + metronidazole 500 mg IV (penicillin allergy). Vascular ligation: bilateral uterine artery ligation (O'Leary) is the first-choice conservative surgical option (simpler, faster, immediate efficacy ~80-90%); internal iliac artery ligation is more complex (ureteral/venous risk, efficacy ~65-70%) and is reserved for failure of the former. Variants: Posadas technique (posterior selective devascularization of the uterine and internal tubal arteries, Series of 750 cases) and Tsirulnikov (triple ligation of the round ligaments, utero-ovarian and uterine arteries). Vaginal bridge: Zea technique (INPer — Zea technique). The hierarchy reflects technical ease and risk profile, not absolute superiority in efficacy (FIGO/WHO).

fichas.titulo: Primary xABCDE survey adapted for the pregnant patient
fichas.texto: Assess and treat in order; if the patient deteriorates, return to “x”. Tasks are carried out simultaneously by team members. xABCDE (ATLS 11th ed., 2025) with pregnancy-specific adjustments Step What to assess/do Adjustment in the pregnant patient x Exsanguinating hemorrhage Massive, compressible external bleeding: direct pressure, packing, tourniquet if involving an extremity (record the time) For obstetric bleeding: activate Code Red and follow the sequence for control by Tone (card 6) A Airway Patency; cervical spine protection if trauma occurred Consider earlier intubation: the pregnant patient desaturates faster. Higher risk of failed intubation: it should be performed by the most experienced operator B Breathing RR, SpO₂, symmetry, auscultation O₂ for SpO₂ 94-98 %. If a chest drain is placed, 1-2 spaces higher (3rd-4th intercostal space) because of diaphragm elevation C Circulation Pulse, BP, capillary refill, 2 large-bore IV lines, labs, bleeding control From 20 weeks: manual left uterine displacement (preferred in the unstable patient) or 15-30° left lateral tilt. The pregnant patient may show no signs until losing around 30% of blood volume; tachycardia with normal BP = early sign D Disability (neurologic deficit) Glasgow or AVPU, pupils, blood glucose Rule out a metabolic cause (blood glucose) before attributing the presentation to trauma E Exposure Undress and examine the entire body Prevent hypothermia: warmed fluids, warm environment, temperature >36.5 °C Acronym variants Variant Difference Source ABCDE Classic scheme, without an initial “x” ATLS through the 10th ed.; maternal collapse guidelines <C>ABCDE “C” for catastrophic hemorrhage before A Victorian State Trauma System; NICE NG39 xABCDE “x” for exsanguinating hemorrhage before A ATLS 11th ed. (ACS, 2025) XABCDE-F Adds “F”: fetal assessment after stabilizing the mother Obstetric emergency checklist (Heras). The “F” is supported by: fetal monitoring from 24 weeks, once the mother is stable; “the best treatment for the fetus is to resuscitate the mother well” (StatPearls; Victoria obstetric guideline) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: StatPearls — Trauma Assessment (xABCDE, ATLS 11th ed.) · ACS — ATLS 11 launch · Victorian State Trauma System — Obstetric Trauma Guideline v2.0, pp. 7-9 and 11 · Krywko DM et al. fichas.titulo: FAST / eFAST in pregnant and postpartum patients
fichas.texto: Views and findings Window Search Subxiphoid Pericardial effusion / tamponade Hepatorenal (Morrison) Free fluid. In preeclampsia/HELLP with epigastric or right upper quadrant pain: subcapsular hepatic hematoma (hypoechoic crescent beneath the capsule) Perisplenic Free fluid Suprapubic / pelvis Free fluid; uterus: fetal heartbeat, placenta, amniotic fluid Pulmonary (eFAST) Pneumothorax, pleural effusion. B-pattern (≥3 B-lines per field) = pulmonary edema Positive FAST in an unstable pregnant patient = significant finding. If stable, it can be performed during the secondary survey, ideally by a second operator. Performance for free fluid: sensitivity 61 % and specificity 94 % in pregnant patients (compared with 71 % and 97 % in nonpregnant patients). A negative FAST does not rule out bleeding. Ultrasound has low sensitivity for placental abruption: it cannot be used to rule it out. Severe preeclampsia: B-pattern was associated with elevated filling pressures. Restrict fluids (pilot study, n = 20). Subcapsular hematoma: bedside ultrasound in the unstable patient; CT if stable. fichas.seccion: Mode of Delivery — Robson, Bishop, Biometry
fichas.texto: Group Definition 1 Nulliparous, singleton, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, spontaneous labor 2 Nulliparous, singleton, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, induced labor (2a) or cesarean before labor (2b) 3 Multiparous with no previous cesarean, singleton, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, spontaneous labor 4 Multiparous with no previous cesarean, singleton, cephalic, ≥37 weeks, induced labor (4a) or cesarean before labor (4b) 5 At least one previous cesarean, singleton, cephalic, ≥37 weeks (5.1: one cesarean; 5.2: two or more) 6 All nulliparous women with a singleton breech fetus 7 All multiparous women with a singleton breech fetus (including previous cesarean) 8 All multiple pregnancies (including previous cesarean) 9 Singleton fetus in transverse or oblique lie (including previous cesarean) 10 Singleton cephalic fetus <37 weeks (including previous cesarean) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification: application manual (2018). It is classified using 6 variables: parity, prior cesarean delivery, onset of labor, number of fetuses, presentation/lie, and GA. Groups are mutually exclusive. Groups 1, 2 and 5 usually account for most cesarean deliveries and are the target of reduction strategies. Source: PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification: application manual (2018). The 6 variables Variable Options Note Parity Nulliparous · Multiparous Multiparous: at least one previous birth, vaginal or cesarean Previous cesarean No · 1 · 2 or more Defines subgroups 5.1 and 5.2 Onset of labor Spontaneous · Induced · Cesarean before labor As found at admission, regardless of what was planned. An emergency cesarean before labor starts counts as «before labor» Number of fetuses Singleton · Multiple Presentation / lie Cephalic · Breech · Transverse or oblique Gestational age Weeks Cut-off at 37+0 CaVeSal® proprietary table · Based on: PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification: application manual (2018). Classification at admission and real-time use It is applied to every woman admitted for birth, prospectively: each woman is assigned a group at admission and followed to the outcome (WHO — Robson Platform; WHO implementation manual). Real-time use is institutional: each birth is recorded as it happens to track the cesarean rate by group and plan actions (quality improvement experience). WHO provides a platform where hospitals upload these data (WHO Bulletin). Standard report by group: number of cesareans, number of women, group size, group cesarean rate, absolute and relative contribution to the overall rate (Robson report table). Robson does not assess whether a cesarean was appropriately indicated: that requires an audit of indications. In CaVeSal®: the Prenatal Calculator shows the probable group (prognosis); the Emergency calculator assigns the group at admission with intrapartum management (Labor tab).

fichas.seccion: Mode of Delivery — Robson, Bishop, Biometry
fichas.texto: Group Management Sources 1 Prolonged latent phase and slow but progressive labor are not indications for cesarean. Partograph according to the chosen model (Ministry CLAP from 4 cm, WHO 2020 from 5 cm, ACOG from 6 cm). Active-phase arrest: ≥6 cm with ruptured membranes and no change with ≥4 h of adequate contractions or ≥6 h of oxytocin with inadequate contractions. Second stage: ≥3 h of pushing before diagnosing arrest (longer with epidural, individualized). Continuous support. WHO — Labour Care Guide 2020 · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 2a / 4a Induce only with a clear indication; from 41+0 weeks induction is recommended. Bishop ≤6: cervical ripening (oral misoprostol 25 µg q2h or vaginal 25 µg q6h, balloon, or balloon + oxytocin). Do not diagnose failed induction in the latent phase before ≥24 h of induction and ≥12-18 h of oxytocin after membrane rupture. Never unsupervised; induce where an operating room is available. WHO — Induction of labour at or beyond term (2022) · WHO — Induction of labour (2011) · WHO — Mechanical methods (2022) · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 2b / 4b Verify and document the indication. Without a medical indication, do not schedule before 39 weeks. ACOG CO 765 (2019) · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 3 Same criteria as Group 1 with multiparous standards. Second stage: ≥2 h of pushing. Lowest cesarean rate group: a cesarean here deserves review of the indication. WHO — Labour Care Guide 2020 · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) 5.1 VBAC if: low transverse (or low vertical) incision, no previous rupture and no contraindication to vaginal birth. Contraindicated: classical cesarean, T or J incision, previous rupture. Only with 24-h emergency cesarean, blood bank and NICU. Continuous fetal monitoring and one-to-one care (abnormal FHR is the most common sign of rupture). Induction with mechanical methods; misoprostol contraindicated; oxytocin with caution. Epidural not contraindicated. Interval under 18 months: higher risk. EFW >4500 g: cesarean (FIGO). FIGO — VBAC (2025) · ACOG PB 205 (2019) · RCOG GTG 45 · WHO — Induction of labour (2011) 5.2 Two cesareans: FIGO generally does not recommend VBAC (only with a previous vaginal birth, senior obstetrician counseling and a high-complexity center); RCOG and ACOG allow it with counseling. Three or more: cesarean. With placenta previa or low anterior placenta, rule out accreta. FIGO — VBAC (2025) · ACOG PB 205 (2019) · RCOG GTG 45 6 Offer external cephalic version (ECV) from 36 weeks. Without ECV: planned cesarean from 39 weeks, or vaginal breech birth only with an institutional protocol, trained operator and written consent. In labor: ultrasound (type of breech, head flexion, EFW) and continuous monitoring; inadequate progress → cesarean. Imminent delivery: hands-off assistance. ACOG CO 745 (2018, reaf. 2023) · RCOG GTG 20b 7 Same as Group 6, with ECV from 37 weeks. With one previous low transverse cesarean, ECV may be attempted if she is a good VBAC candidate. ACOG CO 745 (2018, reaf. 2023) · RCOG GTG 20b · FIGO — VBAC (2025) 8 Uncomplicated dichorionic or monochorionic diamniotic twins, >32 weeks, first twin cephalic, no significant discordance: vaginal birth and cesarean are equally safe. First twin non-cephalic: cesarean. Monoamniotic: cesarean (32+0-33+6). Triplets: cesarean. One previous low transverse cesarean does not contraindicate VBAC. Active third stage due to higher hemorrhage risk. NICE NG137 (2019) · ACOG PB 231 (2021) · ACOG/SMFM — Safe prevention of the primary cesarean delivery (2014) · FIGO — VBAC (2025) 9 In labor or with ruptured membranes: cesarean (cord prolapse, uterine rupture). Before labor and without contraindications: ECV from 37 weeks. Ultrasound to rule out a mechanical cause (placenta previa, fibroids, anomalies). With back down, consider a vertical uterine incision. GLOWM · StatPearls — ECV 10 Lung maturation, neuroprotection, tocolysis and PROM according to the preterm labor and PROM cards in this guide. Notify neonatology. Prematurity alone does not determine the mode of birth; it is decided by obstetric conditions. ACOG CO 831 (2021) CaVeSal® proprietary algorithm · Based on: sources listed for each group · PAHO/WHO — Robson Classification (2018). Fetal lung maturation, magnesium sulfate neuroprotection, tocolysis and PROM follow the management already set in their cards in this guide and in the calculator. Does not replace clinical judgment.

fichas.titulo: Short maternal stature and cephalopelvic disproportion (CPD)
fichas.texto: Height <145-150 cm is not an indication for cesarean delivery (WHO 2018, FIGO, ACOG): it is a biomechanical risk factor; allow a trial of labor with a strict partograph and, if available, intrapartum ultrasound. MSPBS: height <145 cm → referral to orthopedics and genetics (possible skeletal dysplasia), not a criterion for mode of delivery. CPD is diagnosed intrapartum: adequate uterine activity (3-5/10 min, >2-4 h), dilation ≥5-6 cm, and lack of progress in dilation or descent. Signs: cervical edema, marked caput with overlapping sutures, persistent asynclitism. Once confirmed → cesarean delivery. Estimated fetal weight ≥4000 g + short stature → heightened alert for surveillance of CPD, not automatic cesarean delivery. Sources: WHO Intrapartum care 2018 · MSPBS Manual Nacional Prenatal · ACOG PB 216 · Williams Obstetrics 26.ª ed. (2022) · Caldwell-Moloy 1933 (tipos de pelvis).
